Chapter 1. Introduction
Thank you for your interest in Cimetrics’ BACstac software. The BACstac Software provides you with the ability
to create client and server application programs which use ASHRAE’s BACnet protocol for communication. Certain
versions of the BACstac Software also allow you to create gateway application programs that make a collection of
non-BACnet devices appear as a virtual BACnet network containing multiple BACnet devices.
The BACstac Software is available for Windows 7, Windows 8, Windows 8.1, Windows 10, Windows Server 2008,
Windows Server 2008 R2, Windows Server 2012, Windows Server 2012 R2, Linux 2.6.23 or later, and 32-bit embedded platforms.
This document describes the data types and API routines available in Cimetrics’ BACstac software. You will also
need to become familiar with the BACnet protocol. For a complete specification of the BACnet protocol, please refer
to American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers, Inc. ANSI/ASHRAE Standard 1352020 or later, “BACnet™ – A Data Communication Protocol for Building Automation and Control Networks,” and
the addenda to that standard.
For a description of how to install the BACstac software and how to construct applications using the BACstac software,
please refer to the BACstac Installation Guide and the BACstac User’s Guide for your target platform.
The BACstac Programmers’ Reference is divided into the following sections:
•
•
•
•
•
•

data types for BACnet services and properties of BACnet objects
general routines for BACstac applications
handling and generating raw requests
the BACstac object database
handling and generating requests with help from the BACstac object database
handling and generating ioctl requests.

1

Chapter 2. BACstac Data Types
The data types used by the BACstac API routines are defined in the header file BACTYPES.H. Access routines for
these data types are defined in the header file BACACC.H. These files are automatically included when the BACstac
application header files BACSRV.H, BACGTW.H or BACCLI.H are used.
The following sections contain descriptions of each data type, including how to declare a variable of the data type,
the access routines that can be used to manipulate the variable and a list of the BACstac API routines that accept
arguments of the data type. A comment containing either a ‘C’, ‘G’ or ‘S’ indicates whether the BACstac API routines
are available in client, gateway or server applications. The BACstac API routines are described in other sections of
this reference.
Most of the data types used by the BACstac API routines are representations of elements of the BACnet protocol. This reference documentation is intended to be complemented by study of the BACnet protocol as described in
ANSI/ASHRAE Standard 135-2020 or later.

Simple Data Types
Description:
The simple types are redefinitions of fundamental C data types, to allow for future portability of the BACstac API
routines. These types appear as arguments to the data access routines that manipulate the more complex data types.
The definition of BACSTAC_UI16 and BACSTAC_UI32 is platform specific. The implementation should not rely on
whether they are defined as ’unsigned short’ or ’unsigned int’ or ’unsigned long’.

Declarations:
typedef unsigned ... BACSTAC_UI8;
/* unsigned 8-bit integer */
typedef unsigned ... BACSTAC_UI16;
/* unsigned 16-bit integer */
typedef unsigned ... BACSTAC_UI32;
/* unsigned 32-bit integer */
typedef ...
BACSTAC_BOOLEAN; /* any integer suitable to hold 0 and 1 */
typedef BACSTAC_UI8
BACSTAC_BYTE; /* unsigned 8-bit value */
typedef signed int
BACSTAC_INT;
/* at least 16-bit unsigned value */
typedef unsigned int
BACSTAC_UINT; /* at least 16-bit unsigned value */
typedef signed long
BACSTAC_LONG; /* at least 32-bit signed value */
typedef unsigned long BACSTAC_ULONG; /* at least 32-bit unsigned value */

Address
Description:
The Address data type describes the network address of a BACnet Device, or specifies a BACnet network. An Address
is a destination for a BACnet message. The Address data type is used to send BACnet messages to a device or network
when the Device handle of an individual BACnet device is not known. An Address can contain such information as
2

Chapter 2. BACstac Data Types
the device MAC (Medium Access Control) address, its length in bytes, a remote flag, and a BACnet network number.
The device MAC address length also serves to indicate a broadcast on a local or remote network, while the BACnet
network number is used to indicate a broadcast on the global BACnet internetwork.

Declaration:
BACSTAC_ADDRESS address;

Initializers:
BACSTAC_ADDRESS0_INIT(netNumber)
BACSTAC_ADDRESS1_INIT(netNumber, mac0)
BACSTAC_ADDRESS2_INIT(netNumber, mac0, mac1)
BACSTAC_ADDRESS3_INIT(netNumber, mac0, mac1, mac2)
BACSTAC_ADDRESS4_INIT(netNumber, mac0, mac1, mac2, mac3)
BACSTAC_ADDRESS5_INIT(netNumber, mac0, mac1, mac2, mac3, mac4)
BACSTAC_ADDRESS6_INIT(netNumber, mac0, mac1, mac2, mac3, mac4, mac5)
BACSTAC_ADDRESS7_INIT(netNumber, mac0, mac1, mac2, mac3, mac4, mac5, mac6)

Address initializers with the specified network number and MAC. The length 0 means a broadcast.
BACSTAC_LBC_ADDRESS_INIT
BACSTAC_GBC_ADDRESS_INIT
BACSTAC_RBC_ADDRESS_INIT(netNumber)

Local, global, and remote broadcast address initializers.

Access Routines:
BACSTAC_BOOLEAN BACstacInitAddrLocal(
BACSTAC_ADDRESS *pAddress,
const BACSTAC_BYTE *pMac,
BACSTAC_SIZE_T macLength);

Initialise the Address of the local Device or local network.
BACSTAC_BOOLEAN BACstacInitAddrRemote(
BACSTAC_ADDRESS *pAddress,
const BACSTAC_BYTE *pMac,
BACSTAC_SIZE_T macLength,
BACSTAC_UI16 netNumber);

Initialise the Address of the remote Device or remote network.

3

Chapter 2. BACstac Data Types
BACSTAC_BOOLEAN BACstacInitAddrLocalBroadcast(
BACSTAC_ADDRESS *pAddress);

Initialise the Address so that BACnet messages sent using this Address will be broadcast on the local BACnet network.
BACSTAC_BOOLEAN BACstacInitAddrRemoteBroadcast(
BACSTAC_ADDRESS *pAddress,
BACSTAC_UI16 netNumber);

Initialise the Address so that BACnet messages sent using this Address will be broadcast on the remote BACnet
network.
BACSTAC_BOOLEAN BACstacInitAddrGlobalBroadcast(
BACSTAC_ADDRESS *pAddress);

Initialise the Address so that BACnet messages sent using this Address will be broadcast to all connected BACnet
networks.
BACSTAC_BOOLEAN BACstacIsAddrLocal(
const BACSTAC_ADDRESS *pAddress);

Check if the Address refers to a local Device or network.
BACSTAC_BOOLEAN BACstacIsAddrRemote(
const BACSTAC_ADDRESS *pAddress);

Check if the Address refers to a remote Device or network.
BACSTAC_BOOLEAN BACstacIsAddrGlobal(
const BACSTAC_ADDRESS *pAddress);

Check if the Address is set for global broadcast.
BACSTAC_BOOLEAN BACstacIsAddrBroadcast(
const BACSTAC_ADDRESS *pAddress);

Check if the Address is set for any type of broadcast.
BACSTAC_BOOLEAN BACstacSetAddrMAC(

4

Chapter 2. BACstac Data Types
BACSTAC_ADDRESS *pAddress,
BACSTAC_BYTE *pMac,
BACSTAC_SIZE_T macLength);

BACSTAC_BYTE *BACstacGetAddrMACPtr(
const BACSTAC_ADDRESS *pAddress);

A MAC address is a byte string identifying a particular BACnet device on a LAN. The MAC address is contained in a
buffer within the Address data type. An application can read or copy a MAC address once it has a pointer to the buffer.
The buffer is large enough to contain a MAC address of the maximum length of the supported network media. A MAC
address must be provided if the Address is not being used to generate a local or global broadcast. If the Address has
been set for local or remote broadcast, the MAC address will be set to an empty string.
BACSTAC_SIZE_T BACstacGetAddrMACLength(
const BACSTAC_ADDRESS *pAddress);

The actual length of the MAC address is determined by the type of physical network media used by the BACnet
network to which the Address refers. Example: lengths of the MAC address are 1 byte for ARCNET, 6 bytes for
Ethernet.
BACSTAC_BOOLEAN BACstacSetAddrNetworkNumber(
BACSTAC_ADDRESS *pAddress,
BACSTAC_UI16 netNumber);

BACSTAC_UI16 BACstacGetAddrNetworkNumber(
const BACSTAC_ADDRESS *pAddress);

An Address can refer to a device or broadcast on a specific remote BACnet network. If the Address refers to a remote
network, the BACnet network number for the remote network must also be provided. If the Address has been set for
global broadcast, the network number will have all bits set to 1.

APDU Properties
Description:
BACSTAC_APDU_PROPERTIES is a set of APDU parameters used by application to send and receive BACnet
requests. It contains the following parameters:

•

•

•
•
•
•

•
•

Max-APDU-Length is the maximum number of octets that may be contained in a single, indivisible application
layer protocol data unit. The value of this property shall be greater than or equal to 50. The maximum value of this
parameter is constrained by the underlying data link technology. A client request contains this value in the APDU
header rounded up to one of the values defined in section 20.1.2.4 of ANSI/ASHRAE Standard 135-2020 or later.
Segmentation-Supported indicates whether the device supports segmentation for transmission, reception, or both.
It can take one of four values: SEGMENTED_BOTH, SEGMENTED_TRANSMIT, SEGMENTED_RECEIVE,
NO_SEGMENTATION.
Max-Segments-Accepted indicates the maximum number of segments of an APDU that this device will accept. The
default value is 32.
Segment-Window-Size is the proposed size of a segmented message. The actual size window size is determine as
the minimum of the proposed window size of both communicated device. The default value is 16.
APDU-Segment-Timeout indicates the amount of time in milliseconds between retransmission of an APDU segment. The default value for this parameter is 5000 milliseconds.
APDU-Timeout indicates the amount of time in milliseconds between retransmissions of an APDU requiring acknowledgment for which no acknowledgment has been received. The default value for this parameter is 6000
milliseconds.
Number-Of-APDU-Retries indicates the maximum number of times that an APDU shall be retransmitted. The
default value is 3.
Max-Segments-to-Send indicates the maximum number of segments of an APDU that this device will send. If it is
set to 0, then it is considered to be the same as Max-Segments-Accepted. The default value is 0.

The APDU Properties data structure can be used either to set the default values for all requests or, if "raw" API is
used, to specify per-request APDU parameters, which may differ than the default values. For more information about
the default APDU properties, please refer to the Section called Default APDU Properties.

Declaration:
BACSTAC_APDU_PROPERTIES

pAPDUProps;

8

BACSTAC_APDU_PROP_TYPE enumeration is used to specify what numerical attribute should be get or set. It has

Default APDU Properties
Description:
The default APDU properties are used for all transactions that have not provided its own APDU parameters. The
"raw" API can provided its own APDU parameter for each transaction using the pAPDUParams parameter. The handle based API in client applications uses per device APDU properties, which are calculated based on the default
APDU properties and values of device properties read from the peer device. Getting and setting of the default APDU
parameters can be done by BACstacGetDefaultAPDUProperties and BACstacSetDefaultAPDUProperties. A client
application can get and set per device APDU properties using BACstacGetDeviceAPDUProperties and BACstacSetDeviceAPDUProperties.
The Max-APDU-Length, Max-Segments-Accepted, Segmentation-Supported, APDU-Segment-Timeout, APDUTimeout, and Number-Of-APDU-Retries APDU parameters have corresponding properties in the Device Object.
Setting any of these APDU properties does not change the corresponding values in the device object. The server
or gateway application is responsible to set the correct values of the properties in accordance with the current APDU
Properties, so other devices communicate with it can use the proper values. This be done automatically using BACstacSynchDeviceTSMParams. The gateway application should set them in for all devices it has created in the BACstac
database.
The default values for three commonly used APDU parameters: Max-APDU-Length, APDU-Timeout and NumberOf-APDU-Retries can be obtained and set directly without using BACSTAC_APDU_PROPERTIES data structure by
means of the following auxiliary routines.

Auxiliary Routines:
BACSTAC_BOOLEAN BACstacSetAPDURetry(BACSTAC_UINT nRetries);
BACSTAC_UINT BACstacGetAPDURetry(void);

These routines set/get the number of retries, which defines the maximum number of times that a confirmed APDU
shall be retransmitted if no acknowledgment has been received. The default value for the current library version is 3
retries.
BACSTAC_BOOLEAN BACstacSetAPDUTimeout(BACSTAC_UINT nMillisec);
BACSTAC_UINT BACstacGetAPDUTimeout(void);

These routines set/get the APDU timeout, which represents the amount of time in milliseconds between retransmissions of an APDU requiring acknowledgment for which no acknowledgment has been received. The default value for
the current library version is 6 seconds.
BACSTAC_BOOLEAN BACstacSetMaxAPDULength(BACSTAC_UINT nBytes);
BACSTAC_UINT BACstacGetMaxAPDULength(void);

11

Chapter 2. BACstac Data Types
These routines set/get the maximum number of octets in an APDU, which represents a single indivisible application
layer protocol data unit. The default values depends on the underlying data link technology. For instance, it is 1476
for Ethernet and BACnet/IP data links.

Client Initialization Data
Description:
This data structure is used to pass initialization parameters into the client application initialization routine, BACstacClientInit().

Declaration:
BACSTAC_CLI_INIT clientInitData;

The fields of the data structure are:
BACSTAC_UI8

BACstacVersionMajor;

13

Chapter 2. BACstac Data Types
BACSTAC_UI8
BACSTAC_UI16
BACSTAC_DEVICE_COUNT
BACSTAC_OBJECT_COUNT
BACSTAC_UINT

BACstacVersionMinor;
wPortID;
maxDevices;
maxObjects;
flags;

The first two fields should have the values 7 and 10 (data type BACSTAC_UI8) for the current library version. If the
version numbers supplied by an application aren’t compatible with the version of the BACstac library to which the
application was linked, the initialization routine will generate a run-time error.
The wPortID field is the identifier of the Network Port to which the application should be bound. If this parameter is
zero then the first physical port is used.
MaxDevices and maxObjects fields are used to allocate space for tracking remote BACnet objects, and indicate the
maximum number of devices and objects per device to be tracked. maxObjects must be greater than or equal to 1, since
all images of Devices must contain an image of the Device Object. maxDevices and maxObjects may be set to CLI_DEF_MAX_DEVICES and CLI_DEF_MAX_OBJECTS, respectively. These constants are used as default values for
maxDevices and maxObjects and are both equal to 32 for the current library version. However, the application can set
them to higher values.
The flags field specifies additional flags used in initialization. Currently, the following flags are supported:
• BACSTAC_IF_USE_CHAR_STRING is used to indicate that if the decoded BACnet type is Character String then

it should be decoded as the BACSTAC_CHAR_STRING data type. If this flag is not set then different BACstac
data types used for different character sets. For example, an array of BACSTAC_CHAR is used Character Set 0
(UTF-8), and BACSTAC_DBCS_STRING for Character Set 1 (DBCS). Starting with BACstac 7.0, this flag is set
automatically by BACstacInitCliInit.

Database Property Template
Description:
A list of database property templates is used to specify a list of properties and their initial values in a newly created
object. Each property template describes one property in the object and consists of three attributes:

Property-identifier is used to identify the property in the object, and it must be unique. Flags are used to modify the
default actions associated with this property. Property contents specify the initial value of the property. For "auto"
properties, the property contents must be empty.
• Property-contents provides the initial value of the property. For "auto" properties, the initial value should be empty.
• Property-flags define behavior of the property. The flags consist of two groups: regular flags and those that define
internal type of the property.
•

Regular flags only slightly alter the default action for this property without changing how this property is stored inside.
These flags can altered later after creating the object. There are the following regular flags:
•
•
•
•
•

BACSTAC_WRITABLE_FLAG makes this property from the network. This does not require to modify this property
from inside BACstac application using BACstacStorePropertyInstance() or another function.
BACSTAC_READ_CB_FLAG makes the database read procedure to invoke the read callback for this property
BACSTAC_WRITE_CB_FLAG makes the database read procedure to invoke the write callback for this property
BACSTAC_CHANGE_LIST_CB_FLAG makes the database read procedure to invoke the change-list callback for
this property
BACSTAC_SUBSCRIBABLE_FLAG allows another device to this property. This flag may be only used if the default
action for SubscribeCOV is enabled. (See note below.)

The other group of flags defines the internal representation of the property as well as how its value is maintained by
the BACstac database. Currently, there are only two such flags:
BACSTAC_REG_PROP means a regular property, which is stored in the BACstac database in the ASN.1 format,
and whose value can be modified using BACstacStorePropertyInstance.
• BACSTAC_AUTO_PROP means a property whose value is determined based on values. For instance, a value of the
object-list property is determined by the list of objects stored in this device. So, the object-list property must be
"auto". Some other properties such as can be either "regular" or "auto" depending on whether the application wants
to maintain their values or rely on the default action.
•

Note: Setting the "auto" mode for the active-cov-subscriptions property enables the default action for SubscribeCOV and SubscribeCOVProperty services.

Declaration:
BACSTAC_DB_PROPERTY dbProperty;

/*G,S*/

Database Type Information
Description:
The database type information contain type information about custom (proprietary) properties and objects that will be
stored in the BACstac database. It also allows to modify allocated space for standard properties that do not have the
explicit size limit (such as lists). Modification of data types of standard properties is not allowed.

Device
Description:
The Device data type is an abstraction of a BACnet Device for use within a BACstac application. A BACstac application can refer to a Device by obtaining a Device handle. BACstac applications do not manipulate Devices directly,
since the data structures describing Devices are maintained inside the BACstac API routines.
A server application can obtain a Device handle referring to the local Device. A client application can obtain Device
handles referring to a table of local images of remote Devices. A gateway application can obtain Device handles
referring to all of the local Devices. Each Device has a list of the Objects that it contains. Each Device must contain a
Device Object which represents information about the Device which is publicly available to the BACnet network.
A Device can be identified by a Device Object instance number which must be unique within an installation’s BACnet
internetwork. A Device can also be identified by an Address.

Declaration:
BACSTAC_HDEVICE hDevice;
BACSTAC_DEVICE_COUNT nDevices;

Access Routines:
None.

Device ID Resolver Operation
Description:
The Device ID Resolver operation represents an asynchronous operation to resolve some Device instance number.
The operation contains the asynchronous completion routine to be invoked at completion of the operation as well as
some internal data used by the Device ID resolver.

Declaration:
BACSTAC_RESOLVE_OPER resolveOper;

/*C,G,S*/

BACSTAC_RESOLVE_ACR acr);

The access routine initializes a Device ID Resolver Operation and sets the given asynchronous completion routine,
which is invoked when the operation is completed. Any Resolver Operation must be initialized before it can be started.
When it is started, it must not be modified by the application.

Virtual Device Parameters
Description:
This data structure contains parameters to create a virtual device in a gateway application.

Declaration:
BACSTAC_DEVICE_PARAMS

virtualDevice;

The BACSTAC_DEVICE_PARAMS fields are:
const void
const BACSTAC_ADDRESS
BACSTAC_INST_NUMBER
BACSTAC_OBJECT_COUNT
BACSTAC_ELEMENT_COUNT

*deviceTemplate;
address;
instNumber;
maxObjects;
maxCovSubs;

The deviceTemplate field is a pointer to the Device template data structure created by the CBNOBJ.EXE compiler
from a .TPI file description of the objects in the BACnet Server application.
The address field specifies the BACnet address of the device.
The instNumber field is the Instance Number of the Device Object. It must be unique within the connected BACnet
internetwork. The Instance Number provided here overrides the Instance Number compiled into the BACstac data
structures (i.e. created from a .TPI file).
The maxObjects field indicates the maximum number of objects that the virtual Device can have.
The maxCovSubs field is the maximum number of COV Subscriptions that this device can support when the default
action for COV subscriptions is enabled.

Error
Description:
The Error data type is used to represent the BACnet Error, Abort, and Reject responses to service requests. The Error
data type is a C union that contains either a BACSTAC_ABORT_REASON, a BACSTAC_REJECT_REASON or a
BACSTAC_ERROR_TYPE. The choice is indicated by the BACSTAC_FAILURE_TYPE tag which may be either
FAILURE_ABORT or FAILURE_REJECT or FAILURE_ERROR.
BACSTAC_ERROR_TYPE, which shall present in the case Failure_type equal to FAILURE_ERROR only, is a structure containing a BACSTAC_ERROR_CLASS and BACSTAC_ERROR_CODE pair.
Clause 18 of ANSI/ASHRAE Standard 135-2020 or later describes the meaning of these enumerations.
The Error data type is returned by API routines that generate BACnet service requests.

22

Chapter 2. BACstac Data Types
The interpretation of the union is indicated by the BACSTAC_STATUS return code of those routines ( BACSTAC_STATUS_BACNET_ERROR, BACSTAC_STATUS_BACNET_ABORT, or BACSTAC_STATUS_BACNET_REJECT). See also
APPENDIX E — RETURN VALUES.

Gateway Initialization Data
Description:
This data structure is used to pass initialization parameters into the gateway application initialization routine, BACstacGatewayInit().

Declaration:
BACSTAC_GTW_INIT

gatewayInitData;

The BACSTAC_GTW_INIT fields are:
BACSTAC_UI8
BACstacVersionMajor
BACSTAC_UI8
BACstacVersionMinor
BACSTAC_UI16
wPortID
BACSTAC_DEVICE_COUNT
maxDevices
const BACSTAC_DB_TYPE_INFO *devTypeInfo
const BACSTAC_BIT_STRING
*servicesSupported
const BACSTAC_DEVICE_PARAMS *gatewayDevice
BACSTAC_UINT
flags

The first two fields should have the values 7 and 10 (data type BACSTAC_UI8) for the current library version. If the
version numbers supplied by an application are not compatible with the version of the BACstac library to which the
application was linked, the initialization routine will generate a run-time error.

26

Chapter 2. BACstac Data Types
The wPortID field is the identifier of the Network Port to which the application should be bound. Gateway applications
can attach only to a port that represents a virtual network as described in Annex H.2. There can be multiple virtual
ports, so the application must specify which port it wants to use.
The maxDevices field indicates the maximum number of devices that the Gateway can maintain. If the default value
of maxDevices is appropriate, maxDevices can be set to GTW_DEF_MAX_DEVICES value which equals 32 for the
current version. This constant is used as a default value for maxDevices attribute. However, the application can set
maxDevice to a higher value.
The devTypeInfo field specifies additional data type information.
The servicesSupported field can indicate what services are supported by this application.
The flags field specifies additional flags used in initialization. Currently, the following flags are supported:
• BACSTAC_IF_USE_CHAR_STRING is used to indicate that if the decoded BACnet type is Character String then

it should be decoded as the BACSTAC_CHAR_STRING data type. If this flag is not set then different BACstac
data types used for different character sets. For example, an array of BACSTAC_CHAR is used Character Set 0
(UTF-8), and BACSTAC_DBCS_STRING for Character Set 1 (DBCS). Starting with BACstac 7.0, this flag is set
automatically by BACstacInitGtwInit.
• BACSTAC_IF_RPM_TO_RP_HOOK is used to indicate that if the Read-Property hook is installed then the BACstac
default action should convert any Read-Property-Multiple request to Read-Property requests to itself. Note that all
generated Read-Property requests have the source address same as the destination of the RPM request.
• BACSTAC_IF_WPM_TO_WP_HOOK is used to indicate that If the Write-Property hook is installed then the BACstac
default action should convert any Write-Property-Multiple request to Write-Property requests to itself. Note that
all generated Write-Property requests have the source address same as the destination of the WPM request. IMPORTANT: This flag is incompatible with the Value-Source mechanism, so if the BACstac database contains the
Value_Source property this flag should not be set.

Object
Description:
The Object data type is an abstraction of BACnet Objects for use within a BACstac application. A BACstac application
can refer to an Object by obtaining an Object handle. BACstac applications do not manipulate Objects directly, since
the data structures describing Objects are maintained inside the BACstac API routines. Please refer to the Section
called Object Identifier in Chapter 4.
A server or gateway application can obtain Object handles referring to Objects in the local Devices. A client application can obtain Object handles referring to a table of images of Objects for remote Devices.
An Object can be identified within a Device by a unique combination of Object type and Object instance number.
This unique combination is known as the Object Identifier and is described in the Section called Object Identifier in
Chapter 4.
An Object contains a collection of Properties, whose values can be read and modified across the BACnet network,
as well as by the server application maintaining the Object. In BACstac applications, a Property is identified by its
Property Identifier and the handle of its Object. Object handles thus appear as arguments in all API routines that
manipulate either Properties or Objects.

Object Type Information
Description:
The object type information contain type information about custom (proprietary) properties for the given object type.
It can be used to describe a new property object type or add proprietary properties to a standard object type. In
additional, it is possible to use this information to change some aspect of standard properties (such as space allocated
for them in the database), but property type information should be compatible with the standard one. Please refer to
the Section called Property Type Information for more details.
A description of any proprietary object must contain at least three following properties: object-identifier, object-name,
object-type; and those properties must have the correct data type as it is prescribed by the BACnet standard.
If an object contains priority-array and relinquish default properties, those properties may be specified only after
specifying present-value. The relinquish-default property must have the same type as present-value and this type
should be compatible with priority-array, i.e. it can be either Real, Unsigned, Enumeration.

Declaration:
BACSTAC_OBJECT_TYPE_INFO objTypeInfo;

/*G,S*/

Initializer:
BACSTAC_OBJECT_TYPE_INFO_INIT(objType, propCount, propTypeInfo)

Chapter 2. BACstac Data Types

Property
Description:
The Property data type describes local and remote BACnet Properties. A Property is a part of an Object which can
be queried and modified across the BACnet network. To refer to a Property, an application needs both a Property
Identifier and an Object handle. An additional data type, Property Contents, is used to manipulate the value contained
in a Property.
In a server application a Property of a local Object has an attribute, Access Mode (data type BACSTAC_ACCESS),
which takes one of the values, Read-Only or Read-Write. This allows a server application to control remote access
to a Property. In a server application, there are callback procedures which may be invoked when the server processes
requests for the BACnet Services Read Property and Write Property.

Property Contents
Description:
The Property Contents data structure can be used to store the value of a local or remote property. Each property
contents has BACSTAC_DATA_TYPE (which describes the type of the stored value), the number of elements (which
allows to store arrays), and a buffer (which contains a reference to memory where the actual value is stored and the
buffer size).
A Property Contents structure can be initialized to a variable, an array, or a buffer sufficient size. The buffer is used
for reading elements of unknown type or when the desired type has a complex structure. If you write a code that
may be used on non-Intel platform, the buffer should be suitably aligned for the desired data type. Alternatively, the
application can provide an allocator to a BACstac routines, then the BACstac routines will allocate the buffer required
size, attach it to the Property Contents, and decode the result in it.
IMPORTANT: A Property Contents structure should be properly initialized before calling any read operation without
allocator (i.e. when the iAlloc parameter is given the NULL value). If the allocator is provided then there is no need
to initialize the Property Contents, but after any successful reading operation, BACstacFreeContents() should be used
to free the Property Contents that is no longer needed.

Declaration:
BACSTAC_PROPERTY_CONTENTS contents;

Initializers:
BACSTAC_CONTENTS_INIT(dataType, ptr, bufSize, nElements)

BACSTAC_CONTENTS_INIT is a property contents initializer, which initializes the property contents to refer to a
variable, array, or memory buffer pointed by the ptr parameter. The dataType parameter is BACstac data type that
corresponds to the C object type of the variable or array element referred by the property contents. See Appendix D
for supported BACstac data types and corresponding them C object types. bufSize specifies the total size of memory
in bytes that is used or can be used to store data. nElements specifies the number of elements in an array or it must
be 1 if the contents is initialized to refer to a variable.
BACSTAC_CONTENTS_INIT_TO_VAR(dataType, var)

BACSTAC_CONTENTS_INIT_TO_VAR is a property contents initializer, which initializes the property contents to
refer to the given variable. The var parameter is an expression of one of C data type specified in Appendix D, which
designates a variable that will be referred by the property contents, and the dataType parameter is the corresponding

32

Chapter 2. BACstac Data Types
BACSTAC_DATA_TYPE value. The C data type is required to be complete, i.e. its size can be determined using the
sizeof operator.
Note: Because this initializer relies on the sizeof operator, it works for strings variables declared as an array of
chars (i.e. using BACSTAC_CHAR[]) or as a string literal, but produces the wrong result for strings described as
a pointer to BACSTAC_CHAR (i.e. using BACSTAC_CHAR*). If you want to initialize a property contents using a
pointer to BACSTAC_CHAR then BACSTAC_CONTENTS_INIT should be used instead. See examples below.

Note: Usually C compilers do not evaluate the operand of a sizeof operator, but if your compiler does then the var
expression must be a constant expression. Also, some old compilers may not support non-constant expressions
in initializers.

BACSTAC_CONTENTS_INIT_TO_ARRAY(dataType, array)

BACSTAC_CONTENTS_INIT_TO_ARRAY is a property contents initializer, which initializes the property contents
to refer to the given array. The array parameter should be an expression that designates an object of a complete array
data type and each element of the array has any scalar C data type specified in Appendix D. The dataType parameter
is the corresponding BACSTAC_DATA_TYPE value that describes the type of an array element.
Note: This initializer determines the buffer size and number of elements using the sizeof operator, so it works
only with arrays whose type is complete (i.e. its size is known) and where each element has a fixed size (i.e.
not an array itself). If you have a pointer to some array or want to initialize an array of strings then BACSTAC_CONTENTS_INIT should be used instead.

Note: Usually C compilers do not evaluate the operand of a sizeof operator, but if your compiler does then
the array expression must be a constant expression. Also, some old compilers may not support non-constant
expressions in initializers.

BACSTAC_EMPTY_ARRAY_CONTENTS_INIT(dataType)

BACSTAC_EMPTY_ARRAY_CONTENTS_INIT initializes a property contents to represent an empty array of the
given type.
BACSTAC_EMPTY_CONTENTS_INIT

BACSTAC_EMPTY_CONTENTS_INIT initializes a property contents to be empty with the data type set to DATA_TYPE_INVALID, so the property contents will not confused with a valid empty array.
BACSTAC_NULL_CONTENTS_INIT

BACSTAC_NULL_CONTENTS_INIT initializes a property contents to represent ASN NULL value.
BACSTAC_CONTENTS_INIT_TO_BUF(buffer, size)

BACSTAC_CONTENTS_INIT_TO_BUF is a property contents initializer, which initializes the property contents to
the given buffer of the specified size.
Examples of initializer use:
33

Chapter 2. BACstac Data Types
// BACSTAC_CONTENTS_INIT
const BACSTAC_CHAR *str = "My String";
BACSTAC_PROPERTY_CONTENTS pc1 = BACSTAC_CONTENTS_INIT(
DATA_TYPE_UTF_8_STRING, str, strlen(str)+1, 1);
BACSTAC_CHAR multistr[] = "String 1\0String 2\0String 3\0String 4";
BACSTAC_PROPERTY_CONTENTS pc2 = BACSTAC_CONTENTS_INIT(
DATA_TYPE_UTF_8_STRING, multistr, sizeof(multistr), 4);
BACSTAC_UNSIGNED *pMyArray;
BACSTAC_ARRAY_SIZE nElementsInMyArray;
BACSTAC_VALUE_SIZE sizeOfMyArray;
BACSTAC_PROPERTY_CONTENTS pc2 = BACSTAC_CONTENTS_INIT(
DATA_TYPE_UNSIGNED, pMyArray, sizeOfMyArray, nElementsInMyArray);
// BACSTAC_CONTENTS_INIT_TO_VAR
const BACSTAC_CHAR str[] = "My String";
BACSTAC_UNSIGNED value = 5;
BACSTAC_PROPERTY_CONTENTS pc1 = BACSTAC_CONTENTS_INIT_TO_VAR(
DATA_TYPE_UTF_8_STRING, str);
BACSTAC_PROPERTY_CONTENTS pc2 = BACSTAC_CONTENTS_INIT_TO_VAR(
DATA_TYPE_UTF_8_STRING, "My String");
BACSTAC_PROPERTY_CONTENTS pc3 = BACSTAC_CONTENTS_INIT_TO_VAR(
DATA_TYPE_UNSIGNED, value);
// BACSTAC_CONTENTS_INIT_TO_ARRAY
BACSTAC_UNSIGNED array[] = {1, 2, 3};
BACSTAC_PROPERTY_CONTENTS pc = BACSTAC_CONTENTS_INIT_TO_ARRAY(
DATA_TYPE_UNSIGNED, array);

The number of bytes directly used by the value stored in the property contents buffer without taking into account

are stored in the same buffer.
For all data types except character strings (which may use a variable length for each element) the returned value
is sizeof the corresponding data type multiplied by the number of elements stored in the property contents. For a
variable-length data types, the returned value is the sum of sizes of each element stored in the property contents.

Chapter 2. BACstac Data Types

Property Type Information
Description:
Property type information describes type information of a single property stored in the BACstac database. Each combination of an object type and property-identifier may have its own property type descriptor. If an application provides
type information for an (object-id, property-id) pair that is already known to the BACstac database then the new information should be compatible. Property information is considered as compatible if it has the same BACstac data type
and the same property type (scalar, list, or array). In the case of a fixed size array (FSA), the array size should have
the same number of elements.
Note: Property type information is used not only to store proprietary properties in the database, but it also influences on the decoder when the application reads some property for its own or another device.

Each property can be one of four types: scalar, list, fixed size array, and variable size array. The following four flags
are used to describe the property type:

• BACSTAC_PF_SCALAR - scalar
• BACSTAC_PF_LIST - list
• BACSTAC_PF_FS_ARRAY - fixed size array
• BACSTAC_PF_VS_ARRAY - variable size array

In addition, the following property flags can be used:
• BACSTAC_PF_OPTIONAL - optional property (used by RPM service)
• BACSTAC_PF_W_OOS - writable when out of service is true

Each property type information contains the arraySize parameter. If the property is not an array then this parameter
must be zero, otherwise it must some positive number. For variable size arrays, this parameter specifies the maximum
number of elements in the array. For the fixed size array, this parameter specifies the exact number of elements in the
array.
The hintSize parameter should be usually zero, but non-zero parameter may be used to increase or decrease the
space allocated by the BACstac database to store this property. This parameter is treated as a hint, so its value may be
ignored in some cases.
There are a few property-identifiers that cannot be added to an object for different reasons. PROP_ALL, PROP_REQUIRED, PROP_OPTIONAL have special meaning in the standard and cannot be used to specify any property
in any object. PROP_ACTIVE_COV_SUBSCRIPTIONS, PROP_OBJECT_LIST are meant to be used only inside of
the device object, so they are not allowed in other objects.
Some property-identifier can be added but they must they same type as they have in the standard objects. Specifically,
priority-array must be always a fixed-size array of 16 elements, which has the DATA_TYPE_PRI_ARRAY_ITEM
data type. The following properties must be scalar of the specified type:
•

status-flags - DATA_TYPE_BIT_STRING (assumed to be BACnetStatusFlags)

37

Chapter 2. BACstac Data Types
•
•
•
•
•
•
•
•
•
•

event-state - DATA_TYPE_ENUM (assumed to be BACnetEventState)
out-of-service - DATA_TYPE_BOOLEAN
reliability - DATA_TYPE_ENUM (assumed to be BACnetReliability)
notify-type - DATA_TYPE_ENUM (assumed BACnetNotifyType)
cov-period - DATA_TYPE_UNSIGNED
vendor-identifier - DATA_TYPE_UNSIGNED (assumed Unsigned16)
acked-transitions - DATA_TYPE_BIT_STRING (assumed BACnetEventTransitionBits)
object-property-reference - DATA_TYPE_DEV_OBJ_PROP_REFERENCE
max-APDU-length-supported - DATA_TYPE_UNSIGNED
segmentation-supported - DATA_TYPE_ENUM (assumed BACnetSegmentation)

Cov-increment property must be scalar of a type like present-value property. Exclude signed present-value property,
in this case cov-increment property must be scalar of an unsigned type. The allowed maximum for COV_Increment
of the unsigned type is 8388607, so it can be stored in BACSTAC_REAL without losing any precision. In the case
of the Real data type, its value should not exceed exceed the maximum that can be stored in the Real data type
(3.4028234e38).
In addition, there are a few restrictions on the BACstac data type that can be used in the property type information. DATA_TYPE_NEW_STANDARD, DATA_TYPE_PROPRIETARY, DATA_TYPE_EXTENDED, DATA_TYPE_INVALID, and DATA_TYPE_ANY_PRIMITIVE cannot be used in the description of any property. DATA_TYPE_PRI_ARRAY_ITEM may be used only for priority-array.
The order of properties in the description of customer objects is not important except that cov-increment, priorityarray, and relinquish-default properties must be described after the present-value property. The size of priority-array
item and relinquish-default must be 0 or same as the size of present-value. If the size of a commandable present-value
changed (in any standard property) then priority-array and relinquish-default should be redefined too to have the same
size.
Note: Adding new properties from the standard reserved range to standard objects may lead to incompatibility
with the future versions of BACstac.

BACSTAC_PROPERTY_TYPE_INFO propTypeInfo;

Server Initialization Data
Description:
This data structure is used to pass initialization parameters into the Server application initialization routine, BACstacServerInit().

Declaration:
BACSTAC_SRV_INIT

serverInitData;

The attributes contained in a Server Initialization Data are:
BACSTAC_UI8
BACstacVersionMajor;
BACSTAC_UI8
BACstacVersionMinor;
BACSTAC_UI16
wPortID;
const void
*localDevice;
BACSTAC_INST_NUMBER
instNumber;
BACSTAC_OBJECT_COUNT
maxObjects;
const BACSTAC_DB_TYPE_INFO *devTypeInfo;
const BACSTAC_BIT_STRING
*servicesSupported;
BACSTAC_UINT
flags;
BACSTAC_ELEMENT_COUNT
maxCovSubs;

The first two fields should have values 7 and 10 for the current library version. If the version number supplied by
an application isn’t compatible with the version of the BACstac library to which the application was linked, the
initialization routine will generate a run-time error.
The wPortID field is the identifier of the Network Port to which the application should be bound. If this parameter is
zero then the first physical port is used.
The localDevice field is a pointer to the Device template data structure created by the CBNOBJ.EXE compiler from
a .TPI file description of the objects in the BACnet Server application. This data structure is used to create a local
Device.
The instNumber field is the Instance Number of the Device Object. It must be unique within the connected BACnet
internetwork. The Instance Number provided here overrides the Instance Number compiled into the BACstac data
structures (i.e. created from a .TPI file).
The maxObject field indicates the maximum number of objects that the local Device can maintain. SRV_DEF_MAX_OBJECTS can be used as default value and equals 32 for the current version. However the application can set
maxObjects to a higher value.
The devTypeInfo field specifies additional data type information.
The servicesSupported field can indicate what services are supported by this application.
The flags field specifies additional flags used in initialization. Currently, the following flags are supported:
• BACSTAC_IF_USE_CHAR_STRING is used to indicate that if the decoded BACnet type is Character String then

it should be decoded as the BACSTAC_CHAR_STRING data type. If this flag is not set then different BACstac
data types used for different character sets. For example, an array of BACSTAC_CHAR is used Character Set 0
(UTF-8), and BACSTAC_DBCS_STRING for Character Set 1 (DBCS). Starting with BACstac 7.0, this flag is set
automatically by BACstacInitSrvInit.
39

Chapter 2. BACstac Data Types
• BACSTAC_IF_RPM_TO_RP_HOOK is used to indicate that if the Read-Property hook is installed then the BACstac

default action should convert any Read-Property-Multiple request to Read-Property requests to itself. Note that all
generated Read-Property requests have the source address same as the destination of the RPM request.
• BACSTAC_IF_WPM_TO_WP_HOOK is used to indicate that If the Write-Property hook is installed then the BACstac
default action should convert any Write-Property-Multiple request to Write-Property requests to itself. Note that
all generated Write-Property requests have the source address same as the destination of the WPM request. IMPORTANT: This flag is incompatible with the Value-Source mechanism, so if the BACstac database contains the
Value_Source property this flag should not be set.

The maxCovSubs field is the maximum number of COV Subscriptions that this device can support when the default
action for COV subscriptions is enabled.

Deprecated access routines
Access routines that perform shallow copy of a data type are redundant, because they can be replaced with a simple
assignment:
*destArg = *srcArg;

where srcArg and destArg are the source and destination argument of the access routine correspondingly. Therefore,
the follow the following access routines previously defined in this chapter are deprecated in BACstac 7.0:
BACstacCopyAddr
BACstacCopyErrorType
BACstacCopyError
BACstacCloneContents

Chapter 3. Service Data Types
The data types that can appear as parameters of Services are defined in the header file BACTYPES.H. Access routines
for these data types are defined in the header file BACACC.H. These files are automatically included when the BACstac
application header files BACSRV.H, BACGTW.H or BACCLI.H are used. These last three files also define Service data
types and access routines for these data types.
The following sections contain descriptions of each data type, including how to declare a variable of the data type,
and the access routines that can be used to manipulate the variable.

Acknowledge Alarm
Description:
The Acknowledge Alarm Info data type conveys the parameters of an Acknowledge Alarm service request.

Declaration:
BACSTAC_ACK_ALARM_INFO pAckAlarm;

This data structure consists of the following attributes:
BACSTAC_UI32
processID;
BACSTAC_OBJECT_ID
eventObjectID;
BACSTAC_EVENT_STATE eventState;
BACSTAC_TIME_STAMP timeStamp;
BACSTAC_STRING_TYPE type;
BACSTAC_CHAR_STRING ackSource;
BACSTAC_TIME_STAMP ackTime;

A processID attribute specifies the Process Identifier of the Event Notification to which the acknowledgment is a
response.
An eventObjectID attribute is the identifier of the event-initiating object of the event notification to which this acknowledgment is a response.
An eventState attribute must be equal to the value of the "To State" attribute of the Conditional Parameter argument
of the Event Notification request that is being acknowledged.
The timeStamp attribute conveys the same Time-Stamp value that was received from the Event Notification request
that is being acknowledged. Time-Stamp is an attribute of Notification-Mandatory-Parameter data structure.
The ackSource attribute, of type CharacterString, specify the identity of the operator or process that is acknowledging
the event notification.

Audit Log Query
Description:
The Audit Log Query Info data type conveys the parameters of an AuditLogQuery service request.

Declaration:
BACSTAC_AUDIT_LOG_QUERY_INFO pAuditLogQuery;

This data structure consists of the following attributes:
BACSTAC_OBJECT_ID
BACSTAC_AUDIT_LOG_QUERY_PARAM
BACSTAC_UI64
BACSTAC_UI16

auditLog;
parameters;
startAtSeqNumber; /* | BACSTAC_INVALID_SEQ_NUM */
requestedCount;

The auditLog attribute, of type BACSTAC_OBJECT_ID, specifies the Audit Log object to query.
The parameters attribute, of type BACSTAC_AUDIT_LOG_QUERY_PARAM, specifies the query parameters to
apply.
The startAtSeqNumber attribute, of type BACSTAC_UI64, is an optional parameter that identifies, by sequence
number, where in the log to start the query. BACSTAC_INVALID_SEQ_NUM is used to indicate its absent.
The requestedCount attribute, of type BACSTAC_UI16, is used to limit the number of records that will be returned.

Audit Log Query Parameters
Description:
This data type specifies the query parameters to apply by Audit Log Query request.

Declaration:
BACSTAC_AUDIT_LOG_QUERY_PARAM

parameters;

The BACSTAC_AUDIT_LOG_QUERY_PARAM data structure contains the Audit Query By Target Query Parameters, or the Audit Query By Source Query Parameters.
The Audit Query By Target Query Parameters data structure consists attributes:
BACSTAC_UINT
BACSTAC_OBJECT_ID
BACSTAC_ADDRESS
BACSTAC_OBJECT_ID
BACSTAC_PROPERTY_ID
BACSTAC_ARRAY_INDEX
BACSTAC_PRIORITY_LEVEL
BACSTAC_BIT_STRING
BACSTAC_SUCCESS_FILTER

mask;
deviceID;
address;
objectID;
propertyID;
index;
priority;
operations;
resultFilter;

/* | VOID */
/* | VOID */

The mask attribute indicates a set of active parameters. A hexadecimal numeric value indicates the activity or inactivity
of each optional parameters. If any filter is inactive, this numeric value is zero. The mask attribute may be composed
by a logical "OR" operation from the values that correspond to each of optional parameters.
#define BACSTAC_ALQP_ADDRESS
#define BACSTAC_ALQP_OBJECT_ID
#define BACSTAC_ALQP_PROPERTY_ID

0x01
0x02
0x04

48

Chapter 3. Service Data Types
#define BACSTAC_ALQP_OPERATIONS

0x08

The ’deviceID’, ’address’, ’objectID’, ’propertyID’, ’index’ identify the device, object, or property for which audit
records are requested.
The ’priority’ parameter is used to restrict records to only those for the specified priority. Audit records without a
’priority’ will match any ’priority’.
The ’operations’ parameter determines the operation types for which entries are requested. If not present, all operation
types will be returned.
The ’resultFilter’ parameter indicates whether audit records for successful and/or failed actions will be included in the
response.
The Audit Query By Source Query Parameters data structure consists attributes:
BACSTAC_UINT
BACSTAC_OBJECT_ID
BACSTAC_ADDRESS
BACSTAC_OBJECT_ID
BACSTAC_BIT_STRING
BACSTAC_SUCCESS_FILTER

mask;
deviceID;
address;
objectID;
operations;
resultFilter;

The mask attribute indicates a set of active parameters. A hexadecimal numeric value indicates the activity or inactivity
of each optional parameters. If any filter is inactive, this numeric value is zero. The mask attribute may be composed
by a logical "OR" operation from the values that correspond to each of optional parameters.
#define BACSTAC_ALQP_ADDRESS
#define BACSTAC_ALQP_OBJECT_ID
#define BACSTAC_ALQP_OPERATIONS

0x01
0x02
0x08

The ’deviceID’ and ’objectID’ identify the operation source for which audit records are requested.
The ’operations’ parameter determines the operation types for which entries are requested. If not present, all operation
types will be returned.
The ’resultFilter’ parameter indicates whether audit records for successful and/or failed actions will be included in the
response.

Audit Log Query Result
Description:
The Audit Log Query Result data type conveys the result of an AuditLogQuery service request.

Declaration:
BACSTAC_AUDIT_LOG_QUERY_RESULT

result;

The Audit Log Query Result data type has the following attributes:
BACSTAC_OBJECT_ID
auditLog;
BACSTAC_BUFFER
records;
BACSTAC_ELEMENT_COUNT count;
BACSTAC_BOOLEAN
noMoreItems;

The auditLog attribute, of type BACSTAC_OBJECT_ID, specifies the Audit Log object the query was performed
on.
The records attribute, of type BACSTAC_BUFFER, specifies the buffer for returned records. The returned audit log
records, of type BACSTAC_AUDIT_LOG_RECORD_RESULT, are placed in the buffer. Use access routines to get
these records.
The count attribute, of type BACSTAC_ELEMENT_COUNT, specifies number of the returned records.
The noMoreItems attribute, of type BACSTAC_BOOLEAN, specifies whether the query processed to the end of the
Audit Log and found no more records (TRUE), or not (FALSE). When FALSE, there may, or may not, be more items
in the log which match the query.

COV Notification
Description:
Change Of Value (COV) Notification Info data type conveys the information for confirmed and unconfirmed COV
notification service hooks and Ex-routines to process the confirmed or unconfirmed COV notifications that have no
default processing in the current BACstac version.

Declaration:
BACSTAC_COV_NOTIF_INFO

pCOVNotif;

The attributes contained in a COV Notification Info data are:
BACSTAC_UI32
processID;
BACSTAC_OBJECT_ID
initDeviceID;
BACSTAC_OBJECT_ID
monitoredObjectID;
BACSTAC_UNSIGNED
timeRemaining;
BACSTAC_PROPERTY_VALUE
*listOfValues;
BACSTAC_PROPERTY_COUNT
nValueCount;
#define BACSTAC_INFINITE_LIFETIME
((BACSTAC_UNSIGNED) 0)

The processID attribute is the numeric identifier of the Process within the COV client which is to process the COV
notifications. A value of zero is reserved for unsubscribed COV for unconfirmed case only.
The initDeviceID and monitoredDeviceID attributes are the identifier of the Device object of the initiating device and
the identifier of the notification-initiating object within an initiating device.
The timeRemaining attribute indicates the remaining lifetime of the subscription, in seconds. The value of zero indicates an indefinite lifetime or, for unconfirmed service, an unsubscribed notification.
The two last attributes are the pointer to a buffer to convey a list of property values, and a size of the buffer expressed
as the number of property value data structures which this buffer contains. The contents of the list of property values
depends on the type of object being monitored. See Section 13, Table 13-1 of ANSI/ASHRAE Standard 135-2020 or

55

Chapter 3. Service Data Types
later for a summary of standard objects and property values that can be returned in the listOfValues attribute of COV
reporting.

Declaration:

The attributes contained in a COV Notification Multiple Info data are:
BACSTAC_UI32
processID;
BACSTAC_OBJECT_ID
initDeviceID;
BACSTAC_UNSIGNED
timeRemaining;
BACSTAC_BOOLEAN
fTimestampPresent;
BACSTAC_DATE_TIME
timestamp; /* optional */
BACSTAC_COV_NOTIF_ITEM *listOfCOVNotifications; /*= size:count */
BACSTAC_ELEMENT_COUNT count;

The processID attribute, of type BACSTAC_UNSIGNED, shall convey a numeric "handle" meaningful to the subscriber. This handle shall be used to identify the process within the COV client that should receive the notification.
The initDeviceID attribute, of type BACSTAC_OBJECT_ID, shall convey the Device Object_Identifier of the device
that initiated the ConfirmedCOVNotificationMultiple service request.
The timeRemaining attribute, of type BACSTAC_UNSIGNED, shall convey the remaining lifetime of the COVmultiple subscription, in seconds.
The optional timestamp attribute, of type BACSTAC_DATE_TIME, shall convey the date and time of the last change
conveyed in the notification. This parameter shall be present if, and only if, any of the COV notifications conveyed in
the ’List of COV Notifications’ parameter contain the ’Time of Change’ parameter.
The listOfCOVNotifications attribute, shall be a list of one or more ’COV Notifications’, of type BACSTAC_COV_NOTIF_ITEM (see below), each of which corresponds directly to a specific property of the object identified and
whose value has changed, resulting in the COV notification to be issued.
The BACSTAC_COV_NOTIF_ITEM data structure contains attributes:
The monitoredObjectID attribute, of type BACSTAC_OBJECT_ID, shall convey the Object_Identifier of an object
with one or more properties subscribed via SubscribeCOVPropertyMultiple and whose values have changed.

57

Chapter 3. Service Data Types
The listOfValues attribute shall convey a list of one or more property values that have changed, possibly conveyed
as timestamped data. This attribute may include multiple entries for the same property if the ’Timestamped’ flag is
TRUE in the respective COV subscription specification and multiple changes of that property have been queued up
since the last notification. Each item of type BACSTAC_COV_NOTIF_PROP_VALUE
The BACSTAC_COV_NOTIF_PROP_VALUE data structure contains attributes:
The propID attribute, of type BACSTAC_PROPERTY_ID, shall convey the property identifier of the property.
The index attribute, of type BACSTAC_ARRAY_INDEX, shall convey that array index.
The value attribute, of type BACSTAC_PROPERTY_CONTENTS, shall convey the new value of the property
The optional attribute, of type BACSTAC_TIME, shall be present if, and only if, the SubscribeCOVPropertyMultiple
request was made with its ’Timestamped’ parameter set to BACSTAC_TRUE in the COV subscription specification
for the property and shall convey the local time when the data value changed.

Create Object
Description:
BACSTAC_OBJECT_SPECIFIER data type is the helper data type which describes two ways of identifying an
instance of Object to create. Object may be identified either by Object-Type or by Object-Identifier. This data
type contains a BACSTAC_CREATE_OBJECT_TYPE tag field which may be either CREATE_OBJECT_TYPE or
CREATE_OBJECT_ID and a value of either Object-ID or Object-Type.
Create-Object-Info data structure of data type BACSTAC_CREATE_OBJECT_INFO conveys the information for the
Create-Object application hook and Create-Object raw request. This data type contains the objectSpecifier field of
the BACSTAC_OBJECT_SPECIFIER data type (see above) and a number of fields which describe a list of Property
Values to initialize the properties of a newly created object. These fields are: BACSTAC_BOOLEAN attribute which
indicates does a list of Property Values present or not (if its value is FALSE then two next attributes shall be ignored);

60

Chapter 3. Service Data Types
a pointer to a memory block to place the list of Property Values (This attribute may be NULL. In this case a number
of Property Values must be zero.); a number of PROPERTY_VALUE data structures in the list of Property Values.

Get Alarm Summary
Description:
This data type represents one item of the Alarm Summary list in the Get Alarm Summary service.

Declaration:
BACSTAC_ALARM_SUMMARY pAlarmSummary;

The Alarm Summary data structure consists of three attributes:
BACSTAC_OBJECT_ID
objectID;
BACSTAC_EVENT_STATE alarmState;
BACSTAC_BIT_STRING ackedTransitions;

The objectID attribute shall identify the event-initiating object whose Event State property is not equal to STATE_NORMAL, and whose Notify Type property value is equal to NOTIFY_TYPE_ALARM.
The alarmState attribute indicates the value of the Event-State property of the event-initiating object.
The ackedTransitions attribute indicates the value of the Acked-Transitions property of the object. For the possible
values of this attribute, see Appendix D, Event Transition Bits.

Get Enrollment Summary
Description:
This is the service data type which appears in the Get Enrollment Summary service in order to convey the summary
information. This data type structure represents one item of the Enrollment Summary list.

The fNotClassPresent attribute’s value indicates whether the last attribute, which is optional, is to be present
(BACSTAC_TRUE) or not (BACSTAC_FALSE). In the latter case the notificationClass attribute may have any value.
The other attributes convey the event-initiating object information: the Object Identifier of the object, the Event Type
that the object can generate, the initiating-object’s Event State property value, the Priority of notifications generated
by the object and the Notification Class of notifications generated by the initiating-object. The last attribute is optional,
but it must be present if fNotClassPresent attribute value is TRUE.

Get Enrollment Summary - Enrollment Filter
Description:
This data type indicates a set of filters that may be applied to define the search criteria for the event-initiating objects
to be summarized in the Get Enrollment Summary service. Seven filters may be defined by this data structure. The 1st
filter always has to present. One of its possible values means "ALL", as if the filter is absent. The other six filters are
optional. The mask attribute of the Enrollment Filter data type indicates a set of active filters.

Declaration:
BACSTAC_ENROLLMENT_FILTER

pEnrlFilter;

The Enrollment Filter data structure consists of eight attributes:
BACSTAC_UINT
BACSTAC_ACK_FILTER
BACSTAC_RECIPIENT_PROCESS
BACSTAC_STATE_FILTER
BACSTAC_EVENT_TYPE
BACSTAC_UI8
BACSTAC_UI8
BACSTAC_UNSIGNED

mask;
acknowledgment;
enrollment;
eventState;
eventType;
minPriority;
maxPriority;
notificationClass;

68

Chapter 3. Service Data Types
The mask attribute indicates a set of active filters. A hexadecimal numeric value indicates the activity or inactivity
of each optional filter. If any filter is inactive, this numeric value is zero. The mask attribute may be composed by a
logical "OR" operation from the values that correspond to each of optional filters.
#define BACSTAC_EF_ENROLLMENT
#define BACSTAC_EF_EVENT_STATE
#define BACSTAC_EF_EVENT_TYPE
#define BACSTAC_EF_PRIORITY
#define BACSTAC_EF_NOTIF_CLASS

0x01
0x02
0x04
0x08
0x10

The acknowledgment attribute is the Acknowledgment Filter which establishes a search criteria for event-initiating
objects by their Acked Transitions property value: ACK_FILTER_ALL - all event-initiating objects, ACK_FILTER_ACKED - all Event Transition Bits are 1, ACK_FILTER_NOT_ACKED - at least one zero among Event Transition
Bits. This filter is always active.
The enrollment attribute of the Enrollment Filter data type is a data structure which contains two fields: Recipient
and Process Identifier. A number of access routines serve this data structure. Objects shall be summarized by the
Get Enrollment Summary service only if either the Event Enrollment object contains the indicated Process Identifier
and BACnetRecipient, or the event-initiating object references a Notification Class object which contains one or
more BACnetDestination properties containing the indicated Process Identifier and Recipient attributes. This filter is
optional. To make it active the minor bit of the mask attribute has to be 1.
The eventState attribute indicates the value of the Event State filter. This attribute may have one of the following
values:
STATE_FILTER_OFFNORMAL,
STATE_FILTER_FAULT,
STATE_FILTER_NORMAL,
STATE_FILTER_ALL,
STATE_FILTER_ACTIVE.

Only those event-initiating objects whose Event State property matches the value specified by this filter parameter
will be included in the set to be summarized. This filter is optional. To make it active the second bit from the left of
the mask attribute has to be 1.
All the other filters (Event Type, minPriority, maxPriority and Notification Type) restrict the summary to those objects
that can generate event notifications with each of the corresponding parameters matched to the value of this attribute.
All these filters are optional. To make any filter active the corresponding bit of the mask attribute has to be 1. The
same bit, the fourth from the left, serves minPriority and maxPriority filters, so these filters can be either both active
or both inactive.

Get Event Information
Description:
This section describes data types used by the Get-Event-Information routine family.
The BACSTAC_EVENT_INFO_INFO data structure conveys request information. It contains an optional ObjectID
parameter. The COV_EVENT_INFO_LAST_RCV_PRESENT flag indicates the presence of an Object Identifier in
this data structure.
The BACSTAC_EVENT_INFO data structure contains response information, which consists of a list of Event Summary items, an actual number of terms on the list, and the total length of the summary buffer expressed as a number
of items. The More Events flag indicates whether (BACSTAC_TRUE) or not (BACSTAC_FALSE) more objects exist
that meet the active event state criteria of this service request, but that couldn’t be returned in the reply.
Each item in the summary list is of data type BACSTAC_EVENT_SUMMARY. It consists of a number of parameters that describe the appropriate object: ObjectID, Event-State, Acked-Transitions, Notify-Type, and Event-Enable
parameters, conveying values of the corresponding object properties. The Event-Stamps parameter shall convey the
timestamps of the last event notifications for TO-OFFNORMAL, TO-FAULT, and TO-NORMAL events. The EventPriorities parameter conveys the priority specified in the Priority property of the associated notification class object.

Global Group UCOV Notification
Description:
The Global Group Unconfirmed Change-Of-Value Notification data type conveys the information to send a series of Unconfirmed COV Notification requests as it is prescribed by the BACnet standard for Present_Value in a
Global_Group object.

Declaration:
BACSTAC_GLOBAL_GROUP_UCOV_NOTIF

pGlobalGroupUCOVNotif;

The attributes contained in a Global Group UCOV Notification data are:
BACSTAC_UI32
processID;
BACSTAC_OBJECT_ID
initDeviceID;
BACSTAC_OBJECT_ID
monitoredObjectID;
BACSTAC_UNSIGNED
timeRemaining;
BACSTAC_BIT_STRING
membStatusFlags;
BACSTAC_ELEMENT_COUNT
valueCount;
BACSTAC_PROP_ACCESS_RESULT *values;
#define BACSTAC_INFINITE_LIFETIME
((BACSTAC_UNSIGNED) 0)

75

Chapter 3. Service Data Types
The processID attribute is the numeric identifier of the Process within the COV client which is to process the COV
notifications. In the current BACnet standard, this notification is always unsubscribed, therefore this parameter should
be zero.
The initDeviceID is an object identifier of the device that initiates the notification.
The monitoredDeviceID attribute is object identifier of the monitored object whose values are reported in the notification. The object type must be Global_Group.
The timeRemaining attribute indicates the remaining lifetime of the subscription, in seconds. In the current BACnet
standard, this notification is always unsubscribed, therefore this parameter should be zero.
The membStatusFlags attribute is the value of the Member_Status_Flags property of the monitored object.
The valueCount attribute is the size of the array pointed by the value attribute.
The values attribute points to values of the Present_Value property of the monitored object.

Global Group UCOV Result
Description:
The Global Group UCOV Result data type conveys information about BACstacGlobalGroupUCOVNotifEx() execution.

Declaration:
BACSTAC_GLOBAL_GROUP_UCOV_RESULT

pGlobalGroupUCOVResult;

The attributes contained in a Global Group UCOV Notification data are:
BACSTAC_ELEMENT_COUNT requestCount;
BACSTAC_ELEMENT_COUNT failureCount;
BACSTAC_ELEMENT_COUNT valueTooLongCount;
BACSTAC_ELEMENT_COUNT firstValueTooLong;

The BACSTAC_GLOBAL_GROUP_UCOV_RESULT data type contains information about how an Unconfirmed
COV Notification for the Global Group object was sent. It includes the following attributes:
The requestCount attribute contains the total number of Unconfirmed COV Notification requests.
The failureCount attribute contains the number of requests that could not be sent for some reason.
The valueTooLongCount attribute contains the number of value items that were too long to be sent and were replaced
with the corresponding BACnet error.
The firstValueTooLong attribute contains the one-based index of the first item that has a too long value to be sent, or
0 if no value was too long.

RequestingSource;
eRequest;
objectID;

The pRequestingSource attribute specifies the identity of the human operator that initiates this service request. A string
type for the requesting source is indicated by the characterSet attribute. The eRequest attribute specifies the requested
operation (which may take on one of the standard values: NONE, SILENCE, SILENCE_AUDIBLE, SILENCE_VISUAL, RESET, RESET_ALARM, RESET_FAULT). The Object ID attribute is optional — if it is omitted the
request is interpreted as an operation on the all applicable objects within the receiving device. The mask attribute
indicates if the object ID is present.

Private Transfer
Description:
BACSTAC_PRIVATE_TRANSFER_INFO data structure contains numeric Vendor-Identifier and Service-Number
parameters to specify the unique vendor identification code for the type of vendor-proprietary service to be performed
and the desired service to be performed. It contains a BACSTAC_BOOLEAN If-Parameters-Present attribute, a pointer
to the buffer which contains desired service parameters in the case fParametersPresent is TRUE (otherwise the buffer

contents shall be ignored), and a numeric length of the buffer which shall be ignored if fParametersPresent attribute is
FALSE. The Size attribute indicates the size of the data in bytes for the input buffer; for an output buffer it means a
size of the buffer in bytes. A Size attribute shall be 0 if a pointer to the Parameters buffer is NULL.

Read File
Description:
The Read File data types convey the information for routines generating and handling the Atomic Read File service.
The Read File Info data (data type BACSTAC_READ_FILE_INFO) conveys the information for a Read File application hook. This data type contains three fields: and object identifier of the File object, the Access Type of data type
BACSTAC_FILE_ACCESS_TYPE which may be either FILE_ACCESS_STREAM or FILE_ACCESS_RECORD,
and a Read File Range field of data type BACSTAC_READ_FILE_RANGE.
The Read File Range data (data type BACSTAC_READ_FILE_RANGE) indicates the start position from the beginning of the file and the number of requested octets or records. The start position of 0 is the first octet or record of the
file.
The Read File Result data (data type BACSTAC_READ_FILE_RESULT) conveys the result of reading. This data
type contains a boolean End Of File parameter which indicates does the response include the last octet of the file,
Access Type field, and a number of fields which describe the memory block containing the file contents. In the Stream
case there are a Start Position field and an Octet String field. In the Record case there are a Start Record Number field,
a Record Count field that indicates a number of records to read, and a Buffer field. The buffer is formatted as an array
of BACSTAC_OCTET_STRING values which represent the records. The Start position and start record counts begin
from zero. If the Octet String field or Buffer field is not big enough to hold the actual result, a BACSTAC_STATUS_OUT_OF_SPACE reply will be returned. Access routines should be used to obtain pointers to those octet strings.
The Read File Spec data (data type BACSTAC_READ_FILE_SPEC) contains two fields: File Access Type (Stream
or Record) and Read File Range.

Read Property Conditional
Description:
The data type BACSTAC_READ_CON_INFO is used to transmit data for Read-Property-Conditional service request
and hook. This data type contains a Selection Criteria attribute and a list of Property References, i.e. a pointer to a
buffer which contains a list of Property Reference data structures, and the buffer length expressed as a number of
Property References. A buffer length may be zero.
Note: If the number of Property References is zero and the pointer to them is NULL then listOfPropertyReferences
is omitted in ASN.1 encoding. If the number of Property References is zero and the pointer to them is not NULL
then listOfPropertyReferences is encoded in ASN.1 as an empty list.

The Selection-Criteria data structure (data type BACSTAC_SELECTION_CRITERIA) consists of Selection-Logic
value (data type BACSTAC_SELECTION_LOGIC) which may be And, Or or All (the last means that no logical expression is used), and a list of Selection-Criterion data structures (data type BACSTAC_SELECTION_CRITERION)
which is represented by a pointer to the buffer and a buffer length expressed as a number of Selection-Criterion items.
A buffer length may be zero. The Selection-Criterion data structure contains a Property-Identifier, an optional ArrayIndex (if a property is not array, a Void index shall be used), a Relation-Type which may be Equal, Not Equal, Less
Than and so on (see Appendix D, Relation-Type enumeration), and a Property-Contents value to compare with the
object Properties. A single Selection-Criterion requests a comparison of the value of the Object-Property and the provided Property-Contents. The Selection-Criteria data type constructs a boolean expression which is a combination of
these comparisons.
Note: If the number of Selection-Criteria is zero and the pointer to them is NULL then listOfSelectionCriteria is
omitted in ASN.1 encoding. If the number of Selection-Criteria is zero and the pointer to them is not NULL then
listOfSelectionCriteria is encoded in ASN.1 as an empty list.

If a Read-Property-Conditional service request succeeds, the RPC-Result data structure (data type BACSTAC_RPC_RESULT) returns the result. This data structure consists of a pointer to a buffer to transmit a list of Read-Access-Result
data structures (Read-Access-Result data type is described in the Section called Read Property Multiple) and a buffer
length expressed as a number of Read-Access-Result items.

Read Property Multiple
Description:
The Read Multiple Hook Info data (data type BACSTAC_READ_MUL_HOOK_INFO) conveys the information for a
Read Property Multiple application hook. This data type contains the list of object identifiers and property references
of the properties to be read.
The Read Access Result data (data type BACSTAC_READ_ACCESS_RESULT) conveys the result of reading all the
properties which belong to a single object. The former data type name BACSTAC_HOOK_RESULT_LIST also may
be used. The result of reading any single property may be either the property value or the reason for failure. The list
of Read Access Result data structures is the argument of the BACstacReadPropMultipleResponse() routine which is

96

Chapter 3. Service Data Types
a completion routine for the Read Property Multiple application hook. Read-Property-Conditional service also uses
this data type.

Declaration:
BACSTAC_READ_MUL_HOOK_INFO
BACSTAC_READ_ACCESS_SPEC
BACSTAC_READ_ACCESS_RESULT

readMultipleInfo;
readAccSpec;
readAccessResult;

The BACSTAC_READ_MUL_HOOK_INFO data structure contains a pointer to a list of readSpec (data type
BACSTAC_READ_ACCESS_SPEC) as the 2nd attribute, and the length of the list as the 1st attribute. BACSTAC_READ_ACCESS_SPEC data structure indicates a list of properties which belong to a single object. The former data
type name BACSTAC_READ_ACCESS_SPEC also may be used. This data structure contains three attributes: the
Object Identifier, the length of the buffer as a number of Property References it contains, and a pointer to the buffer
which contains the list of Property References.
The BACSTAC_READ_ACCESS_SPEC data type corresponds to the BACSTAC_READ_LIST data type which is
used in the BACstacReadPropertyMultiple2() routine.
The BACSTAC_READ_ACCESS_RESULT data structure consists of three attributes: the 1st attribute is the Object
Identifier, the 2nd attribute is the number of items in the next buffer, and the 3rd attribute is the pointer to the buffer
containing the list of BACSTAC_READ_RESULT_ITEM data structures. The BACSTAC_READ_RESULT_ITEM
data type and the helper data type BACSTAC_RPM_RESULT_COUNT are described in the Section called Read
Property Multiple - Client.
Note: If the number of items is zero and the pointer to items is NULL then listOfReadAccessResults is omitted in
ASN.1 encoding. If the number of items is zero and the pointer to items is not NULL then listOfReadAccessResults
is encoded in ASN.1 as an empty list.

Read Property Multiple - Client
Description:
The Read Property Multiple data types BACSTAC_READ_LIST and BACSTAC_READ_RESULT_LIST correspond
to BACnet Read Access Specifications and Read Access Results parameters in a Read Property Multiple confirmed
service request. The READ_RESULT_ITEM data type is an attribute of the BACSTAC_READ_RESULT_LIST data
type. In the ReadPropertyMultipleEx() routine, the BACSTAC_READ_RAW_RESULT_LIST data type is used. This
data structure differs from BACSTAC_READ_RESULT_LIST in the first attribute only: it uses an Object ID instead
of an Object Handle.

Declaration:
BACSTAC_READ_RESULT_ITEM
Item;
BACSTAC_BOOLEAN
status;
BACSTAC_READ_RESULT_LIST
ResultList;
BACSTAC_READ_LIST
List;
BACSTAC_READ_RAW_RESULT_LIST readAccessResult

The BACSTAC_READ_LIST data type contains an Object handle field, a pointer to a buffer in which to place a
Property Reference list, and a size of the buffer expressed as a number of Property References. It represents a list of
Properties to be read in the given Object. The Read Property Multiple service uses a number of BACSTAC_READ_RESULT_LIST data type parameters to provide a list of objects, and each object has its own list of properties to be
read.
The list of elements of this data type structure is the second argument of the BACstacReadPropertyMultiple2() routine
in the Client API.
The result of every single property reading may be either success (copying the value of a Property), or failure and
information about the reason for failure. The READ_RESULT_ITEM data structure, which provides this information, consists of the Property information (Property Identifier and Array index if the property is an array, void if not)
and either Property Contents (if the reading was successful), or Error type in the case of failure, and a BACSTAC_BOOLEAN tag to choose. An error as the result of reading a single Property does not mean a failure of the BACstacReadPropertyMultiple2(), but only a failure to access that property.
The BACSTAC_READ_RESULT_LIST data type contains the result of reading all the properties which belong to a
single Object. This data type contains an Object Handle field, a pointer to a buffer in which to place a list of Read
Result Items, the size of the buffer expressed as a number of Read Result Items, and the actual number of Read Result
Items which the Read Property Multiple service will convey.

101

Chapter 3. Service Data Types
The BACSTAC_READ_RAW_RESULT_LIST data type contains the Object ID as the first attribute. All other attributes are the same as in the BACSTAC_READ_RESULT_LIST data type.
