Read Range
Description:
The Read-Range data types convey information for the Read Range service API routines. The Read Range service
permits reading a specific range of data items from properties that are either lists or arrays of lists. The service was
modified in Addendum 135-2001b, which is included in ASHRAE Standard 135-2004 (BACnet revision 3). BACstac
7.6 or later does not support deprecated range choices anymore.
The requested data items are specified by optional ’Range’ parameter, which can be one of supported range types.
The BACSTAC_RANGE_TYPE enumeration is used to specify the range type or BACSTAC_RANGE_NONE if
the ’Range’ parameter is omitted. For devices that support BACnet revision 3 or later, there are three possible
range types: ’By Position’ (BACSTAC_RANGE_BY_POSITION), ’By Sequence Number’ (BACSTAC_RANGE_BY_SEQUENCE_NUM), and ’By Time’ (BACSTAC_RANGE_BY_TIME2).
If the range type is by ’By Position’ then the data items to be read are specified by the given ’Reference Index’ and
’Count’ parameters. The absolute value of the ’Count’ parameter specifies the number of records to be read. If ’Count’
is positive, the record specified by ’Reference Index’ shall be the first record read and returned; if ’Count’ is negative
the record specified by ’Reference Index’ shall be the last record. ’Count’ may not be zero.
If the range type is by ’By Sequence Number’ then the data items to be read are specified by the given ’Reference
Sequence Number’ and ’Count’ parameters. The absolute value of the ’Count’ parameter specifies the number of
records to be read. If ’Count’ is positive, the record specified by ’Reference Sequence Number’ shall be the first
record read and returned; if ’Count’ is negative the record specified by ’Reference Sequence Number’ shall be the last
record. ’Count’ may not be zero.
If the range type is by ’By Time’ then the data items to be read are specified by the given ’Reference Time’ and
’Count’ parameters. The absolute value of the ’Count’ parameter specifies the number of records to be read. If ’Count’
is positive, the record specified by ’Reference Sequence Number’ shall be the first record read and returned; if ’Count’
is negative the record specified by ’Reference Sequence Number’ shall be the last record. ’Count’ may not be zero.
First Sequence Number’ is only included if the ’Range’ parameter of the request was of the type ’By Sequence Number’ or ’By Time’ and ’Item Count’ is greater than 0. BACSTAC_INVALID_SEQ_NUM is used to denote absence of
the Sequence Number.

106

Chapter 3. Service Data Types
Addendum 135-2016bi introduced extremely large logs, which use the Read Range service with 64-bit values of ’Reference Index’ and ’Sequence Number’. To preserve backward compatibility, the BACstac API provides both 32-bit
and 64-bit variants of Read Range API. If BACSTAC_USE_64_BIT_READ_RANGE is defined then BACstac Read
Range API uses 64-bit unsigned integers as ’Reference Index’ (BACSTAC_REF_INDEX) and ’Sequence Number’
(BACSTAC_SEQ_NUM); otherwise BACstac Read Range API uses 32-bit unsigned integers as as ’Reference Index’
(BACSTAC_REF_INDEX) and ’Sequence Number’ (BACSTAC_SEQ_NUM).
The BACSTAC_READ_RANGE_RANGE data structure can contain any supported range. Depending on whether
BACSTAC_USE_64_BIT_READ_RANGE is defined, it can be either an alias to BACSTAC_READ_RANGE_64_RANGE or BACSTAC_READ_RANGE_32_RANGE. The following declaration provides a generic description
of this data structure.

Declaration:
/* By Position */
BACSTAC_REF_INDEX nRefIndex;
BACSTAC_INTEGER
nCount;
/* By Time */
BACSTAC_DATE_TIME
refTime;
BACSTAC_INTEGER
nCount;
/* By Sequence Number */
BACSTAC_SEQ_NUM
nRefSequenceNum;
BACSTAC_INTEGER
nCount;

The BACSTAC_READ_RANGE_SPEC data structure specifies the range or absence of the range. The ’tag’ field specifies the range type that the ’range’ field contains. Depending on whether BACSTAC_USE_64_BIT_READ_RANGE
is defined, it can be either an alias to BACSTAC_READ_RANGE_64_SPEC or BACSTAC_READ_RANGE_32_SPEC. The following declaration provides a generic description of this data structure.

Declaration:
BACSTAC_RANGE_TYPE
BACSTAC_READ_RANGE_RANGE

tag;
range;

The BACSTAC_READ_RANGE_INFO data structure contains the property reference (object and property identifiers
and array index, which may be VOID) and the range to read. Depending on whether BACSTAC_USE_64_BIT_READ_RANGE is defined, it can be either an alias to BACSTAC_READ_RANGE_64_INFO or BACSTAC_READ_RANGE_32_INFO.

Declaration:
BACSTAC_OBJECT_ID
BACSTAC_PROPERTY_ID
BACSTAC_ARRAY_INDEX
BACSTAC_RANGE_TYPE
BACSTAC_READ_RANGE_RANGE

objectID;
ePropertyID;
nIndex;
tag;
range;

The BACSTAC_READ_RANGE_RAW_RESULT data structure is used to convey a result of reading. It contains the
property reference (object and property identifiers and array index), the Result-Flag attribute, a Property Contents
107

Chapter 3. Service Data Types
buffer into which to copy the values and the sequence number of the first returned item. Depending on whether
BACSTAC_USE_64_BIT_READ_RANGE is defined, it can be either an alias to BACSTAC_READ_RANGE_64_RAW_RESULT or BACSTAC_READ_RANGE_32_RAW_RESULT.
The Result-Flag attribute (data type BACSTAC_BIT_STRING) consists of several flag bits that describe characteristics of the response data: BACSTAC_FIRST_ITEM, BACSTAC_LAST_ITEM, BACSTAC_MORE_ITEMS. The
BACSTAC_FIRST_ITEM, flag indicates whether this response includes the first list or array element (in the case of
positional indexing), or the oldest timestamped item (in the case of time indexing). The BACSTAC_LAST_ITEM,
flag indicates whether this response includes the last list or array element (in the case of positional indexing), or the
newest timestamped item (in the case of time indexing). The BACSTAC_MORE_ITEMS flag indicates whether more
items matched the request but were not transmittable within the reply.

Reinitialize Device
Description:
Reinitialize Device Info is a data structure (data type BACSTAC_REINIT_DEV_INFO) that is used by the BACstacReinitializeDeviceEx() routine and the Reinitialize-Device service hook (hook type BACSTAC_REINIT_DEV_HOOK_PROC). This data type contains two attributes: Reinit Type, and the password character string. The password
can be up to 20 characters. This data type replaces the BACSTAC_REINIT_DEV_HOOK_INFO data type which,
however, may still be used. Reinit Type may have one of the next values:
REINIT_COLDSTART;
REINIT_WARMSTART;
REINIT_STARTBACKUP;
REINIT_ENDBACKUP;
REINIT_STARTRESTORE;
REINIT_ENDRESTORE;
REINIT_ABORTRESTORE;
REINIT_ACTIVATE_CHANGES.

Coldstart and Warmstart Reinit Type values are used to reinitialize device, the others are used to control the backup
or restore procedure. The backup or restore procedure begins with ReinitializeDevice(STARTBACKUP) or ReinitializeDevice(STARTRESTORE) message. During the backup or restore procedure the requesting device shall read or
write each configuration file of the responding device using Atomic Read File or Atomic Write File services. After finishing the backup or restore procedure, the requesting device shall send ReinitializeDevice(ENDBACKUP) or
ReinitializeDevice(ENDRESTORE) message. ReinitializeDevice(ABORTRESTORE) message may be sent to abort
restore in progress.

Subscribe COV
Description:
Subscribe COV Info is the service data type which appears in the Subscribe COV service to convey the information
from the COV Client to the COV Server. This data type replaces BACSTAC_SUBSCRIBE_COV_HOOK_INFO.

Declaration:
BACSTAC_SUBSCRIBE_COV_INFO pInfo;

The attributes contained in Subscribe COV Info data are:
BACSTAC_BOOLEAN
BACSTAC_UI32
BACSTAC_OBJECT_ID
BACSTAC_BOOLEAN
BACSTAC_UNSIGNED

fSubscribe;
processID;
monitoredObjectID;
issueConfirmedNotifications;
lifetime;

115

Chapter 3. Service Data Types
The fSubscribe attribute is TRUE if the data structure is used to create a new subscription. It is FALSE if this data
structure is used to cancel the existing subscription. In this case the last two attributes are not use by the service
routine.
The processID attribute is the numeric identifier of the Process within the COV client which shall receive the COV
notifications.
The monitoredObjectID attribute is the identifier of the object within the receiving device for which a subscription is
desired.
The issueConfirmedNotifications attribute (data type BACSTAC_BOOLEAN) indicates whether the COV-server
device shall issue ConfirmedCovNotification (BACSTAC_TRUE) or UnconfirmedCovNotification (BACSTAC_FALSE).
The lifetime attribute indicates the lifetime of the subscription in seconds. The value of BACSTAC_INFINITE_LIFETIME indicates an indefinite lifetime, with shall not automatically cancelled after any time. If the Subscribe
COV Info data is to cancel the subscription, then its first attribute’s value is FALSE, and two last attributes may have
any values.

Subscribe COV Property
Description:
The BACSTAC_SUBSCRIBE_COVP_INFO data structure is used by Subscribe COV Property service to convey any
requested information. This data structure contains a set of parameters: process identifier, monitored object identifier,
monitored property reference, confirmed flag, COV increment, and subscription lifetime. Bit flags grouped into the
mask field are used to indicate presence of the following optional parameters: lifetime, increment and confirmed flag. If
both lifetime and confirmed flag parameters are absent, the request shall be considered a cancellation. If the confirmed
flag is present but the lifetime parameter is not present, then infinite lifetime shall be assumed. The presence of both
lifetime and confirmed flag means a finite subscription. The last combination — lifetime is present and confirmed flag
is absent — is invalid. The value of zero (BACSTAC_INFINITE_LIFETIME) for lifetime designates infinite lifetime.

Subscribe COV Property Multiple Error
Description:
The BACSTAC_SUBS_COVP_MULTI_ERROR data type represents the BACnet error returned by the SubscribeCOVPropertyMultiple service requests. This data type contains either the ’Error Type’ parameter, of type
BACSTAC_ERROR_TYPE, or the ’First Failed Subscription’ parameter, which contains the ’Monitored Object
Identifier’ parameter, of type BACSTAC_OBJECT_ID, the ’Monitored Property Reference’ parameter, of type
BACSTAC_PROP_REF, and the ’Error Type’ parameter, of type BACSTAC_ERROR_TYPE. The choice is indicated

Text Message
Description:
This data structure of data type BACSTAC_TEXT_MESSAGE_INFO contains the Object Identifier of the Device
that initiated the request, a BACSTAC_BOOLEAN If-Message-Class-Present attribute (if it is FALSE then the Message Class attribute shall be ignored), the Message Class attribute of the BACSTAC_MESSAGE_CLASS data type,
which can contain either an unsigned or character string value, the Message Priority of the BACSTAC_MESSAGE_PRIORITY enumeration, which can be either MESSAGE_PRIORITY_NORMAL or MESSAGE_PRIORITY_URGENT, and the Character String conveying the text message.

Description:
The Time Synchronization Info data type BACSTAC_TIME_SYNC_INFO conveys the information for the TimeSynchronization application routines. This data type contains only the DateTime attribute. This data type replaces
BACSTAC_TIME_SYNC_INFO data type which, however, may still be used. The data type BACSTAC_UTC_TIME_SYNC_INFO which conveys information for Universal Time Co-ordinated Synchronisation routines represents the same data structure.

Who-Has
Description:
The BACSTAC_WHO_HAS_HOOK_INFO conveys the information for a WHO_HAS application hook. This data
type contains filterMin and filterMax, the optional arguments for the Who-Has request, which limit the range of
the Device instance numbers which are expected to respond to the Who-Has request. These arguments are omitted
from the request if both routine parameters have the value BACSTAC_NO_FILTER. This data type also contains a
Specification-Type attribute which is either Object-Name or Object-ID, and a tag to choose. A tag value may be either
WHO_HAS_ID or WHO_HAS_NAME. If a choice is Object-Name, the character string is to convey the name of
object and a String-Type to indicate a type of coding a character string.

Write File
Description:
The Write File data types convey the information for routines which generate and handle Atomic Write File service
requests. The BACSTAC_WRITE_FILE_INFO data type conveys the information for a Write File application hook.
This data type contains three fields: an object identifier of the File object, an Access Type of data type BACSTAC_FILE_ACCESS_TYPE which may be either FILE_ACCESS_STREAM or FILE_ACCESS_RECORD, and a Write
File Data field of data type BACSTAC_WRITE_FILE_DATA.
The BACSTAC_WRITE_FILE_DATA data type holds an octet string to copy into the file. In the Stream case there
are a Start Position parameter that indicates a start octet number from the beginning of the file at which the data shall
start being written, and an Octet String field that is to be written to the file. In the Record case there are a Start Record
Number field, a Record Count field that indicates a number of records to copy, and an Octet String field.
The BACSTAC_WRITE_FILE_RESULT data type indicates that the service was successfully executed. This data
structure contains a File Access Type field and either a Start Position or Start Record Number field which indicates
the number of octets or records from the beginning of the file where the data was actually written. A start position or
start record of zero indicates the first record/octet of the file.
The Write File Spec data structure (data type BACSTAC_WRITE_FILE_SPEC) contains two fields: File Access Type
(File Access Stream or File Access Record) and Write File Data.

Write Property Multiple
Description:
The BACSTAC_WRITE_PROP_MUL_INFO data type conveys the information for a Write Property Multiple application hook. This data type contains the information needed to access properties, and to write property values.
The BACSTAC_WRITE_PROP_MUL_INFO data structure contains two attributes. The first attribute indicates the
size of the buffer in the next attribute, expressed as the number of BACSTAC_WRITE_ACCESS_SPEC items in the
buffer. The second attribute is a pointer to the buffer which contains a list of BACSTAC_WRITE_ACCESS_SPEC
data structures.
The BACSTAC_WRITE_ACCESS_SPEC data structure contains the information to modify a number of properties
which belong to a single object. This data structure contains the Object Identifier, the size of the buffer (expressed as
the number of Write Items it contains), and the pointer to the buffer which contains a list of BACSTAC_PROPERTY_VALUE data structures. The BACSTAC_PROPERTY_VALUE data type is described in the Section called Property
Value in Chapter 4.

Chapter 4. Property Value Data Types
The data types that can appear as values of Properties are defined in the header file BACTYPES.H. Access routines for
these data types are defined in the header file BACACC.H. These files are automatically included when the BACstac
application header files BACSRV.H, BACGTW.H or BACCLI.H are used.
A BACstac application uses the Property Contents data type to represent the value of a Property in situations where
the Property could have any possible type. For instance, a Property Contents data type is used as an argument for
the Read-Property service request API routine. A Property Contents is attached to a C variable of one of the possible
types. The variable contains the actual value of the Property.
The following sections contain descriptions of each data type, including how to declare a variable of the data type, and
the access routines that can be used to manipulate the variable. The Property value data types are specified by Clause
21 of the BACnet protocol. This reference documentation is intended to be complemented by study of the BACnet
protocol as described in ANSI/ASHRAE Standard 135-2020 or later.

Access Rule
Description:
A Property Contents containing data of this type will have its tag equal to DATA_TYPE_ACCESS_RULE. An Access
Rule structure contains the following attributes:

•

Time-Range-Specifier is an Enumeration that specifies the evaluation of the Time-Range attribute.
This attribute can take two values:
• BACSTAC_AR_TIME_RANGE_SPECIFIED means that Time-Range references a property that will be evaluated
to BACSTAC_TRUE or BACSTAC_FALSE as defined for the Time-Range field.
• BACSTAC_AR_TIME_RANGE_ALWAYS means that the value of the Time-Range attribute is ignored and always
evaluates to BACSTAC_TRUE.

•

Time-Range is an attribute, of type Device Object Proterty Reference, references a property that can be evaluated
to BACSTAC_TRUE or BACSTAC_FALSE, which defines whether the rule is valid (BACSTAC_TRUE) or not
(BACSTAC_FALSE).
The Time-Range reference shall be considered unspecified if it contains 4194303 in the instance part of the object
identifier and in the device instance part of the device identifier, if present.
This attribute shall be present if Time-Range-Specifier is BACSTAC_AR_TIME_RANGE_SPECIFIED. If TimeRange-Specifier is BACSTAC_AR_TIME_RANGE_ALWAYS and this attribute is present, then this reference shall
be unspecified.
If Time-Range-Specifier is BACSTAC_AR_TIME_RANGE_SPECIFIED and this attribute references a property of
type other than BACSTAC_BOOLEAN, then the following evaluations apply:
• If the value of the referenced property is of type Unsigned, a value of zero shall evaluate to BACSTAC_FALSE,
while any other value shall evaluate to BACSTAC_TRUE.
• If the value of the referenced property is of type INTEGER, a value of less than or equal to zero shall evaluate to
BACSTAC_FALSE, while any value greater than zero shall evaluate to BACSTAC_TRUE.

148

Chapter 4. Property Value Data Types
•

•

•

If the value of the referenced property is of type BACnetBinaryPV, then INACTIVE shall evaluate to
BACSTAC_FALSE, while ACTIVE evaluates to BACSTAC_TRUE.
If the referenced property does not exist or is unspecified, or if its value cannot be retrieved or is of type NULL,
the Time-Range evaluates to BACSTAC_FALSE.
If the reference property is of any other type, then the evaluation is a local matter.

•

Location-Specifier is an enumeration that specifies how the Location attribute is evaluated. This attribute can take
two values:
• BACSTAC_AR_LOCATION_SPECIFIED mean that the Location attribute references a specific Access Point or
Access Zone object and is evaluated as specified for the Location attribute.
• BACSTAC_AR_LOCATION_ALL means that the value of the Location is ignored and matches any access controlled point.

•

Location is an optional attribute, of type Device Object Reference, refers to the Access Point or Access Zone that
this access rule is valid for.
The Location reference shall be considered unspecified if it contains 4194303 in the instance part of the object
identifier and in the device instance part of the device identifier, if present.
This attribute shall be present if Location-Specifier is BACSTAC_AR_LOCATION_SPECIFIED. If LocationSpecifier is BACSTAC_AR_LOCATION_ALL and this attribute is present, then this reference shall be unspecified.
If Location-Specifier is BACSTAC_AR_LOCATION_SPECIFIED, then the following evaluations apply:
When Location refers to an Access Point object, this access controlled point is required to be the location where
the credential used to request access has been authenticated.
• When Location refers to an Access Zone object, the access controlled point where the credential used to request
access has been authenticated is required to be an entry point to this zone.
• If the referenced object does not exist, is unspecified, or cannot be retrieved, then the Location evaluates to
BACSTAC_FALSE.
•

•

Enable is a Boolean attribute that specifies whether this rule is enabled (BACSTAC_TRUE) or not (BACSTAC_FALSE).

BACSTAC_ACCESS_RULE accessRule;

Action
The Action-Command and Action-List data types are used to represent the Action property of Command object.
Action property is an array of Action-Lists (a Property Contents tag shall be DATA_TYPE_ACTION_LIST). The
Action-List data structure contains a pointer to a buffer which contains a sequence of Action-Commands and a length
of the buffer expressed as a number of Action-Commands. If the action property is accessed using the list operations
(Add or Remove List Elements) then the Property Contents should contain one or more Action-Commands and the
tag shall be BACSTAC_ACTION_COMMAND.
The Action-Command data structure is a specification of a single value to be written to a single property of a single
object. It contains all co-ordinates of the value to be written: Device, Object and Property identifiers, Array-Index and
Priority (VOID if the property is not array or it is not a commandable property). This data structure also indicates
a behaviour of the process of writing an optional Post-Delay attribute represents a delay in seconds prior to the
execution of the next writing, Quit-On-Failure flag indicates if the device shall terminate the execution of the action
list prematurely in the case of writing fail (BACSTAC_TRUE) or writing shall continue after each failure with the next
element of the action list. A Write-Successful attribute of Action-Command data structure shall be set to BACSTAC_FALSE if the write fails for any reason. If the Quit-On-Failure attribute of Action-Command data structure is TRUE
and the write fails, then it terminate the execution list prematurely and set Write-Successful flag in subsequent entries
in the same list to BACSTAC_FALSE.

Declaration:
BACSTAC_ACTION_COMMAND action;
BACSTAC_ACTION_LIST actionList;

An Action-List is a list of Action-Commands, which may be empty. A Device-Id attribute of Action-Command data
structure is optional. If this attribute is not present, then the write shall be performed on objects residing in the device
that contains the Command object.

Audit Log Record
Description:
The Audit Log Record data type represents log records in the Audit Log object. These log records can be accessed
using the ReadRange and AuditLogQuery services for the Log Buffer property.
The data type contains the following attributes:
• timestamp, of type BACSTAC_DATE_TIME, stores the local date and time that the entry was placed into the

audit log.
• tag , of type BACSTAC_LOG_DATUM_TYPE, specifies the type of the logDatum attribute.
• logDatum stores the audit notification information, or a change in status or operation of the Audit Log object itself.

The logDatum can store one of the following attributes:
• logStatus, of type BACSTAC_BIT_STRING, represents a change in the status or operation of the Audit Log

object. Use BACSTAC_LOG_STATUS_BITS to set the correpoding bits in the logStatus Bit String.
• notification, of type BACSTAC_AUDIT_NOTIF, represents an audit notification that was received.
• timeChange, of type BACSTAC_REAL, represents a change in the clock setting in the device, records the number

of seconds and fraction of a second by which the clock changed.

Audit Notification
Description:
The Audit Notification contains the following attributes:

Source Timestamp, which conveys the time the operation was requested by the operation source (this attribute is
optional);
• Target Timestamp, which conveys the time the operation was performed by the operation target (this attribute is
optional);
•

Source Device, which conveys the device requesting the operation;
Source Object, which conveys the object requesting the operation (this attribute is optional);
Operation, which conveys the operation being requested;
Source Comment, which conveys a human readable description of the operation (this attribute is optional);
Target Comment, which conveys a human readable description of the operation (this attribute is optional);
Invoke Id, which conveys the invoke id from the service request that resulted in this audit record (this attribute is
optional);
Source User Id, which conveys the user performing the operation (this attribute is optional);
Source User Role, which conveys the role of the user performing the operation (this attribute is optional);
Target Device, which conveys the target device of the operation;
Target Object, which conveys the target object of the operation (this attribute is optional);
Target Property, which conveys the target of the operation if it is targeted at a property (this attribute is optional);
Target Value. For operations which include a value (such as when a write occurs) this field is present and contains
the new value;
Current Value. When an operation includes a value (such as when a write occurs) and the current value (before the
operation) of the target property is known, this field is present and contains the current property value;
Result. When the operation fails, this field shall be present and indicates the error that occurred.

Authentication Factor
Description:
An Authentication Factor structure is used to encapsulate an authentication factor value. This data structure contains
the following attributes:

Format-Type specifies the format of the authentication factor value in the Value field. The value of this field shall
be one of the format types specified in the Supported_Formats property. If there is no current authentication factor
value read by this object, then this field shall take on the value UNDEFINED. In addition, if this field contains a
value that is not specified in the Supported_Formats property, such as after a modification to the Supported_Formats
property or after the Out_Of_Service property changes from BACSTAC_TRUE to BACSTAC_FALSE, then this
field shall take on the value UNDEFINED. If an authentication factor is read that contains errors or that cannot be
interpreted as one of the specified format types, then this field shall take on the value ERROR.
• Format-Class shall contain the value specified in the Supported_Format_Classes array field that corresponds to the
authentication format type in the Format-Type field. If the Supported_Format_Classes property is not present, this
field shall always have a value of zero. If Format-Type has a value of UNDEFINED, then this field shall have a
value of zero.
• Value holds the authentication factor value data. The encoding of this value is specified in the Format-Type field.
•

A Property Contents containing data of this type will have its tag equal to DATA_TYPE_AUTHN_FACTOR.

Authentication Factor Format
Description:
An Authentication Factor Format data structure contains the following attributes:

Format-Type This attribute, of BACnetAuthenticationFactorType enumeration, specifies a supported authentication
factor format type.
• Vendor-ID This optional attribute, of type Unsigned16, is required when Format-Type attribute has a value of
CUSTOM. It shall contain the BACnet vendor identifier of the vendor which defined the custom format. This value
may differ from the Vendor_Identifier property value in the Device object, which identifies the device manufacturer.
If the Format-Type attribute does not have a value of CUSTOM and this attribute is present it shall have a value of
zero.
• Vendor-Format This optional attribute of type Unsigned16 is required when Format-Type attributes has a value
of CUSTOM. It shall contain a unique identifier that identifies a specific custom authentication factor format as
defined by the BACnet vendor in the Vendor-ID attribute. If the Format-Type attribute does not have a value of
CUSTOM and this attribute is present, then it shall have a value of zero.
•

A Property Contents containing data of this type will have its tag equal to DATA_TYPE_AUTHN_FACTOR_FORMAT.

vendorFormat to be present.

Authentication Policy
Description:
An Authentication Policy structure specifies the authentication policies defined for an Access Point object. This data
structure contains the following attributes:

Policy is a list of sequence elements that specifies the Credential Data Input objects which are used for this authentication policy. Each element of the list has Authentication Policy Item data type. If two or more entries of the
Policy list have the same index value this indicates that there is a choice between any of the authentication factors
supported by the Credential Data Input objects referenced by these entries. In this case the user may present any
one of these authentication factors.
• Order-Enforced if BACSTAC_TRUE, then the ordering sequence, as specified by the Index fields of this Policy list,
is enforced. If BACSTAC_FALSE, then the order is not enforced.
• Timeout of type Unsigned, specifies the maximum time in seconds for which all authentication factors, as defined
by this policy, must be presented. A value of zero indicates an unlimited time to present all authentication factors.
If not all authentication factors are presented in the allotted time, then a timeout occurs and authentication fails.
•

A Property Contents containing data of this type will have its tag equal to DATA_TYPE_AUTHN_POLICY.

Bit String
Description:
A Bit String is a BACnet primitive data type. A Property Contents containing data of this type will have its tag equal
to DATA_TYPE_BIT_STRING. A common Property that is represented as a Bit String is the Protocol-ServicesSupported Property maintained by each Device Object. The actual length of the Bit String (the number of reliable bits
in the data field) is indicated by the bitCount field. A BACstac Bit String is stored in a fixed length byte array, with a
capacity of 80 bits.

Channel Value
Description:
The Channel Value data type is a tagged union, which has two attributes: tag and value. The tag attribute, of data
type BACSTAC_DATA_TYPE, specifies the data type stored in the value attribute, which can be one of the following
data types: Real, Enumerated, Unsigned, Boolean, Integer, Double, Time, Character String, Octet String, Bit String,
Date, Object Identifier, or Lighting Command. If the tag attribute is DATA_TYPE_NULL then the value of Channel
Value is considered to be Null and the value attribute is ignored.

Character String
Description:
A Character String is a BACnet primitive data type. Any BACnet character string can be stored in the BACSTAC_CHAR_STRING data type. A Property Contents containing this data type will have its tag equal to DATA_TYPE_ANY_CHAR_STRING. A BACnet character string can be one of the five character sets described below. The enumeration data type BACSTAC_STRING_TYPE is used to represent each BACnet character set. In addition, BACSTAC_STRING_TYPE may have a STRING_NONE value, which is used to indicate the absent of an optional string.
Character Set

StringType

Delimiter

"C" data type

ISO 10646 (UTF-8)

STRING_UTF_8

X’00’

BACSTAC_CHAR[]

IBM/Microsoft DBCS

STRING_DBCS

X’00’

BACSTAC_CHAR*

JIS X 0208

STRING_JIS_X_0208

X’00’

BACSTAC_CHAR[]

ISO 10646 (UCS-4)

STRING_UCS_4

X’00000000’ BACSTAC_UCS4_CHAR[]

ISO 10646 (UCS-2)

STRING_UCS_2

X’0000’

BACSTAC_UCS2_CHAR[]

STRING_ISO_8859_1

DATA_TYPE_ISO_8859_1_STRING

X’00’

BACSTAC_CHAR[]

Note: [] symbols after some C type in the above table means an array of that type that is terminated by NULLcharacter. It should not confused with a pointer to that type, because the buffer of the property contents contains
an array of that type and not a pointer to it.

The delimiter is added by ASN decoder for convenience, but the application does not have to rely on it to determine
the total length of the string, because the total size of the string in bytes is ready available in BACSTAC_CHAR_STRING. When an application initializes a BACSTAC_CHAR_STRING, it can either specify the size explicitly (in
this case, the delimiter is not required) or it can specify BACSTAC_NULL_TERM_STRING as the character string
size. In the later case, the delimiter must be present, and it will be used by ASN encoder to determine the actual size
of the character string.

Declaration:
BACSTAC_CHAR_STRING charString;

Initializers:

BACSTAC_DBCS_CSTRING_INIT(codePage, string)

BACSTAC_UCS2_CSTRING_INIT(string)
BACSTAC_LATIN1_CSTRING_INIT(string)

BACSTAC_CHAR_STRING initializers for null-terminated C strings.
183

Chapter 4. Property Value Data Types
BACSTAC_UTF8_NSTRING_INIT(string, size)
BACSTAC_DBCS_NSTRING_INIT(codePage, string, size)
BACSTAC_JISX_NSTRING_INIT(string, size)
BACSTAC_UCS4_NSTRING_INIT(string, size)
BACSTAC_UCS2_NSTRING_INIT(string, size)
BACSTAC_LATIN1_NSTRING_INIT(string, size)

BACSTAC_CHAR_STRING initializers for strings whose length is specified explicitly as a number of _bytes_. The
string parameter does not have to be NULL-terminated, and if a NULL-terminated string is provided, the size parameter should indicate its length without the terminating NULL character. For example:
#define MY_ASTR "Hello world!"
BACSTAC_CHAR_STRING myAStr = BACSTAC_UTF8_NSTRING_INIT(MY_ASTR, sizeof(MY_ASTR)-1);
#define MY_WSTR L"Hello world!"
// For platforms where wchar_t is 16-bit:
BACSTAC_CHAR_STRING myWStr = BACSTAC_UCS2_NSTRING_INIT(MY_WSTR, sizeof(MY_WSTR)-2);
// For platforms where wchar_t is 32-bit:
BACSTAC_CHAR_STRING myWStr = BACSTAC_UCS4_NSTRING_INIT(MY_WSTR, sizeof(MY_WSTR)-4);

185

Chapter 4. Property Value Data Types

Alternative, it is possible to avoid using BACSTAC_CHAR_STRING and store the corresponding "C" data type
directly in the Property Contents. This method may appear simpler, especially if the application works only with one
character set, but it has a few shortcomings. First, it is impossible to learn the string length without scanning it until
the terminating symbol is found. Second, it is impossible to represent a BACnet character string that contains this
terminating symbol in the middle (such as a UTF-8 string with null-character). Third, having different BACSTAC_DATA_TYPE for representing the same BACnet type (character string) usually leads to larger and more complex code
where support of different character set is required. Fourth, it is impossible to put to the property contents a string if
it is not null-terminated. Fifth, all character strings in an array have to be encoded in the same character set.
However, to provide better compatibility with previous version of BACstac, the ASN decoder currently does not use
BACSTAC_CHAR_STRING (unless it is impossible to decode the character string otherwise) and decodes received
BACnet character strings directly to corresponding "C" data types inside of the Property Contents as described by the
following table.
String type

Tag

Delimiter

"C" data type

ISO 10646 (UTF-8)

DATA_TYPE_UTF_8_STRING

X’00’

BACSTAC_CHAR[]

IBM/Microsoft DBCS

DATA_TYPE_DBCS_STRING

X’00’

BACSTAC_DBCS_STRING

JIS X 0208

DATA_TYPE_JIS_X_0208_STRING

X’00’

BACSTAC_CHAR[]

ISO 10646 (UCS-4)

DATA_TYPE_UCS_4_STRING

X’00000000’ BACSTAC_UCS4_CHAR[]

ISO 10646 (UCS-2)

DATA_TYPE_UCS_2_STRING

X’0000’

BACSTAC_UCS2_CHAR[]

ISO 8859-1

DATA_TYPE_ISO_8859_1_STRING

X’00’

BACSTAC_CHAR[]

Note: [] symbols after some C type in the above table means an array of that type that is terminated by NULLcharacter. It should not confused with a pointer to that type, because the buffer of the property contents contains
an array of that type and not a pointer to it.

Client COV Increment
Description:
The Client-COV data structure is used to represent the Client-COV-Increment property in a Trend Log object. It may
contain either a real value increment or value NULL. A real value increment is used to determine that a change of value
has occurred. If the referenced object and property supports COV reporting according to Section "Change of Value
Reporting" of ANSI/ASHRAE Standard 135-2020 or later, NULL may be used, so a change of value is determined by
the criteria of the said section.

Declaration:
BACSTAC_CLIENT_COV clientCOV;

Initializers:
BACSTAC_NULL_CLIENT_COV_INIT

This macro initializes the Client-COV data structure with the default increment, which is the value NULL.
BACSTAC_REAL_CLIENT_COV_INIT(incrementValue)

This macro initializes the Client-COV data structure with the real increment. The increment parameter is a real value
that specifies the increment to be used in determining that a change of value has occurred.

Access Routines:
BACSTAC_BOOLEAN BACstacInitClientCOVToReal(
BACSTAC_CLIENT_COV *clientCOV ,

188

Chapter 4. Property Value Data Types

BACSTAC_CLIENT_COV *clientCOV );

COV Multiple Subscription
Description:
BACSTAC_COV_MULTI_SUBSCRIPTION is a data structure representing value of a PROP_ACTIVE_COV_MULTI_SUBSCRIPTIONS property in the device object. A Property Contents containing data of this type will
have its tag equal to DATA_TYPE_COV_MULTI_SUBSCRIPTION. The data type consists of a Recipient (which
has the BACSTAC_RECIPIENT_PROCESS data type), an Issue Confirmed Notifications flag, a Time Remaining
value (which is the number seconds of seconds before the subscription is expired), a Max Notification Delay (which
has the BACSTAC_UNSIGNED data type) and a List of COV Subscription Specifications. Each element of this list
has the BACSTAC_COV_SUBSCRIPTION_SPEC data type and consists of a Monitored ObjectID (which has the
BACSTAC_OBJECT_ID data type) and a List of COV References. Each element of this list has the BACSTAC_COV_REFERENCE data type and consists of a Monitored Property (which has the BACSTAC_PROP_REF data
type), an optional COV Increment (which is used for subscription to properties that have the Real data type) and a
Timestamped flag.

BACSTAC_COV_MULTI_SUBSCRIPTION subscription;

COV Subscription
Description:
BACSTAC_COV_SUBSCRIPTION is a data structure representing value of a PROP_ACTIVE_COV_SUBSCRIPTIONS property in the device object. A Property Contents containing data of this type will have
its tag equal to DATA_TYPE_COV_SUBSCRIPTION. The data type consists of a Recipient (which has the
BACSTAC_RECIPIENT_PROCESS data type), a Monitored Property Reference (BACSTAC_OBJ_PROP_REF), an
Issue Confirmed Notifications flag, a Time Remaining value (which is the number seconds of seconds before the
subscription is expired), and an optional COV Increment (which is used for subscription to properties that have
the Real data type). The BACSTAC_INFINITE_LIFETIME constant is used as a Time Remaining value for
subscriptions that never expire.

Date
Description:
A Date is a BACnet primitive data type. A Property Contents containing data of this type will have its tag equal to
DATA_TYPE_DATE. A Date contains year, month, day of month and day of week attributes. Each of the attributes has
a special value indicating that the attribute is unspecified: YEAR_UNSPECIFIED, MONTH_UNSPECIFIED, DAY_OF_MONTH_UNSPECIFIED, and DAY_OF_WEEK_UNSPECIFIED correspondingly. The day of week attribute is
not modified by BACstac to be consistent with the other attributes of the Date.

Date Range
Description:
A Date Range contains a Start Date and an End Date. This data type is one of the possible contents of the Calendar
Entry data type, which is used in the Date List Property in the Calendar Object and the Special Event Property of a
Schedule Object. A Property Contents containing data of this type will have its tag equal to DATA_TYPE_DATE_RANGE. Fields of a Date data type may be unspecified, so it is possible for the Start Date or End Date of a Date
Range to be unspecified. In this case the attribute acts as a wildcard: for example, if the Start Date is unspecified, it
means "any date up to and including the End Date".

Destination
Description:
A Destination determines a set of conditions for sending notifications. A list of this data type is used in the Recipient
List property of the Notification Class Object. Destination attributes indicate valid days of week and time interval, a
notification recipient, a process identifier, whether the notification should be made using the confirmed or unconfirmed
service, and flag bits which indicate those state transitions (Offnormal, Fault, Return) for which this recipient is
suitable. A Property Contents containing data of this type will have its tag equal to DATA_TYPE_DESTINATION.

Object Selector
Description:
The Object Selector data type is a tagged union, which has two attributes: tag and selector . The tag attribute, of
data type BACSTAC_DATA_TYPE, specifies the data type stored in the selector attribute, which can be one of the
following data types: Enumerated(Object Type) or Object Identifier. If the tag attribute is DATA_TYPE_NULL then the
value of Object Selector is considered to be Null and the selector attribute is ignored.

Event Log Record
Description:
The Event Log Record conveys the event notification parameters or status changes in the Event Log object. This data
structure contains the following attributes:

•
•

Timestamp stores the local date and time when the record was collected.
LogDatum contains the notification information, or a change in status or operation of the Event Log object itself.

BACSTAC_LOG_DATUM_TYPE is used to describe the LogDatum type. The list of possible values for BACSTAC_LOG_DATUM_TYPE is given in Appendix D. For meaning of each LogData type, please refer to Section 12.27.13
of ANSI/ASHRAE Standard 135-2020 or later.

Declaration:
BACSTAC_EVENT_LOG_RECORD

logRecord;

The standard types of log datum and the corresponding data and their fields are the following:
Status

logStatus;

Notification

Time Change
BACSTAC_REAL

timeChange;

Event Notification
Description:
The Event Notification contains the following attributes:

•
•
•
•
•
•
•
•
•
•
•
•
•

Process Identifier, which conveys the identification of the process in the receiving device for which the notification
is intended;
Initiating Device Identifier, which conveys the Device Object_Identifier of the device that initiated the Event Notification Request;
Initiating Object Identifier, which specifies the Object_Identifier of the object that is initiating the notification;
Time Stamp, which conveys the current time as determined by the clock in the device issuing the service request;
Notification Class, which designates the notification class of the event;
Priority, which specifies the priority of the event that has occurred;
Event Type, which specifies the type of event that has occurred;
Message Text, which conveys a string of printable characters (this attribute is optional);
Notify Type, which conveys whether this notification is an event or an alarm or a notification that someone has
acknowledged a previous event notification;
AckRequired, which conveys whether this notification requires acknowledgment or not (this attribute shall only be
present if the ’Notify Type’ parameter is EVENT or ALARM);
From State, which indicates the Event_State of the object prior to the occurrence of the event that initiated this
notification (this attribute shall only be present if the ’Notify Type’ parameter is EVENT or ALARM);
To State, which indicates the Event_State of the object after the occurrence of the event that initiated this notification;
Event Values, which conveys a set of values relevant to the particular event and whose content depends on the type
of object that initiated the notification.

Declaration:
BACSTAC_EVENT_NOTIF eventNotif;

Chapter 4. Property Value Data Types

Event Notification - Notification Parameters
Description:
Notification Parameters data type describes the reason an event has occurred. This data type appears as the Event
Values parameter of the Event Notification structure. The data structure of Notification Parameters depends on the
type of event-initiating object. Every Event Type tag represents the corresponding Notification Parameter data type.
The complex event type or Extended event type can be used for implementation of proprietary event algorithm. For
a discussion of the relationship between the Event Type and Object Type and the Alarm and Event Services see
clause 13 of the BACnet standard. To support a new BACnet encoding method that was introduced in Add-135-2001b
BACSTAC_NP_BUFR_PARAM2 structure and corresponding access routines were added. BACSTAC_NP_BUFR_PARAM data type and corresponding access routines also may be used. The Event Type tag changes that were made
in versions 4.1 and 4.2 are described in Addendum 135a 2001 (extended), Addendum 135b 2001 (bufferReady2) and
Addendum 135c 2001(unsignedRange).

Initialize the Notification Parameters for each type of Event. For Complex Events, the Event Type must exceed 64.
For Command Failure Events, Notification Parameters receive a Property Contents buffers provided by Command
Value and Feedback Value arguments of an Init() routine. For Change of Status Flags Events, if optional argument
pPresentValue is present (is not NULL) Notification Parameters receive a Property Contents buffer provided by Present
Value argument of an Init() routine.

Extended Notify Parameter
Description:
The Extended Notify Parameter data type is used to define an array of parameters, which is pointed to by the
pParameters attribute in the Extended data type of Notification Parameters.
The Extended Notify Parameter data type is a tagged union, which has two attributes: tag and param. The tag
attribute, of data type BACSTAC_DATA_TYPE, specifies the data type stored in the param attribute, which can be
one of the following data types: Real, Unsigned, Boolean, Integer, Double, Octet String, Bit String, Character String,
Enumerated, Date, Time, Object Identifier, or Device Object Property Value. If the tag attribute is DATA_TYPE_NULL
then the value of Extended Notify Parameter is considered to be Null and the param attribute is ignored.

Declaration:
BACSTAC_NP_E_PARAMETER

extParam;

Event Notification Subscription
Description:
An Event Notification Subscription data structure contains the following attributes:

Recipient This attribute, of type Recipient specifies the destination device(s) to receive notifications.
Process Identifier This attribute, of type Unsigned32 specifies the handle of a process within the recipient device
that is to receive the event notification.
• Issue Confirmed Notifications This attribute, of type Boolean is BACSTAC_TRUE if confirmed notifications are to
be sent and BACSTAC_FALSE if unconfirmed! notifications are to be sent.
• Time Remaining This attribute, of type Unsigned specifies actual time the entry will remain in the Subscribed_Recipients in seconds.
•

Event Parameter
Description:
The Event Parameter data type defines the conditions that will generate an event. This data type is used in the Event
Parameters property of the Event Enrollment Object. A Property Contents containing data of this type will have its tag
equal to DATA_TYPE_EVENT_PARAMETER2. Events generation is based on the value of a referenced property.
Depending on the type of event initiating object and the event type, an Event Parameters can contain one of several
sets of fields. The choice of fields is indicated by an Event Type tag (see BACSTAC_EVENT_TYPE enumeration in
Appendix D). Events are described in clauses 12.11 and 13.X of ANSI/ASHRAE Standard 135-2020 or later.

Declaration:
BACSTAC_EVENT_PARAMETER2 parameter;

The standard types of event and the corresponding data structures and their fields are the following:
The BACnet standard defines the following event types:
•
•
•
•
•
•
•
•
•
•
•
•
•
•
•
•
•
•
•

Change of Bit String
Change of State
Change of Value
Command Failure
Floating Limit
Out of Range
Buffer Ready
Change of Life Safety
Unsigned Range
Extended
Access Event
Double Out of Range
Signed Out of Range
Unsigned Out of Range
Change of Character String
Change of Status Flags
None
Change of Discrete Value
Change of Timer

Change of Bit String specifies an event that occurs when the value of the referenced property becomes equal to one
of the values contained in the List_Of_Bitstring_Values after applying the Bitmask, and that value remains equal for
Time_Delay seconds.
Change of State specifies an event that occurs when the value of the referenced property becomes equal to one of the
values contained in the List_Of_Values, and this value remains equal for Time_Delay seconds.
Change of Value specifies an event that occurs when the absolute value of a referenced property changes by an amount
equal to or greater than the Referenced_Property_Increment, and this condition remains for Time_Delay seconds.

239

Chapter 4. Property Value Data Types
Command Failure specifies an event that occurs if the values of the referenced property and the Feedback_Property_Reference disagree for a time period greater than the Time_Delay parameter.
Floating Limit specifies an event that occurs if the referenced property leaves a range of values determined by the
current value of the Setpoint_Reference, High_Diff_Limit, Low_Diff_Limit, and Deadband.
Out of Range specifies an event that occurs if the referenced property leaves a range of values defined by the
High_Limit and Low_Limit parameters and remains there for Time_Delay seconds.
Buffer Ready specifies an event that occurs when the number of records specified by Notification_Threshold have
been entered into the log since the start of operation or the previous notification, whichever is most recent.
Change of Life Safety specifies an event that occurs when the value of the referenced property becomes equal to any of
the values in the List_Of_Life_Safety_Alarm_Values, and remains within the set of values in this list for Time_Delay
seconds.
Unsigned Range specifies an event that occurs if the referenced property leaves the range of values from Low_Limit
through High_Limit parameters and remains there for Time_Delay seconds.
Extended specifies a proprietary event algorithm. It contains vendorID, extendedEventType, and a sequence of parameters. Each parameter can be any primitive data type or a reference to a property.
Access Event specifies an event that occurs when the value of the property referred to by
Access_Event_Time_Reference changes and the referenced property is equal to one of the values contained in the
List_Of_Access_Events. This type of event may be applied only to properties that are of type BACnetAccessEvent.
Double Out of Range occurs if the referenced property leaves a range of values defined by the High_Limit and
Low_Limit parameters and remains there for Time_Delay seconds.
Signed Out of Range occurs if the referenced property leaves a range of values defined by the High_Limit and
Low_Limit parameters and remains there for Time_Delay seconds.
Unsigned Out of Range occurs if the referenced property leaves a range of values defined by the High_Limit and
Low_Limit parameters and remains there for Time_Delay seconds.
Change of Character String occurs when the value of the referenced property contains one of the nonempty values in
the List_Of_Values, and continues to contain a non-empty value from the list for Time_Delay seconds.
Change of Status Flags occurs when the referenced property, which must be of type BACnetStatusFlags, has a value
of BACSTAC_TRUE for any of its flags that also has a value of BACSTAC_TRUE in the corresponding flag in the
Selected_Flags event parameter for longer than Time_Delay seconds.
None was introduced for the case an object does not apply an event algorithm.
Change of Discrete Value occurs when the referenced property, which must be of type Boolean, Unsigned, Integer,
Enumerated, Character String, Octet String, Date, Time, BACnetObjectIdentifier or BACnetDateTime, changes and
remains changed for Time_Delay seconds.
Change of Timer occurs when the value of the referenced property becomes equal to any any of the values contained
in Alarm_Values, and remains within the set of values in this list for Time_Delay seconds.

an event notification is issued.

Initialize Event Parameter for a Change of Life Safety Event. Event of this type occurs when the value of the referenced
property becomes equal to any of the values in the List Of Life Safety Alarm Values, and remains within the set of
values in this list for Time Delay seconds. The resulting event state is LIFE_SAFETY_ALARM.
A Change of Life Safety Event also occurs when the value of the referenced property becomes equal to any of the
values in the List Of Alarm Values, and remains within the set of values in this list for Time Delay seconds. The
resulting event state is OFFNORMAL.
The Fault_Values property lists each of the possible Present_Value states that shall be interpreted as FAULT.

Copy an Event Parameter into a Property Contents.

Extended Event Parameter
Description:
The Extended Event Parameter data type is used to define an array of parameters, which is pointed to by the
pParameters attribute in the Extended data type of Event Parameter.
The Extended Event Parameter data type is a tagged union, which has two attributes: tag and param. The tag
attribute, of data type BACSTAC_DATA_TYPE, specifies the data type stored in the param attribute, which can be
one of the following data types: Real, Unsigned, Boolean, Integer, Double, Octet String, Bit String, Character String,
enumerated, Date, Time, Object Identifier, or Device Object Property Reference. If the tag attribute is DATA_TYPE_NULL then the value of Extended Event Parameter is considered to be Null and the parameters attribute is ignored.

Declaration:
BACSTAC_EP_E_PARAMETER extParam;

Access Routines:
BACSTAC_BOOLEAN BACstacInitEP2ExtParamNull(
BACSTAC_EP_E_PARAMETER *pExtParam);
BACSTAC_BOOLEAN BACstacInitEP2ExtParamReal(

Extended Fault Parameter
Description:
The Extended Fault Parameter data type is used to define an array of parameters, which is pointed to by the
parameters attribute in the Extended data type of Fault Parameter.
The Extended Fault Parameter data type is a tagged union, which has two attributes: tag and param. The tag
attribute, of data type BACSTAC_DATA_TYPE, specifies the data type stored in the param attribute, which can be
one of the following data types: Real, Unsigned, Boolean, Integer, Double, Octet String, Bit String, Character String,
Enumerated, Date, Time, Object Identifier, or Device Object Property Reference. If the tag attribute is DATA_TYPE_NULL then the value of Extended Fault Parameter is considered to be Null and the param attribute is ignored.

Declaration:
BACSTAC_FAULT_EXT_PARAMETER extParam;

Fault Parameter
Description:
The Fault Parameter data type specifies parameters of Fault Algorithm (see clauses 12.11 and 13.X of ANSI/ASHRAE
Standard 135-2020 or later). This data type is used in the Fault Parameters property of the Event Enrollment Object.
A Property Contents containing data of this type will have its tag equal to DATA_TYPE_FAULT_PARAMETER. A
Fault Parameters can contain one of several sets of fields. The choice of fields is indicated by an Fault Type tag (see
BACSTAC_FAULT_TYPE enumeration in Appendix D).

Declaration:
BACSTAC_FAULT_PARAMETER parameter;

The standard types of fault and the corresponding data structures and their fields are the following:
The BACnet standard defines the following fault types:
•
•
•
•
•

Fault None
Fault Characterstring
Fault Extended
Fault Life Safety
Fault State
257

Chapter 4. Property Value Data Types
Fault Status Flags
Fault Out Of Range
• Fault Listed
•
•

Fault None has not parameters.
Fault Characterstring contains parameter Fault_Values. This parameter, of type list of CharacterString, represents a
list of character strings that are considered fault values.
Fault Extended contains following parameters: Vendor_ID of type Unsigned, represents the vendor identification
code for the fault type of the vendor-proprietary fault algorithm. Fault_Type of type Unsigned, represents the vendorproprietary fault algorithm. Parameters represents a list of primitive or constructed values whose interpretation is
specific to the proprietary fault algorithm. Each element of the list has Extended Fault Parameter data type.
Fault Life Safety contains following parameters: Mode_Property_Reference has Device Object Property Reference
data type, referent’s value represents the life safety mode value monitored by this algorithm. Fault_Values of type list
of Life Safety State, represents a list of values that are considered fault values.
Fault State contains parameter Fault_Values. This parameter is a list of discrete values that represent the fault values.
Fault Status Flags contains parameter Status_Flags. This parameter has Device Object Property Reference data type,
referent’s value is the status flags value monitored by this algorithm.
Fault Out Of Range contains following parameters: Min has Real, Unsigned, Double or Integer data type. MinTag
parameter of data type BACSTAC_DATA_TYPE is to make a choice of a parameter data type. These parameters
represents the minimum normal value. Max has Real, Unsigned, Double or Integer data type. MaxTag parameter of
data type BACSTAC_DATA_TYPE is to make a choice of a parameter data type. These parameters represents the
maximum normal value.
Fault Listed contains parameter Listed. This parameter has Device Object Property Reference data type, referent’s
value is the fault signals value monitored by this algorithm.

An FDT Entry data type structure contains four attributes: the B/IP address of the registrant (the array of bytes), the
length of this array, time to live in seconds at the time of registration (Unsigned16) and remaining time to live in
seconds, incl. grace period (Unsigned16).

Landing Door Status
Description:
A Landing Door Status structure represents the list of landing doors for the door of the car. Each element of this list
is Landing Call data sructure and consists of the universal floor number and the currently active door status for the
landing door. The status values that each landing door status can take on are:

•
•
•
•
•
•
•
•

UNKNOWN The landing door status is unknown.
NONE There is no landing door for the respective car door.
CLOSING The landing door is closing.
CLOSED The landing door is fully closed but not locked.
OPENING The landing door is opening.
OPENED The landing door is fully opened.
SAFETY_LOCK The landing door is fully closed and locked.
LIMITED_OPENED The landing door remains in a state between fully closed and fully opened.

Chapter 4. Property Value Data Types

Lighting Command
Description:
Lighting Command structure is used to request special lighting commands with specific behaviors. This data structure
contains the following attributes:

•
•
•
•
•
•

Operation This attribute is an enumeration of type BACSTAC_LIGHTING_OPERATION that defines the lighting
operation desired.
Target Level This attribute, of type BACSTAC_REAL, represents the target lighting output level in the normalized
range (0.0%...100.0%).
Ramp Rate This attribute, of type BACSTAC_REAL, represents the rate of change in percent-per-second for ramp
operations. The range of allowable ramp-rate values is 0.1 to 100.0 inclusive.
Step Increment This attribute, of type BACSTAC_REAL, represents the percent amount to be added to
Present_Value when stepping. The range of allowable values is 0.1% to 100.0% inclusive.
Fade Time This attribute, of type BACSTAC_UNSIGNED, represents the time in milliseconds over which fade
operations take place. The range of allowable fade-time values is 100 ms to 86400000 ms (1 day) inclusive.
Priority This attribute, of type BACSTAC_PRIORITY_LEVEL, represents the priority values 1 (highest priority)
through 16 (lowest priority).

Log Multi Record
Description:
The Log Multi Record conveys either a set of recorded data values or errors related to data-collection, a status change
in the Trend Log Multiple object, or an indication that the time and/or date was changed in the device hosting the
Trend Log Multiple object. This data structure contains the following attributes:

Timestamp stores the local date and time when the record was collected.
• LogData contains the set of recorded data values or errors related to data-collection, a status change in the Trend
Log Multiple object itself, or an indication that the time and/or date was changed in the device hosting the Trend
Log Multiple object.
•

BACSTAC_LOG_DATA_TYPE is used to describe the type of the LogData. The list of possible values for
BACSTAC_LOG_DATA_TYPE is given in Appendix D. For meaning of each LogData type, please refer to Section 12.30.19 of ANSI/ASHRAE Standard 135-2020 or later.

277

Chapter 4. Property Value Data Types

BACSTAC_LOG_MULTI_RECORD

logMultiRecord;

logMultiRecord contains Timestamp and LogData fields. Timestamp defines the timestamp of the record, and is defined
as:
BACSTAC_DATE_TIME

timeStamp;

LogData contains log data of the current record, which may be one of the following types:
BACSTAC_BIT_STRING
BACSTAC_LOG_DATA_LIST
BACSTAC_REAL

logStatus;
logData;
timeChange;

Log Record
Description:
The Log-Record data structure is used in a Trend Log object to represent the Log-Buffer property, which is a list of
Log-Records. Each Log-Record conveys a recorded data value, an error related to data-collection, or status changes
in the Trend Log object, and has data fields as follows:

Timestamp stores the local date and time when the record was collected.
LogDatum contains the data value read from the monitored object and property, an error encountered in an attempt
to read a value, or a change in status or operation of the Trend Log object itself.
• StatusFlags stores the Status_Flags property of the monitored object, if present. If the Status_Flags property is not
present or not available atomically associated with the data value, this item shall not be included in the log record.
•
•

BACSTAC_LOG_RECORD_TYPE is used to describe the type of the record. The list of possible values for
BACSTAC_LOG_RECORD_TYPE is given in Appendix D. For meaning of each record type, please refer to Section
12.25.14 of ANSI/ASHRAE Standard 135-2020 or later.

Declaration:
BACSTAC_LOG_RECORD logRecord;

A Name Value data type consists of three attributes. A Name attribute has its Character string. A Value attribute has
its data type either NULL, or Boolean, or Unsigned, or Integer, or Real, or Double, or Character String, or Octet

Null
Description:
A Null value is a special BACnet primitive data type. A Property Contents containing data of this type will have
its tag equal to DATA_TYPE_NULL. A Null value is written to a commandable Property to relinquish control of a
commandable Property. When this is done the corresponding Priority Array Item will have a Null value. A Null value
can only exist inside a Property Contents or Priority Array Item, and has no external C representation.

None.

Priority Array Item
Description:
A Priority Array is a property that is present in an Object that contains a commandable Property (such as the presentvalue of an Output or Value Object). A Priority Array has BACSTAC_MAX_PRI_ARRAY (16) slots, each of which
can contain a value for the commandable Property. For the Object types supported in the present BACstac version,
the value contained in a Priority Array has one of the data types Null, Enumerated, Real, Unsigned, Boolean, Integer,
Double, Time, Character String, Octet String, Bit String, Date, Object Identifier or Date Time. See Section 19 of
ANSI/ASHRAE Standard 135-2020 or later for a description of command prioritization using Priority Arrays.
A Property Contents containing a single Priority Array Item or an entire Priority Array, will have its tag equal to
DATA_TYPE_PRIORITY_ARRAY_ITEM. The Elements-Number attribute of a Property Contents indicates whether
it contains a single Priority Array Item or an entire array.

Property Value
Description:
A Property Value contains the identity and current value of a Property. It consists of a Property Identifier, optional
Array Index, value and optional Priority Level. A list of Property Values is used by the Read-Property-Multiple and
Write-Property-Multiple Services, and as Notification Parameters for Complex Events. A Property Contents containing data of this type will have its tag equal to DATA_TYPE_PROPERTY_VALUE.

Proprietary Property
Description:
A proprietary property may be defined in any object by the application. If the property cannot be represented by an
existing data type, the application can provide "raw" ASN.1 representation of that data type. Similarly, if the BACstac
decoder encounters a proprietary property, which data types is unknown, it passes the result to the application in the
"raw" ASN.1 format. The BACSTAC_RAW_ASN1_VALUE structure is used for this purpose. It contains a reference
to ASN.1 data and its length. A Property Contents containing data of this type have the data type tag equal to DATA_TYPE_PROPRIETARY or DATA_TYPE_NEW_STANDARD or DATA_TYPE_EXTENDED. The DATA_TYPE_PROPRIETARY is used for properties that have property-identifier or object-type in the range reserved for proprietary
properties and object; DATA_TYPE_NEW_STANDARD is used when the above parameters in the range reserved for
standard properties and objects, but BACstac does not know it yet; DATA_TYPE_EXTENDED is used in the case
where the combination of the object-type and property-identifier is known to the BACstac stack, but it cannot be
decoded (presumably this data type was extended, but it could be a result of incorrect encoding by the peer device).

Declaration:
BACSTAC_RAW_ASN1_VALUE

rawValue;

Initializers:
BACSTAC_RAW_ASN1_VALUE_INIT(asnData, asnLength)
BACSTAC_EMPTY_RAW_ASN1_VALUE_INIT

Access Routines:

BACSTAC_RAW_ASN1_VALUE *asn1Value,
const BACSTAC_BYTE *asnData,

322

BACSTAC_VALUE_SIZE asnLength);

buffer to store the cloned structure. The cloned structure preserves the reference to the same ASN.1 data as the original
one had. The data type tag of the property contents is set to DATA_TYPE_PROPRIETARY.

Real
Description:
A Real value is a BACnet primitive data type. A Property Contents containing data of this type will have its tag equal
to DATA_TYPE_REAL. A Real value is represented in BACstac applications as a C double.

Declaration:
BACSTAC_REAL realValue;

Recipient
Description:
A Recipient identifies a BACnet Device that can receive events or Change-of-Value notifications. The recipient device
can be identified either by an Object Identifier or by a BACnet Address. The Recipient data type is used by Device,
Event Enrollment and Notification Class objects. A Property Contents containing data of this type will have its tag
equal to DATA_TYPE_RECIPIENT.

Chapter 4. Property Value Data Types

Scale
Description:
A Scale data structure contains either floatScale or integerScale, which indicates the conversion factor to be multiplied
with the value of the Present_Value property to provide a value in the units indicated by Units. For floatScale, the
indicated value in Units is the result of a multiplication Present_Value with this floatScale. For integerScale, the
indicated value in Units is the result of a multiplication Present_Value with power of ten of this integerScale. A
Property Contents containing data of this type will have its tag equal to DATA_TYPE_SCALE.

Declaration:
BACSTAC_SCALE scale;

Access Routines:
BACSTAC_BOOLEAN BACstacInitScaleReal(
BACSTAC_SCALE *pScale,
BACSTAC_REAL floatScale);

The routine initializes the Scale data structure with to have the given floatScale.
BACSTAC_BOOLEAN BACstacInitScaleInt(
BACSTAC_SCALE *pScale,
BACSTAC_INTEGER integerScale);

The routine initializes the Scale data structure to have the given integerScale.
BACSTAC_DATA_TYPE BACstacGetScaleType(
const BACSTAC_SCALE *pScale);

The routine returns DATA_TYPE_REAL for floatScale or DATA_TYPE_INTEGER for integerScale.
BACSTAC_REAL BACstacGetScaleFloatScale(
const BACSTAC_SCALE *pScale);
BACSTAC_INTEGER BACstacGetScaleIntegerScale(
const BACSTAC_SCALE *pScale);

These routines return a value of the corresponding scale.

The Shed Level type is used in the Load Control Object, and may express the shedding level either in percent of the
Full Duty rating (LEVEL_TYPE_PERCENT), or as a number of preconfigured levels (LEVEL_TYPE_LEVEL), or in
amount of kilowatts (LEVEL_TYPE_AMOUNT). To support the Load Control Object, the application should support
at least the LEVEL type. Support for PERCENT and AMOUNT types is optional. A Property Contents containing
data of this type will have its tag equal to DATA_TYPE_SHED_LEVEL.

Declaration:
BACSTAC_SHED_LEVEL shedLevel;

Stage Limit Value
Description:
The Stage Limit Value data structure determines behavior of the object when a Present_Value is changed. This structure consists of three attributes: the Limit attribute, of type Real, determines the upper limit of the current stage; the
Value attribute, of type Bit-String, determines which values are written to objects referred by the Target_References
property when the Present_Stage is changed; the Deadband attribute, of type Real, determines how much the
Present_Value should deviate from the Limit value for the Present_Stage property to change. The Present_Stage
property does not change as long as the Present_Value is less or equal to the Limit value plus the Deadband value of
the current stage and it is greater or equal to the Limit value minus the Deadband value of the previous stage.

BACSTAC_STAGE_LIMIT_VALUE stageLimitValue;

DATA_TYPE_TIME. The BACstac Time consists of hour, minute, second and hundredths of second attributes. Each
of the attributes has a special value indicating that the attribute is unspecified: HOUR_UNSPECIFIED, MINUTE_UNSPECIFIED, SECOND_UNSPECIFIED, and HUNDREDTHS_UNSPECIFIED correspondingly.

Timer State Change Value
Description:
The Timer State ChangeValue represents the values that are to be written to the referenced properties when a change
of the timer state occurs. This data type is a choice of the following options:

•
•

•
•
•

no-value option, of type NULL, is used to indicate that no value shall be written when the respective change of
timer state occurs.
null, boolean, unsigned, signed, real, double, octetstring, character-string, bit-string, enumerated, date, time,
object-id options specify a value of the respective primitive datatype. The option ’null’ may be used in combination with other datatypes for specifying a relinquish command for a commandable property.
constructed-value option specifies a value of complex datatype. This option shall not be selected if the respective
data type is supported by a defined option.
date-time option specifies a value of datatype BACnetDateTime.
lighting-command option specifies a value of datatype BACnetLightingCommand.

Declaration:
BACSTAC_TS_CHANGE_VALUE timerStateChangeValue;

Time Value
Description:
A Time Value contains a Time and a Property Value. This data type is used in the Daily Schedule and Special Event

Declaration:
BACSTAC_TIME_VALUE timeValue;

Initializers:

BACSTAC_TIME_VALUE_INIT is a Time Value initializer, which initializes the data structure to the given time and
property contents.
BACSTAC_TIME_VALUE_INIT_TO_VAR(hour, minute, second, hundredths, dataType, var)

BACSTAC_TIME_VALUE_INIT_TO_VAR is a Time Value initializer, which initializes the data structure with the
given time and property contents being a reference to the specified variable. The dataType parameter describes the
BACstac data type of this variable.

for BACSTAC_TIME_VALUE_INIT(BACSTAC_CONTENTS_INIT_TO_VAR(BACSTAC_TIME_INIT(hour, minute,
second, hundredths), BACSTAC_CONTENTS_INIT_TO_VAR(dataType, var))

Chapter 5. General API
The following routines are used by an application to initialize and control the BACstac libraries and underlying
protocol stack.
The underlying protocol stack has a number of default communication properties (APDU timeouts, segmentation
parameters, local address, etc.) that can be changed if necessary.
On some platforms, the protocol stack can multiplex BACnet services to allow a few client applications to share one
port. An application that wants to receive COV and event notification, should register one or more Process IDs in
which it is interested.
If an applications wants to change or to extend the BACstac default action for some service, it should register hooks
the corresponding hook.

BACstacCancelResolveOper
Name

Synopsis

BACSTAC_RESOLVE_OPER *operArea);

Arguments
operArea

A pointer to the resolver operation that should be canceled.

Description
Cancels an asynchronous resolver operation.

Return Value
The routine returns BACSTAC_TRUE if the operation was canceled. The function returns BACSTAC_FALSE if the
operation is completed, and the user callback is already invoked or is about to be invoked.

in Appendix E.

BACstacDecodeAsnValue
Name
BACstacDecodeAsnValue — decodes an ASN.1 value to the given C type

Synopsis
BACSTAC_STATUS BACstacDecodeAsnValue(
const BACSTAC_BYTE *asnValue,
BACSTAC_VALUE_SIZE asnLength,
BACSTAC_PROPERTY_CONTENTS *cValue,
BACSTAC_VALUE_SIZE *decodedLength,

363

Chapter 5. General API
BACSTAC_IALLOC *iAlloc);

Arguments
asnValue

Pointer to an ASN.1 value to decode.
asnLength

Length of the ASN.1 value in bytes.
cValue

Pointer to a Property Contents that contains the buffer into which the value will be decoded. If iAlloc is NULL,
the buffer attribute must be initialized by the callee to a buffer sufficient size to hold the decoded value. If iAlloc
is not NULL, the buffer of the required size will be allocated by the decoder, but the callee is responsible to
free it later using the BACstacFreeContents() routine. The callee is also responsible to set Property Contents tag
attribute to the desired data type, and nElements to the maximum number of elements that the Property Contents
may contain. Upon successful completion of this routine, the nElements attribute contains the actual number of
decoded elements.
decodedLength

Pointer to the variable that on successful completion contains the actually decoded ASN.1 length. This allows
to decode only the beginning of the given ASN.1 value as the specified data type without decoding the rest. If
this pointer is NULL then either the whole value is decoded or BACSTAC_STATUS_INVALID_DATA_TYPE
is returned.
iAlloc

A pointer to an allocator interface. This parameter may be NULL then the buffer pointed by the pContents
parameter will be used to receive the result. If the allocator interface is provided then the buffer will be allocated
and should be freed later using the BACstacFreeContents() routine.

Description
The routine decodes an ASN.1 value to the specified C data type.

Return Value
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_STATUS
in Appendix E.

364

Chapter 5. General API

BACstacDecodePropertyValue
Name
BACstacDecodePropertyValue — decodes an ASN.1 value of a property

Synopsis
BACSTAC_STATUS BACstacDecodePropertyValue(
BACSTAC_OBJECT_TYPE objectType,
BACSTAC_PROPERTY_ID propertyID,
BACSTAC_ARRAY_INDEX arrayIndex,
const BACSTAC_BYTE *asnValue,
BACSTAC_VALUE_SIZE asnLength,
BACSTAC_PROPERTY_CONTENTS *cValue,
BACSTAC_IALLOC *iAlloc);

Arguments
objectType

The Object type of the object that contains the property.
propertyID

The Property Identifier of the property.
nIndex

The index of an array item. If the property is not an array, the index value shall be BACSTAC_VOID_INDEX.
If the property is an array then BACSTAC_ENTIRE_ARRAY is used to decode a value that represents the entire
array; BACSTAC_ARRAY_COUNT is used to decode a value that represents the number of elements in it;
andpositive number is used to decode a value that represent just one element of the array.
cValue

Pointer to a Property Contents that contains the buffer into which the value will be decoded. If iAlloc is NULL,
the buffer attribute must be initialized by the callee to a buffer sufficient size to hold the decoded value. If iAlloc
is not NULL, the buffer of the required size will be allocated by the decoder, but the callee is responsible to
free it later using the BACstacFreeContents() routine. Upon successful completion of this routine, the Property
Contents tag attribute indicates the type of the Property, and the nElements attribute contains the number of
decoded elements of the specified type.
asnValue

Pointer to ASN.1 value.

365

Chapter 5. General API
maxBACnetLength

The size of the ASN.1 value in bytes.
iAlloc

A pointer to an allocator interface. This parameter may be NULL then the buffer pointed by the pContents
parameter will be used to receive the result. If the allocator interface is provided then the buffer will be allocated
and should be freed later using the BACstacFreeContents() routine.

Description
The routine decodes an ASN.1 value for the specified property. The combination of objectType, propertyID, and
arrayIndex determines the desired C type.

Return Value
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_STATUS
in Appendix E.

BACstacDisconnectDirectConnect
Name
BACstacDisconnectDirectConnect — disconnect a direct connection

Synopsis
BACSTAC_STATUS BACstacDisconnectDirectConnect(
BACSTAC_BYTE portID,
const BACSTAC_BYTE vmac[6]);

Arguments
portID

Port identifier of the BACnet/SC port.

366

Chapter 5. General API
vmac

VMAC address of the peer BACnet/SC node.

Description
The routine initiates the local disconnection procedure for an initiated or accepted direct connection. The direct connection is identified by portID and VMAC. The local disconnect procedure is described in Clause AB.6.2.2 and
AB.6.2.3 of the BACnet standard for an initiated and accepted direct connection correspondingly.
The routine does not guarantee that the connection is closed on successful return, however, it is possible to initiate
a new direct connection with the same PortID and VMAC immediately without waiting for the specified connection
being closed.
Note: The routine returns success if the given PortID specifies an existing BACnet/SC port and either the disconnect procedure has been started or the direct connection has not been found (it could have been closed before or
did not exist at all).

Return Value
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_STATUS
in Appendix E.

Arguments
enable

Enable (BACSTAC_TRUE) or disable (BACSTAC_FALSE) receive notifications with any Process Identifier.

Description
By default, a BACstac application can receive only COV and Event/Alarm notifications with ProcessIDs that are explicitly registered using the BACstacRegisterProcessID() or BACstacRegisterUniqueProcessID() routines. This routine allows to receive notifications with any Process Identifier except those that are explicitly registered by other
applications that share the same port as the current application.

Return Value
None.
