Chapter 5. General API

BACstacGetDeviceBinding
Name
BACstacGetDeviceBinding — obtains Device Binding information from the resolver cache

Synopsis
BACSTAC_STATUS BACstacGetDeviceBinding(
BACSTAC_ADDRESS_BINDING *buffer,
BACSTAC_ELEMENT_COUNT size,
BACSTAC_ELEMENT_COUNT *count);

Arguments
buffer

A pointer to the buffer that receives the array of variables of the BACSTAC_ADDRESS_BINDING data type.
size

The maximum number of elements that can be stored in the buffer.
count

A pointer that on successful return contains the number of elements stored in the buffer.

Description
Obtains device binding information currently stored in the resolver cache. The resolver cache does not store information about all discovered device on the BACnet internetwork, but not more than the Device ID Cache Size specified
in the BACstac configuration. If the total number of devices exceed that number than the cache preserves information
about most recently used devices.
By giving buffer equal to NULL and size to zero, it is possible to obtain the current number of elements stored in
the resolver cache. However, it this number can be changed asynchronously by the default action of I-Am. So, two
consequent calls to the cache can return different numbers of device binding elements.

378

BACstacSetHook
Name
BACstacSetHook — sets a service hook

Synopsis
BACSTAC_STATUS BACstacSetHook(
BACSTAC_HOOK_TYPE eHookType,
BACSTAC_HOOK_PROC pfnHookProc);

Arguments
eHookType

The hook type, which may be one of BACSTAC_HOOK_TYPE enumeration values (see Appendix D of this
document).

392

Chapter 5. General API
pfnHookProc

A pointer to the hook routine. Hook routines are provided by application.

Description
Registers a hook routine, which receives an incoming BACnet requests for the corresponding BACnet service. The
hook may be used to implement the service procedure or to modify the default BACstac processing of BACnet service
requests. There can be only one hook procedure per a BACnet service. If another hook is registered for the same
BACnet service, then the new hook procedure replaces the old one. A NULL pointer cancels the current hook.
Usually hooks are registered immediately after initialization of BACstac and remain registered until BACstacClose().
Though it is possible to set or cancel a hook at any time, the old hook may still be invoked for some time after its
replacement or cancellation. This happens because hooks are invoked asynchronously on other threads than the one
that invoked BACstacClose(). Therefore, the application should never destroy resources used by a hook after canceling
it without taking extra steps to exclude the race condition.
The recommended way to destroy resources used by hook is to guard these resources with a mutex and a cancellation
flag. Before using the resources, the hook should acquire the mutex and check the cancellation flag. If the cancellation
flag is not set, the hook can use the resources, and after finishing using them, the hook should release the mutex. When
the application wants to destroy the resources, it should acquire the mutex, set the cancellation flag and destroy the
resources, then release the mutex. The mutex should remain valid until BACstacClose() is complete.
Note: If the same mutex is used by different hooks, this may create undesirable mutex contention, so if you need
to replace or cancel more than one hook, you may want to have a dedicated mutex for each hook.

Return Value
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_STATUS
in Appendix E.

Chapter 6. Handling Requests - Hooks
Service Hooks are application supplied subroutines, which are registered with the BACstac libraries to handle incoming BACnet requests. A hook receives all service parameters of an incoming BACnet request as the appropriate C
data structure. The description of service specific parameters is provided in Chapter 3. The description of general data
types used to represent different property values are described in Chapter 4. Besides the service parameters, hooks
also receive the source and destination addresses of an incoming request as well as the request identifier (called a TSM
handle, after the Transaction State Machine used by the BACnet application layer to process each request).
Hooks are registered with the libraries using the BACstacSetHook routine and are executed asynchronously on one of
internal BACstac threads. There can be only one registered hook per BACnet service. Usually an application registers
all hooks during start and keeps them until they are cancelled by BACstacClose(). If an application wants to cancel
or change a hook on the fly, it can do that, but it should take extra steps to exclude potential race conditions due to
asynchronous execution of hooks. For more information, see the description of the BACstacSetHook() routine.
Some BACnet services have the default action using the BACstac database. For these services, the hook can return
HOOK_STATUS_DEFAULT to indicate that the default action should be invoked to process the request. If a BACnet
service does not have the default action then the hook is responsible for execution of an incoming request and sending
a response if it is a confirmed service.
An application can handle any request either directly in the hook or asynchronously in another thread (potentially after
returning from the hook). In either case, the hook should return HOOK_STATUS_OK to indicate that the application is
responsible for execution of the received request.
Execution of any request starts with validation of its service parameters. If parameters are valid then the request can be
processed. If necessary, the application can access objects and properties stored in the BACstac database. Processing
of any confirmed service must be completed with either sending a successful response, or an error, or abort, or reject
as it is specified in the BACnet Service Procedure. If no response can be sent (e.g. the transaction has been aborted
by APDU timeout or a Client-Abort) then BACstacDestroyTSM should be used to destroy the transaction and free all
resources associated with it.
It is important to keep in mind the lifetime of pointers received by hook upon its invocation. For confirmed services, all
received pointers remain until a response is sent or the transaction is destroyed. For unconfirmed services all received
pointers remain valid until return from the hook.
Thus if you want to execute any unconfirmed service asynchronously, you have to copy all data that you want to use
in asynchronous processing. This includes BACnet addresses, service parameters, and all other data pointed to by
service parameters (i.e. you have to perform a deep copy of C data structures).
If you want to execute a confirmed service asynchronously, you can rely on all pointers to remain valid until the
response is sent, so there is no need to copy service parameters. However, it is important not to use any received
pointer after the response is sent successfully even if it happens inside of the hook. This is because sending any
response completes the transaction and frees all resources. You still may use any pointer if the response function
failed for any reason, because in this case the transaction is not complete and associated with it data remain valid.
Note: If an application forgets to complete a transaction either by sending a response or by destroying it, then the
transaction remains dormant indefinitely, which leads to leak of resources and eventually inability of the application
to receive any new confirmed request from the network.

400

items. If the list of items is too long to fit to the response, it is automatically truncated to the allowed size of the
response, so it contains as many items as possible. When the list of items is truncated the ’noMoreItems’ flag is reset
in the response.

Return Value
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_STATUS
in Appendix E.

Name

Synopsis
BACSTAC_STATUS BACstacDestroyTSM(
BACSTAC_HTSM hTransaction);

Arguments
hTransaction

Transaction handle for the request to be processed by the hook.

Description
Completes a service procedure by destroying the transaction without generating any BACnet reply. A BACstac gateway application can use this routine to terminate the transaction directed to a non-existing device. If the destination
device exists, the only valid reason to use this routine is to destroy a transaction that cannot be answered in a normal
way (for instance, the transaction was already aborted before the application tried to send a response or the current
Device Communication state does not allow to send any response).

Return Value
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_STATUS
in Appendix E.

Arguments
hTransaction

Transaction handle for the request to be processed by the hook.
pSummaries

A pointer to a memory block to hold a list of Enrollment Summary items. This argument may be NULL if the
list contains no items. In this case the nSummaryCount argument also has to be 0.
nSummaryCount

The number of items in the Enrollment Summary list. If there are no items in the list, this argument is 0 and
pSummaries == NULL.

Description
Completes the Enrollment-Summary service procedure by generating an Enrollment-Summary-ACK reply. Conveys
information about all event-initiating objects that meet the search criteria specified in the request routine. This information is represented as a list of Enrollment Summary data structures. The list may be NULL if no object was found.
In this case the list length must be zero. This is a hook completion routine. All confirmed service hooks must call
a response or error completion routine to perform transaction clean-up and to send a response over the BACnet. On
successful completion, the routine frees all resources used by the transaction. Otherwise, BACstacSrvcAbort should
be used to send the appropriate abort (such as ABORT_BUFFER_OVERFLOW if the error code was BACSTAC_STATUS_RESPONSE_TOO_LONG). If the transaction was already aborted or sending abort is not possible for any
other reason then BACstacDestroyTSM should be used to free all resources consumed by the transactions.

Completes the Get-Event-Information service procedure by generating a Get-Event-Information-ACK, which conveys
the information about "event-active" objects. "Event-active" objects are objects that have an Event State property other
than STATE_NORMAL or have an acked-transitions property which has at least one of the bits (TO_OFFNORMAL,
TO_FAULT, TO_NORMAL) set to BACSTAC_FALSE.
On successful completion, the routine sends the Get-Event-Information-ACK and frees all resources used by the
transaction. Otherwise, BACstacSrvcAbort should be used to send the appropriate abort (such as ABORT_BUFFER_OVERFLOW if the error code was BACSTAC_STATUS_RESPONSE_TOO_LONG). If the transaction was already
aborted or sending abort is not possible for any other reason then BACstacDestroyTSM should be used to free all
resources consumed by the transactions.

A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_STATUS
in Appendix E.

than STATE_NORMAL or have an acked-transitions property which has at least one of the bits (TO_OFFNORMAL,
TO_FAULT, TO_NORMAL) set to BACSTAC_FALSE. If the response is too long include all event summaries, it is
truncated to the maximum possible count for the given APDU parameters. In an unlike case that even a single event

the transaction. Otherwise, BACstacSrvcAbort should be used to send the appropriate abort (such as ABORT_SEGMENTATION_NOT_SUPP if the error code was BACSTAC_STATUS_SEG_NOT_SUPPORTED). If the transaction was already aborted or sending abort is not possible for any other reason then BACstacDestroyTSM should be

Name

Synopsis

BACSTAC_HTSM hTransaction);

Arguments
hTransaction

Transaction handle for the request to be processed by the hook.

428

Chapter 6. Handling Requests - Hooks

Description
Completes a service procedure by generating a Simple-ACK. This completion routine should be used
only by services that do not convey any specific response information to the request initiator. For
instance, such services are Acknowledge-Alarm, Add-List-Element, Confirmed-COV-Notification,
Confirmed-Event-Notification, Device-Communication-Control, Reinitialize-Device, Remove-List-Element,
Subscribe-COV, Subscribe-COV-Property, Write-Property, Write-Property-Multiple and some other services. On
successful completion, the routine sends the Simple-ACK and frees all resources used by the transaction. Otherwise,
BACstacSrvcAbort should be used to send the appropriate abort (such as ABORT_BUFFER_OVERFLOW if the
error code was BACSTAC_STATUS_RESPONSE_TOO_LONG). If the transaction was already aborted or sending
abort is not possible for any other reason then BACstacDestroyTSM should be used to free all resources consumed
by the transactions.

Return Value
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_STATUS
in Appendix E.

BACSTAC_ACK_ALARM_HOOK_PROC
Name
BACSTAC_ACK_ALARM_HOOK_PROC — acknowledgeAlarm service hook

Synopsis
BACSTAC_HOOK_STATUS (*BACSTAC_ACK_ALARM_HOOK_PROC)(
BACSTAC_HTSM hTransaction,
BACSTAC_ADDRESS *sourceAddress,
BACSTAC_ADDRESS *destinationAddress,
const BACSTAC_ACK_ALARM_INFO *pServiceInfo);

Arguments
hTransaction

Transaction handle for the current service request.
pSourceAddress
pDestinationAddress

Pointers to the BACnet Addresses of the request initiator and request destination.
pServiceInfo

A pointer to the service information data structure. This data structure is of data type BACSTAC_ACK_ALARM_INFO. It is described in the Section called Acknowledge Alarm in Chapter 3.

Description
The BACSTAC_ACK_ALARM_HOOK_PROC type defines a pointer to the Acknowledge-Alarm service hook. This
hook allows a BACstac application to process the Acknowledge-Alarm service, as there is no default action for this
service in the present BACstac version. The hook receives all parameters of a service request and is responsible for
all error checking (object existence, supporting of event generation by this type of objects, correctness of timestamp
and event states, and other necessary checks).
432

Chapter 6. Handling Requests - Hooks
If necessary, the service procedure can access local properties stored in the BACstac database using BACstacRetrievePropertyInstance2, BACstacStorePropertyInstance, or any building block routine described in Chapter 12.
The hook must return HOOK_STATUS_OK to indicate that it is responsible for processing a service request. Processing of a service request must be completed by invoking one of the following transaction completion API routines:
BACstacSrvcResponse, BACstacSrvcAbort, BACstacSrvcError, BACstacSrvcReject, or BACstacDestroyTSM. BACstacDestroyTSM() should be used only when no response can be sent (for example, the transaction has been aborted
due to APDU_Timeout). The completion of a transaction frees all memory associated with it, so the transaction handle
and all pointers passed to the hook become invalid.

Return Value
HOOK_STATUS_OK

Indicates that the application becomes responsible for processing the service request.

BACSTAC_ADD_ELEMENT_HOOK_PROC
Name
BACSTAC_ADD_ELEMENT_HOOK_PROC — addListElement service hook

Synopsis
BACSTAC_HOOK_STATUS (*BACSTAC_ADD_ELEMENT_HOOK_PROC)(
BACSTAC_HTSM hTransaction,
BACSTAC_ADDRESS *pSourceAddress,
BACSTAC_ADDRESS *pDestinationAddress,
const BACSTAC_CHANGE_LIST_INFO *pServiceInfo);

Arguments
hTransaction

Transaction handle for the current service request.
pSourceAddress
pDestinationAddress

Pointers to the BACnet Addresses of the request initiator and request destination.

433

Chapter 6. Handling Requests - Hooks
pServiceInfo

A pointer to the service information data structure. The fields of this data structure include the objectID, ePropertyID, nIndex, and a buffer in which to place the Property Contents data type list. This data structure is of data type
BACSTAC_CHANGE_LIST_INFO. It is described in the Section called Add/Remove List Element in Chapter 3.

Description
The BACSTAC_ADD_ELEMENT_HOOK_PROC type defines a pointer to the Add-List-Element service hook. This
hook allows a BACstac application to override the default BACstac processing of an Add-List-Element service request.
This hook receives all parameters of a service request and is responsible for all error checking (object and property
existence, array index correctness, value correctness, and so forth).
If necessary, the service procedure can access local properties stored in the BACstac database using BACstacRetrievePropertyInstance2, BACstacStorePropertyInstance, BACstacAddElement, or any other building block routine
described in Chapter 12.
If the hook procedure chooses not to override the default action, it must return HOOK_STATUS_DEFAULT and do
not try to process the request. If the hook procedure takes responsibility for processing a service request, it must return
HOOK_STATUS_OK and complete processing a service request by invoking one of the following transaction completion API routines: BACstacSrvcResponse, BACstacSrvcAbort, BACstacChangeListError, BACstacSrvcReject, or
BACstacDestroyTSM. BACstacDestroyTSM() should be used only when no response can be sent (for example, the
transaction has been aborted due to APDU_Timeout). The completion of a transaction frees all memory associated
with it, so the transaction handle and all pointers passed to the hook become invalid.

Return Value
HOOK_STATUS_OK

Indicates that the application becomes responsible for processing the service request.
HOOK_STATUS_DEFAULT

Indicates that the hook did not service the request, and that the default BACstac actions should handle the service
request.

The BACSTAC_CREATE_OBJECT_HOOK_PROC type defines a pointer to the Create-Object service hook. This
hook allows a BACstac application to process the Create-Object service, as there is no default processing of this
service in the present BACstac version. The hook receives all parameters of a service request and is responsible for
all error checking (device existence, support dynamic creation of objects of the given type, validity all initialization
parameters, and so forth).
The hook must return HOOK_STATUS_OK to indicate that it is responsible for processing a service request. Processing of a service request must be completed by invoking one of the following transaction completion API routines: BACstacCreateObjectResponse, BACstacSrvcAbort, BACstacCreateObjectError, BACstacSrvcReject, or BACstacDestroyTSM. BACstacDestroyTSM() should be used only when no response can be sent (for example, the transaction has been aborted due to APDU_Timeout). The completion of a transaction frees all memory associated with it,
so the transaction handle and all pointers passed to the hook become invalid.

Return Value
HOOK_STATUS_OK

Indicates that the application becomes responsible for processing the service request.

A pointer to the service information data structure. The fields of this data structure include the time duration

Description
The BACSTAC_DCC_HOOK_PROC type defines a pointer to the Device-Communication-Control service hook. This
hook allows a BACstac application to override the default BACstac processing of a Device-Communication-Control
service request. The hook receives all parameters of a service request and is responsible for all error checking (device
existence, timeout value, password correctness).
Aside from validation of service parameters and starting a timer, if necessary, the service procedure should normally
use either BACstacSetDCCValue (in a BACstac server) or BACstacSetDCCValueByAddress in a BACstac gateway)
to disable or enable processing of service requests by the BACstac stack.
If the hook procedure chooses not to override the default action, it must return HOOK_STATUS_DEFAULT and do
not try to process the request. If the hook procedure takes responsibility for processing a service request, it must

transaction has been aborted due to APDU_Timeout). The completion of a transaction frees all memory associated

BACSTAC_HTSM hTransaction,

hTransaction

pDestinationAddress

pServiceInfo

A pointer to the service information data structure. The fields of this data structure include the objectID, ePropertyID and nIndex. Read Info data structure is described in the Section called Read Property in Chapter 3.

457

Chapter 6. Handling Requests - Hooks

Description
The BACSTAC_READ_PROP_HOOK_PROC type defines a pointer to the Read-Property service hook. This hook
allows a BACstac application to override the default BACstac processing of a Read-Property service request. The hook
receives all parameters of a service request and is responsible for all error checking (object and property existence,
array index correctness).
If necessary, the service procedure can access local properties stored in the BACstac database using BACstacRetrievePropertyInstance2 or any building block routine described in Chapter 12. The service procedure should treat the
Object-Identifier parameter equal to {OBJ_DEVICE, BACSTAC_INST_NUMBER_MAX} as the Object-Identifier
matching the local Device object.
If the hook procedure chooses not to override the default action, it must return HOOK_STATUS_DEFAULT and do
not try to process the request. If the hook procedure takes responsibility for processing a service request, it must
return HOOK_STATUS_OK and complete processing a service request by invoking one of the following transaction
completion API routines: BACstacReadPropResponse, BACstacSrvcAbort, BACstacSrvcError, BACstacSrvcReject,
or BACstacDestroyTSM. BACstacDestroyTSM() should be used only when no response can be sent (for example, the
transaction has been aborted due to APDU_Timeout). The completion of a transaction frees all memory associated
with it, so the transaction handle and all pointers passed to the hook become invalid.
Note: If the Read-Property service hook is registered, the default action for the Read-Property-Multiple service
is no longer takes values from the BACstac database directly but sends Read-Property service requests to itself.
This allows the Read-Property hook to intercept the read requests that comes in the form of Read-PropertyMultiple requests. However, sending a lot of Read-Property requests to itself significantly slows down processing
of the Read-Property-Multiple service. Therefore, it is better to avoid setting the Read-Property hook and use the
Read-Property callback if it is sufficient for the stated goal. Alternatively, you may also register the Read-PropertyMultiple hook and retrieve property values directly from the BACstac database without sending Read-Property
requests to itself.

Return Value
HOOK_STATUS_OK

Indicates that the application becomes responsible for processing the service request.
HOOK_STATUS_DEFAULT

Indicates that the hook did not service the request, and that the default BACstac actions should handle the service
request.

(password correctness, the device internal status, the current Communication status, etc).
The hook must return HOOK_STATUS_OK to indicate that it is responsible for processing a service request. Processing of a service request must be completed using one of the transaction completion API routines: BACstacSrvcResponse, BACstacSrvcAbort, BACstacSrvcError, BACstacSrvcReject, BACstacActivateNpoChanges, or BACstacDestroyTSM. BACstacDestroyTSM() should be used only when no response can be sent (for example, the transaction
has been aborted due to APDU_Timeout). The completion of a transaction frees all memory associated with it, so the
transaction handle and all pointers passed to the hook become invalid.

Return Value
HOOK_STATUS_OK

Indicates that the application becomes responsible for processing the service request.

Chapter 6. Handling Requests - Hooks

BACSTAC_HTSM hTransaction,

const BACSTAC_CHANGE_LIST_INFO *pServiceInfo);

Arguments
hTransaction

Transaction handle for the current service request.
pSourceAddress
pDestinationAddress

Pointers the BACnet Addresses of the request initiator and request destination.
pServiceInfo

A pointer to a BACSTAC_CHANGE_LIST_INFO data structure. The fields of this data structure include the
objectID, ePropertyID, nIndex and a buffer in which to place the Property Contents data type list. This data
structure is described in the Section called Add/Remove List Element in Chapter 3.

Description
The BACSTAC_REMOVE_ELEMENT_HOOK_PROC type defines a pointer to the Remove-List-Element service
hook. This hook allows a BACstac application to override the default BACstac processing of an Remove-List-Element
service request. This hook receives all parameters of a service request and is responsible for all error checking (object
and property existence, array index correctness, value correctness, and so forth).
If necessary, the service procedure can access local properties stored in the BACstac database using BACstacRetrievePropertyInstance2, BACstacStorePropertyInstance, BACstacRemoveElement, or any other building block routine described in Chapter 12.
If the hook procedure chooses not to override the default action, it must return HOOK_STATUS_DEFAULT and do
not try to process the request. If the hook procedure takes responsibility for processing a service request, it must return
HOOK_STATUS_OK and complete processing a service request by invoking one of the following transaction completion API routines: BACstacSrvcResponse, BACstacSrvcAbort, BACstacChangeListError, BACstacSrvcReject, or
BACstacDestroyTSM. BACstacDestroyTSM() should be used only when no response can be sent (for example, the
transaction has been aborted due to APDU_Timeout). The completion of a transaction frees all memory associated
with it, so the transaction handle and all pointers passed to the hook become invalid.

463

Return Value
HOOK_STATUS_OK

Indicates that the application becomes responsible for processing the service request.
HOOK_STATUS_DEFAULT

Indicates that the hook did not service the request, and that the default BACstac actions should handle the service
request.

Name

Synopsis
BACSTAC_HOOK_STATUS (*BACSTAC_SUBSCRIBE_COV_HOOK_PROC)(
BACSTAC_HTSM hTransaction,
BACSTAC_ADDRESS *sourceAddress,
BACSTAC_ADDRESS *destinationAddress,
const BACSTAC_SUBSCRIBE_COV_INFO *pServiceInfo);

Arguments
hTransaction

Transaction handle for the current service request.
pSourceAddress
pDestinationAddress

Pointers to the BACnet Addresses of the request initiator and request destination.
pServiceInfo

A pointer to the service information data structure. This data structure is of data type BACSTAC_SUBSCRIBE_COV_INFO. It is described in the Section called Subscribe COV in Chapter 3.

464

Chapter 6. Handling Requests - Hooks

Description
The BACSTAC_SUBSCRIBE_COV_HOOK_PROC type defines a pointer to the Subscribe-COV service hook. This
hook allows a BACstac application to process this service. If the BACstac database has the Active_COV_Subscriptions
property in the Device object set to ’AUTO’ in the TPI file then BACstac has the default action for this service. In
this case, the hook will override the default BACstac processing of a Subscribe-COV service request. If the BACstac
database does not have the Active_COV_Subscriptions property in the Device object or this property was not set to
’AUTO’ in the TPI file then BACstac does not have the default action for the Subscribe-COV service.
If necessary, the service procedure can access local properties stored in the BACstac database using BACstacRetrievePropertyInstance2, BACstacStorePropertyInstance, BACstacChangeCovSubs, or any building block routine described
in Chapter 12.
If the BACstac has the default action for this service enabled (by setting the Active_COV_Subscriptions property
to ’AUTO’) and the hook procedure chooses not to override the default action, it must return HOOK_STATUS_DEFAULT and do not try to process the request. Otherwise the hook procedure takes responsibility for processing a
service request, so it must return HOOK_STATUS_OK and complete processing a service request by invoking one of
the following transaction completion API routines: BACstacSrvcResponse, BACstacSrvcAbort, BACstacSrvcError,
BACstacSrvcReject, or BACstacDestroyTSM. BACstacDestroyTSM() should be used only when no response can be
sent (for example, the transaction has been aborted due to APDU_Timeout). The completion of a transaction frees all
memory associated with it, so the transaction handle and all pointers passed to the hook become invalid.

Return Value
HOOK_STATUS_OK

Indicates that the application becomes responsible for processing the service request.
HOOK_STATUS_DEFAULT

Indicates that the hook did not service the request, and that the default BACstac actions should handle the service
request. It is only possible if the default action for this service is enabled.

of a service request and is responsible for all error checking (device and object existence, the source BACnet address,
and others).
The BACSTAC_CONF_AUDIT_RAW_HOOK_PROC type is just an alias to BACSTAC_CONF_AUDIT_HOOK_PROC, which is added to make the HOOK_PROC name match its hook type: HOOK_CONF_AUDIT_NOTIF_RAW.
If an application wants to process a service request after returning from the hook procedure, it should copy all hook
parameters, because all pointers passed to the hook become invalid on return from the hook. Because this service
has no default action, the hook is responsible for processing a service request, so it should always return HOOK_STATUS_OK.

HOOK_STATUS_OK

parameters have the value BACSTAC_NO_FILTER. The fields of this data structure also include either the

The BACSTAC_WHO_HAS_HOOK_PROC type defines a pointer to the Who-Has service hook. This hook allows a

parameters of a service request and is responsible for all error checking.
If the application wants to process a service request after returning from the hook procedure, it should copy all hook
parameters, because all pointers passed to the hook become invalid on return from the hook. During processing a
Who-Has request, the service procedure may want to use the BACstacSelectObjects() API routine, which returns the
list of all objects that satisfy the given Who-Has parameters.

The BACSTAC_WHO_IS_HOOK_PROC type defines a pointer to the Who-Is service hook. This hook allows a
BACstac application to override the default BACstac processing of a Who-Is service request. The hook receives all
parameters of a service request and is responsible for all error checking (validity of the device instance range).
If the application wants to process a service request after returning from the hook procedure, it should copy all hook
parameters, because all pointers passed to the hook become invalid on return from the hook. During processing a
service request, the service procedure of a BACstac gateway application may want to get the list of all available
devices in the BACstac database using the BACstacGetDeviceList API routine.
If the hook procedure chooses not to override the default action, it must return HOOK_STATUS_DEFAULT. If the
hook procedure takes responsibility for processing a service request, it must return HOOK_STATUS_OK.

Return Value
HOOK_STATUS_OK

Indicates that the application becomes responsible for processing the service request.
HOOK_STATUS_DEFAULT

Indicates that the hook did not service the request, and that the default BACstac actions should handle the service
request.

pDestinationAddress

pServiceInfo

A pointer to the service information data structure. The fields of this data structure include objectID, File Access
Type (either FILE_ACCESS_STREAM or FILE_ACCESS_RECORD) and Write File Data structure. Write File
Info and Write File Range data structures are described in the Section called Write File in Chapter 3.

Description
The BACSTAC_WRITE_FILE_HOOK_PROC type defines a pointer to the Atomic-Write-File service hook. This
hook allows a BACstac application to process this service, as there is no default action for this service in the present
BACstac version. The hook receives all parameters of a service request and is responsible for all error checking.
The hook must return HOOK_STATUS_OK to indicate that it is responsible for processing a service request. Processing of a service request must be completed by invoking one of the following transaction completion API routines:
BACstacWriteFileResponse, BACstacSrvcAbort, BACstacSrvcError, BACstacSrvcReject, or BACstacDestroyTSM.
BACstacDestroyTSM() should be used only when no response can be sent (for example, the transaction has been
aborted due to APDU_Timeout). The completion of a transaction frees all memory associated with it, so the transaction handle and all pointers passed to the hook become invalid.

Return Value
HOOK_STATUS_OK

Indicates that the application becomes responsible for processing the service request.

Description
The BACSTAC_WRITE_PROP_HOOK_PROC type defines a pointer to the Write-Property service hook. This hook
allows a BACstac application to override the default BACstac processing of a Write-Property service request. The hook
receives all parameters of a service request and is responsible for all error checking (object and property existence,
correctness of array index, command priority, and written property value).
If necessary, the service procedure can access local properties stored in the BACstac database using BACstacStorePropertyInstance or any building block routine described in Chapter 12.
If the hook procedure chooses not to override the default action, it must return HOOK_STATUS_DEFAULT and do
not try to process the request. If the hook procedure takes responsibility for processing a service request, it must
return HOOK_STATUS_OK and complete processing a service request by invoking one of the following transaction completion API routines: BACstacSrvcResponse, BACstacSrvcAbort, BACstacSrvcError, BACstacSrvcReject,
or BACstacDestroyTSM. BACstacDestroyTSM() should be used only when no response can be sent (for example, the

484

Chapter 6. Handling Requests - Hooks
transaction has been aborted due to APDU_Timeout). The completion of a transaction frees all memory associated
with it, so the transaction handle and all pointers passed to the hook become invalid.
Note: If the Write-Property service hook is registered, the default action for the Write-Property-Multiple service
is no longer writes values directly to the BACstac database, instead it sends Write-Property service requests to
itself. This allows the Write-Property hook to intercept the write requests that comes in the form of Write-PropertyMultiple requests. However, sending a lot of Write-Property requests to itself significantly slows down processing
of the Write-Property-Multiple service. Therefore, it is better to avoid setting the Write-Property hook and use the
Write-Property callback if it is sufficient for the stated goal. Alternatively, you may also register the Write-PropertyMultiple hook and write values directly to the BACstac database (after appropriate validation) without sending
Write-Property requests to itself.

Return Value
HOOK_STATUS_OK

Indicates that the application becomes responsible for processing the service request.
HOOK_STATUS_DEFAULT

Indicates that the hook did not service the request, and that the default BACstac actions should handle the service
request.

Chapter 7. Generating Requests - Raw API
The BACstac libraries provide two techniques for generating requests. The simple API, described in Chapter 14, is
based on the BACstac object database and default actions to hide some of the request complexity from the application.
The raw API, described in this chapter, provides full control over generating a BACnet request.
An application supplies source (for gateway applications) and destination addresses, all request parameters, as well
as storage for reply or error parameters. An application can override the protocol communication settings (APDU
parameters) for a request, such as the Maximum APDU length, support of segmentation, the APDU timeout, etc. In
case of an unconfirmed request, only Maximum APDU length is used.
An application can provide a reply handler, called an Asynchronous Completion Routine (ACR), which is invoked
from an internal BACstac thread when the reply is received or the transaction is terminated for any other reason. If
the ACR is not NULL, the request routine returns immediately, without waiting for the response, and it returns a TSM
handle that can be used by the application to match the response with the request.
Note: Because an ACR is invoked on another thread, it is possible for it to be invoked before the request routine
returns and thus before the TSM handle of the request is received. Thus to use the TSM handle, the application
has to use a synchronizer to ensure that the TSM handle was received. An alternative approach (which does
not require any additional synchronization) is to use any output parameter (such as pError ) to locate the context
associated with the transaction.

BACstacAcknowledgeAlarmEx
Name
BACstacAcknowledgeAlarmEx — sends an acknowledgeAlarm request

Synopsis
BACSTAC_STATUS BACstacAcknowledgeAlarmEx(
const BACSTAC_ADDRESS *pSourceAddress,
const BACSTAC_ADDRESS *pDestinationAddress,
const BACSTAC_ACK_ALARM_INFO *pAckAlarmParams,
BACSTAC_SIMPLE_ACK_ACR_PROC pfACR,
const BACSTAC_APDU_PROPERTIES *pAPDUParams,
BACSTAC_HTSM *phTransaction,
BACSTAC_ERROR *pError);

488

Chapter 7. Generating Requests - Raw API

Arguments
pSourceAddress

A pointer to BACnet address of the request initiator. For Client and Server applications this argument is ignored.
pDestinationAddress

The pointer to the BACnet Address of the acknowledgment destination.
pAckAlarmParams

A pointer to the memory block which contains a number of acknowledgment parameters: a process identifier to
recognize a notification to which this acknowledgment is responding, an event object’s identifier, an event state,
a time stamp to identify the event notification that is acknowledging, the identifier of operator or process that is
acknowledging this event notification, and the time this acknowledgment was issued. This data structure is of
data type BACSTAC_ACK_ALARM_INFO. It is described in the Section called Acknowledge Alarm in Chapter
3.
pfACR

A pointer to the routine which will be called asynchronously to process the response information. If this argument
is NULL, the BACstacAcknowledgeAlarmEx() routine executes synchronously and completes its execution after
the transaction is complete.
pAPDUParams

A pointer to the APDU-Properties structure which sets APDU properties for this transaction. This does not
change global settings for the application APDU Properties. This argument may be NULL; in this case the global
APDU properties are used. The APDU-Properties data type is described in the Section called APDU Properties
in Chapter 2.
phTransaction

The pointer to the Transaction State Machine (TSM) handle which identifies this transaction. In the synchronous
case (if pfACR is NULL) this argument may be NULL, but if provided, the value BACSTAC_INVALID_HANDLE will be returned.
pError

A pointer to a variable to hold BACnet Error information. pError may be NULL.

Description
This routine sends a Acknowledge-Alarm request to the initiating device to acknowledge that the operator has seen
and responded to the event notification that required the acknowledgment. This routine may acknowledge either
Confirmed-Event-Notification or Unconfirmed-Event-Notification requests.
The initiating device is identified by its BACnet address instead of device handle. The routine allows to specify APDU
properties such as the APDU length, support of segmentation, the APDU timeout, etc.
The routine can execute the request asynchronously, i.e. the routine will return immediately without waiting for the
response. To execute the request asynchronously, the ACR of type BACSTAC_SIMPLE_ACK_ACR_PROC should
be provided, which receives the result on completion. If the ACR is not provided (i.e. it is NULL) then the request is
executed synchronously, i.e. the routine does not returns until the transaction is completed.
489

Chapter 7. Generating Requests - Raw API

Return Value
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_STATUS
in Appendix E.

This routine sends a Audit Log Query request, which makes it possible to find and retrieve audit information without
reading and processing a complete audit log.
The queries currently facilitated by the AuditLogQuery service are:
Audit Query By Target - Retrieve the audit records for the specified target device, object, and property. Records are
returned in reverse sequence number order (newest to oldest).
• Audit Query By Source - Retrieve all audited actions initiated by the specified operation source. Records are returned
in the reverse sequence number order (newest to oldest).
•

The destination device is specified by BACnet Address. The routine allows to specify APDU properties such as the
APDU length, support of segmentation, the APDU timeout, etc.

response. To execute the request asynchronously, the ACR of type BACSTAC_SIMPLE_ACK_ACR_PROC should

APDU properties are used. The APDU-Properties data type is described in the Section called APDU Properties
in Chapter 2.

case (if pfACR is NULL) this argument may be NULL, but if provided, the value BACSTAC_INVALID_HANDLE will be returned.

Description
This routine sends a Confirmed-COV-Notification-Multiple request to notify a subscriber about changes that may have
occurred to the properties to one or more properties of one or more objects. The subscriber is identified by its BACnet
address and Process Identifier. The routine allows to specify APDU properties such as the APDU length, support of
segmentation, the APDU timeout, etc.
The routine can execute the request asynchronously, i.e. the routine will return immediately without waiting for the
response. To execute the request asynchronously, the ACR of type BACSTAC_SIMPLE_ACK_ACR_PROC should
be provided, which receives the result on completion. If the ACR is not provided (i.e. it is NULL) then the request is
executed synchronously, i.e. the routine does not returns until the transaction is completed.

in Appendix E.

confirmation reply is expected to indicate that the notification has arrived. The event recipient could later use the
Acknowledge-Alarm service to indicate that the event has been noted by an operator or supervisory program. Only
one recipient can be notified by a single invocation of this service.

Description
This routine sends a Confirmed-Text-Message request to transmit a text to the remote device. Messages may be
prioritized into Normal or Urgent categories. In addition, a text message may be optionally classified by a numeric

identified by its BACnet address instead of device handle. The routine allows to specify APDU properties such as the
APDU length, support of segmentation, the APDU timeout, etc.
The routine can execute the request asynchronously, i.e. the routine will return immediately without waiting for the
response. To execute the request asynchronously, the ACR of type BACSTAC_SIMPLE_ACK_ACR_PROC should

executed synchronously, i.e. the routine does not returns until the transaction is completed.

pDestinationAddress

pfACR

A pointer to the routine which will be called asynchronously to process the response information. If this argument

A pointer to the APDU-Properties structure which sets APDU properties for this transaction. This does not

pSummaryBuffer

A pointer to a memory block into which to place summary information, which is a list of Alarm Summary
items. Each item of data type BACSTAC_ALARM_SUMMARY consists of three parameters: the Object ID of
the appropriate object, the Event-state of this object, and Acked-Transitions property values. The BACSTAC_ALARM_SUMMARY data structure is described in the Section called Get Alarm Summary in Chapter 3. This

Description
This routine sends a Get-Alarm-Summary request to obtain a summary of "event-active" objects within the given
device that are capable of alarm processing. The "event-active" objects are objects that have any value but STATE_NORMAL for the Event_State property and NOTIFY_TYPE_ALARM for the Notify_Type property. The destination
device is identified by its BACnet address instead of device handle. The routine allows to specify APDU properties
such as the APDU length, support of segmentation, the APDU timeout, etc.
The routine can execute the request asynchronously, i.e. the routine will return immediately without waiting for the
response. To execute the request asynchronously, the ACR of type BACSTAC_ALARM_SUMM_ACR_PROC should
be provided, which receives the result on completion. If the ACR is not provided (i.e. it is NULL) then the request is
executed synchronously, i.e. the routine does not returns until the transaction is completed.
Note: Support for the execution of this service is recommended to not be implemented in devices supporting
Protocol Revision 16 or later.

Return Value
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_STATUS
in Appendix E.

pAPDUParams

A pointer to the APDU-Properties structure which sets APDU properties for this transaction. This does not
change global settings for the application APDU Properties. This argument may be NULL; in this case the global
APDU properties are used. The APDU-Properties data type is described in the Section called APDU Properties
in Chapter 2.
phTransaction

The pointer to the Transaction State Machine (TSM) handle which identifies this transaction. In the synchronous
case (if pfACR is NULL) this argument may be NULL, but if provided, the value BACSTAC_INVALID_HANDLE will be returned.
pInfoBuffer

A pointer to a memory block of data type BACSTAC_EVENT_INFO to place the response information. It contains a list of Event Summary items. Each item of data type BACSTAC_EVENT_SUMMARY consists of a
number of parameters that describe the appropriate object. ObjectID, Event-State, Acked-Transitions, NotifyType, and Event-Enable parameters convey values of the corresponding properties of the object. Event-Stamps
parameter conveys the timestamps of the last event notifications for TO-OFFNORMAL, TO-FAULT, and TONORMAL events. Event-Priorities parameter conveys the priorities specified in the Priority property of the associated notification class object. Event Info data structure contains actual number of the items returned, and the
total length of Event-Summary list buffer expressed as a number of items this buffer can hold. The last parameter
of BACSTAC_EVENT_INFO data structure is More Events flag which indicates whether (BACSTAC_TRUE)
or not (BACSTAC_FALSE) more objects exist that should be listed, but that cannot be conveyed by the reply because APDU is too short. The BACSTAC_EVENT_SUMMARY and BACSTAC_EVENT_INFO data structures
are described in the Section called Get Event Information in Chapter 3.
pError

A pointer to a variable to hold BACnet Error information. pError may be NULL.
iAlloc

A pointer to an allocator interface. This parameter may be NULL then the buffer located inside of pInfoBuffer
(pInfoBuffer->pSummaries) will be used to store the result. If the allocator interface is provided then the buffer
will be allocated and should be freed later using the BACstacFreeEventInfoAck() routine.

Description
This routine sends a Get-Event-Information request to obtain a summary of "event-active" objects within the given
device that generates event notifications. The "event-active" objects are objects that have any value other than STATE_NORMAL for the Event_State property, or have an acked-transitions property that has at least one of the bits
(TO_OFFNORMAL, TO_FAULT, TO_NORMAL) set to BACSTAC_FALSE. The destination device is identified
by its BACnet address instead of device handle. The routine allows to specify APDU properties such as the APDU
length, support of segmentation, the APDU timeout, etc.
The routine can execute the request asynchronously, i.e. the routine will return immediately without waiting for the
response. To execute the request asynchronously, the ACR of type BACSTAC_EVENT_INFO_ACR_PROC should
be provided, which receives the result on completion. If the ACR is not provided (i.e. it is NULL) then the request is
executed synchronously, i.e. the routine does not returns until the transaction is completed.

514

Chapter 7. Generating Requests - Raw API

Return Value
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_STATUS
in Appendix E.

pDestinationAddress

A pointer to the BACnet Address of the request destination.

Instance Number and the values of three Device Object Properties (max APDU length, segmentation supported,
and vendor identifier). BACSTAC_I_AM_INFO data type is described in the Section called I-Am in Chapter 3.
pAPDUParams

A pointer to the APDU-Properties structure which sets APDU properties for this transaction. This does not
change global settings for the application APDU Properties. This argument may be NULL; in this case the global
APDU properties are used. The APDU-Properties data type is described in the Section called APDU Properties
in Chapter 2.

515

Chapter 7. Generating Requests - Raw API

Description
This routine sends a BACnet I-Am message to the given BACnet address, which may be broadcast or unicast. If
the I-Am is broadcast, this broadcast may be on the local network only, a remote network only, or globally on all
networks at the discretion of the application. In general, sending global broadcasts should be avoided, especially in
large installations or when the I-Am is being sent in response to a Who-Is request. In the latter case, I-Am shall be
sent in such a manner that the device that sent the Who-Is will receive the resulting I-Am.

Return Value
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_STATUS
in Appendix E.

This routine sends a Atomic-Read-File request to read the contents of the specified file beginning from the specified position. The file may be accessed as records or as a stream of octets that is defined by the contents of
File_Access_Method property of the File object. The destination device is identified by its BACnet address instead of
device handle. The routine allows to specify APDU properties such as the APDU length, support of segmentation, the
APDU timeout, etc.
The routine can execute the request asynchronously, i.e. the routine will return immediately without waiting for the
response. To execute the request asynchronously, the ACR of type BACSTAC_READ_FILE_ACR_PROC should be

executed synchronously, i.e. the routine does not returns until the transaction is completed.

Properties to read. BACSTAC_READ_CON_INFO data type is described in the Section called Read Property
Conditional in Chapter 3.
pfACR

A pointer to the routine which will be called asynchronously to process the response information. If this argument is NULL, the BACstacReadPropertyConditionalEx2() routine executes synchronously and completes its
execution after the transaction is complete.

Chapter 7. Generating Requests - Raw API

A pointer to a buffer to place the Result data if successful reading (data type BACSTAC_RPC_RESULT). This
data structure is described in the Section called Read Property Conditional in Chapter 3.

Description
This routine sends a Read-Property-Conditional request to read the object identifiers and values of zero or more specified properties of all objects that meet a list of selection criteria (conditions). The conditions are Boolean expressions
of the form (Property.Conditional_Operator.Constant). In addition, a list of conditions may be logically OR’ed or
AND’ed to determine whether a particular Object shall be included in the set of objects whose properties are to be
read. The destination device is identified by its BACnet address instead of device handle. The routine allows to specify
APDU properties such as the APDU length, support of segmentation, the APDU timeout, etc.
The routine can execute the request asynchronously, i.e. the routine will return immediately without waiting for
the response. To execute the request asynchronously, the ACR of type BACSTAC_READ_PROP_CON_ACR_PROC
should be provided, which receives the result on completion. If the ACR is not provided (i.e. it is NULL) then the
request is executed synchronously, i.e. the routine does not returns until the transaction is completed.
Note: This service has been removed in Protocol Revision 12, because the lack of its support by nearly all BACnet
devices.

Return Value
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_STATUS
in Appendix E.

This routine sends a Read-Property request to read the value of a property of an object. The destination device is

response. To execute the request asynchronously, the ACR of type BACSTAC_READ_PROP_ACR_PROC should be
provided, which receives the result on completion. If the ACR is not provided (i.e. it is NULL) then the request is
executed synchronously, i.e. the routine does not returns until the transaction is completed.
Note: In case of an asynchronous request (i.e. pfACR is not NULL), the variable pointed by pReadInfo should
remain alive and not modified until the completion routine is invoked.

in Appendix E.

specify APDU properties such as the APDU length, support of segmentation, the APDU timeout, etc.

APDU properties are used. The APDU-Properties data type is described in the Section called APDU Properties
in Chapter 2.

This routine sends a BACnet UTC-Time-Synchronization request to the specified BACnet address, which may be
broadcast or unicast. The routine allows to notify remote devices about the correct current time, so they can synchronize their internal clocks. This routine is for Gateway applications only. See BACstacUTCTimeSynchronization for
Client and Server applications.

Name

Synopsis

const BACSTAC_ADDRESS *pSourceAddress,

553

Chapter 7. Generating Requests - Raw API
const BACSTAC_ADDRESS *pDestinationAddress,

BACSTAC_WRITE_FILE_ACR_PROC pfACR,
const BACSTAC_APDU_PROPERTIES *pAPDUParams,
BACSTAC_HTSM *phTransaction,
BACSTAC_WRITE_FILE_RESULT *pResult,
BACSTAC_ERROR *pError);

Arguments
pSourceAddress

A pointer to BACnet address of the request initiator. For Client and Server applications this argument shall be
ignored.
pDestinationAddress

A pointer to the BACnet Address of the request destination.
pWriteInfo

A pointer to the service request information data structure. This data structure contains the objectID, File
Access Type (FILE_ACCESS_STREAM or FILE_ACCESS_RECORDS) and Write File Data information.
BACSTAC_WRITE_FILE_INFO data type is described in the Section called Write File in Chapter 3.
pfACR

A pointer to the routine which will be called asynchronously to process the response information. If this argument is NULL, the BACstacWriteFileEx() routine executes synchronously and completes its execution after the
transaction is complete.
pAPDUParams

A pointer to the APDU-Properties structure which sets APDU properties for this transaction. This does not
change global settings for the application APDU Properties. This argument may be NULL; in this case the global
APDU properties are used. The APDU-Properties data type is described in the Section called APDU Properties
in Chapter 2.
phTransaction

The pointer to the Transaction State Machine (TSM) handle which identifies this transaction. In the synchronous
case (if pfACR is NULL) this argument may be NULL, but if provided, the value BACSTAC_INVALID_HANDLE will be returned.
pResult

A pointer to a buffer to place the response data if successful writing (data type BACSTAC_WRITE_FILE_RESULT). This data structure is described in the Section called Write File in Chapter 3.
pError

A pointer to a variable to hold BACnet Error information. pError may be NULL.

554

Chapter 7. Generating Requests - Raw API

Description
This routine sends an Atomic-Write-File request to write an octet string into a specified position or a list of octet
strings into a specified group of records in a file. The file may be accessed as records or as a stream of octets. Choice
is defined by the value of File_Access_Method property of the File object. The destination device is identified by its
BACnet address instead of device handle. The routine allows to specify APDU properties such as the APDU length,
support of segmentation, the APDU timeout, etc.
The routine can execute the request asynchronously, i.e. the routine will return immediately without waiting for the
response. To execute the request asynchronously, the ACR of type BACSTAC_WRITE_FILE_ACR_PROC should be
provided, which receives the result on completion. If the ACR is not provided (i.e. it is NULL) then the request is
executed synchronously, i.e. the routine does not returns until the transaction is completed.

Return Value
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_STATUS
in Appendix E.

Name
BACstacWriteGroupEx —

Synopsis

const BACSTAC_ADDRESS *pDestinationAddress,
const BACSTAC_WRITE_GROUP_INFO *pWGInfo,
const BACSTAC_APDU_PROPERTIES *pAPDUParams);

Arguments
pSourceAddress

A pointer to BACnet address of the request initiator. For Client and Server applications this argument shall be
ignored.
pDestinationAddress

The pointer to the BACnet Address of the request destination.
555

Chapter 7. Generating Requests - Raw API
pWGInfo

A pointer to the service information data structure. The BACSTAC_WRITE_GROUP_INFO data type is described in the Section called Write Group in Chapter 3.
pAPDUParams

A pointer to the APDU-Properties structure which sets APDU properties for this transaction. This does not
change global defaults for the application APDU Properties. This argument may be NULL; in this case the global
APDU properties are used. The APDU-Properties data type is described in the Section called APDU Properties
in Chapter 2.

Description
The WriteGroup service is used by a sending BACnet-user to update arbitrary Channel objects’ Present_Value properties for a particular numbered control group. The WriteGroup service is an unconfirmed service. Upon receipt of
a WriteGroup service request, all devices that are members of the specified control group shall write to their corresponding Channel objects’ Present_Value properties with the value applicable to the Channel Number, if any. A
device shall be considered to be a member of a control group if that device has one or more Channel objects for which
the ’Group Number’ from the service appears in its Control_Groups property. If the receiving device does not contain
one or more Channel objects with matching channel numbers, then those values shall be ignored.

Return Value
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_STATUS
in Appendix E.

Synopsis
void (*BACSTAC_EVENT_INFO_ACR_PROC)(

Arguments

pSourceAddress
pDestinationAddress

Pointers to the BACnet Addresses of request initiator and request destination.
status

Return-Value information that the transaction conveys to the request initiator.
pInfoBuffer

A pointer to a memory block of data type BACSTAC_EVENT_INFO is to place the response information. It
contains a list of Event Summary items. Each item of data type BACSTAC_EVENT_SUMMARY consists of
a number of parameters that describe the appropriate object. ObjectID, Event-State, Acked-Transitions, NotifyType, and Event-Enable parameters convey values of the corresponding properties of the object. Event-Stamps
parameter conveys the timestamps of the last event notifications for TO-OFFNORMAL, TO-FAULT, and TONORMAL events. Event-Priorities parameter conveys the priorities specified in the Priority property of the associated notification class object. Event Info data structure contains actual number of the items returned, and the
total length of Event-Summary list buffer expressed as a number of items this buffer can hold. The last parameter
of BACSTAC_EVENT_INFO data structure is More Events flag which indicates whether (BACSTAC_TRUE)
or not (BACSTAC_FALSE) more objects exist that should be listed, but that cannot be conveyed by the reply because APDU is too short. The BACSTAC_EVENT_SUMMARY and BACSTAC_EVENT_INFO data structures
are described in the Section called Get Event Information in Chapter 3.
pError

A pointer to a variable to hold the additional BACnet Error information, if the value of the status argument is
BACSTAC_ERROR. pError is NULL if NULL was passed to BACstacGetEventInfoEx2(). See also Appendix
E.

Chapter 8. Object Database - Device
The BACstac object database can be used by an application to store information about BACnet devices, objects and
properties.
Server and gateway applications can store the values of all the properties in their objects. The BACstac default actions
can then respond to many types of BACnet requests by using the values in the BACstac object database. The devices
in a server or gateway database can be loaded from a template created at the time of application compilation. Objects
may also be added and deleted dynamically.
Client applications can maintain local images of remote devices and objects. The main use for these images is to cache
device ID, address and APDU parameters of remote devices. The BACstac default action for the I-Am service will
automatically create device images using the information from the I-Am. This information is then used automatically
when generating requests to the remote device using the "simple" API.

BACstacChangeCovSubs
Name
BACstacChangeCovSubs — Add or remove a subscription from the local device

Synopsis
BACSTAC_STATUS BACstacChangeCovSubs(
BACSTAC_HDEVICE hDevice,
const BACSTAC_SUBSCRIBE_COVP_INFO *pSubscriber,
const BACSTAC_ADDRESS *pRecipient);

Arguments
hDevice

The handle of the Device. In a server application, this argument can be BACSTAC_INVALID_HANDLE.
pSubscriber

a pointer to Subscribe Change-Of-Value Property Information, which specifies what subscription should be added
or deleted.
pRecipient

A pointer to BACnet address of the subscribing device.

582

Chapter 8. Object Database - Device

Description
Add or remove a subscription of some another device to this local device. This function can be used only when the
default action for COV notification is enabled, that is the value of the Active-COV-Subscriptions property is AUTO.
Note: covIncrement must be a normal value (i.e. not NaN or infinity). Before BACstac 6.4, if a negative value
of the COV increment was given then its absolute value was used in all comparisons. Starting with BACstac 6.4,
negative values of the COV increment are prohibited.

Return Value
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_STATUS
in Appendix E.

Name

BACSTAC_HDEVICE *deviceHandle);

Arguments

A pointer to the Address of the Device.
instNumber

585

Chapter 8. Object Database - Device
deviceHandle

A pointer to a variable into which to place the new Device handle.

Description
Creates a new device image and adds it to the BACstac Object Database, which for a client application contains images
of a remote devices. The main purpose of this routine is to create images of BACnet devices that do not support the
I-Am service, such as, for example, MS/TP subordinate devices.
Devices images created by this routine are similar to created by the default action for the I-Am message.
The Device is identified by its Device Object instance number. This routine does not verify that the Device actually
exists at the specified Address. If the Device image is successfully created or it has already existed (BACSTAC_STATUS_ALREADY_EXISTS), the Device handle is passed back to the application in the variable pointed to by phDevice. If the device existed, none of its attribute is changed. When a new device is created with the address used by
another device, the old device will mark as unreachable, i.e. having no known BACnet address.

Return Value
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_STATUS
in Appendix E.

Removes a Device from the internal Device image list. The Device is identified by a Device handle. A Device image
contains all the discovered information about a Device, including the Device Object and Object list.

Return Value
The routine returns BACSTAC_TRUE if the Device image was successfully deleted.

587

Chapter 8. Object Database - Device

BACstacDeleteDeviceImages
Name
BACstacDeleteDeviceImages — delete device images accordingly to filter

Synopsis
BACSTAC_DEVICE_COUNT BACstacDeleteDeviceImages(
BACSTAC_DEVICE_IMG_FILTER filter,
BACSTAC_INST_NUMBER filterMin,
BACSTAC_INST_NUMBER filterMax,
const BACSTAC_ADDRESS *address);

Arguments
filter

The filter parameter specifies what devices should be deleted. It can take one of three values: BDIF_ALL - all devices, BDIF_AUTO -- automatically created by the default action of BACstac, or BDIF_MANUAL -explicitly created by BACstacCreateDeviceImage.
filterMin
filterMax

Instance number filter arguments that limit the range of deleted to the specified range of instance numbers. If both
arguments are set to BACSTAC_NO_FILTER then no filtering based on device instance numbers is performed.
address

An optional address that serves as additional restriction on what devices should be deleted from the internal
device list. It can be set to a broadcast address to limit to delete all devices from the specified network. If this
parameter is NULL then no filtering is performed based on the device address.

Description
Removes device from the internal device image list. The filter parameter specifies what devices should be deleted. All
objects associated with deleted devices will be also destroyed, so their handles will become invalid and should not be
used.

Return Value
The routine returns the number of deleted devices.

588

BACstacGetDeviceAPDUProperties
Name
BACstacGetDeviceAPDUProperties — obtains APDU properties for a remote device

Synopsis
BACSTAC_BOOLEAN BACstacGetDeviceAPDUProperties(
BACSTAC_HDEVICE hDevice,
BACSTAC_APDU_PROPERTIES *pAPDUProps);

Arguments
hDevice

The Device handle of the remote device
pAPDUProps

A pointer to the APDU Properties Data structure in which to place the values of APDU Properties. This data
structure is described in the Section called APDU Properties in Chapter 2.

Description
The function obtains the APDU properties for the given remote device. All fields in the BACSTAC_APDU_PROPERTIES structure are set to the currently used values as they are used by BACstac to send requests to this
device, but only those fields that have their bits set to non-zero in the APDU mask, are considered "fixed". The "fixed"

593

Chapter 8. Object Database - Device
values are not changed over time and can be only modified by BACstacSetDeviceAPDUProperties(). The rest of
APDU properties are detected automatically based on default APDU values and values of properties learned from
I-Am, ReadProperty and other requests.

Return Value
The routine returns BACSTAC_TRUE on success.

BACstacGetDeviceList
Name
BACstacGetDeviceList — obtains the current list of remote device images

Synopsis
BACSTAC_BOOLEAN BACstacGetDeviceList(
BACSTAC_HDEVICE *phDevices,
BACSTAC_DEVICE_COUNT hDevicesCount,
BACSTAC_DEVICE_COUNT *phDevicesAvailable);

Arguments
phDevice

A pointer to a buffer into which to copy the list of Device handles.
hDevicesCount

The size of the buffer expressed as a number of Device handles.
phDevicesAvailable

A pointer to a variable which is set to the actual number Device handles available to be copied into the buffer.
The actually number copied is MIN(Count, Available). If both phDevices == NULL and hDevicesCount == 0,
the number of Device handles available will be returned without copying any Device handles.

Description
Returns a list of Devices that are in the internal Device image list. A device image is added to the BACstac Object
Database, which contains a cache of remote devices, when the application receive an I-Am broadcast from that device.
The I-Am message can be generated by device on their own initialtive or can be sent in response to a Who-Is message
issued by this client or another BACnet device attached to this BACnet network. Alternatively, a device can also be
created by the BACstacCreateDeviceImage() routine.
Note: When an I-Am message is received from a new device (i.e. a new instance number), but this device has the
same address of one existing device, then the old existing device will be marked as unreachable, i.e. without any valid
address; and it will stay in this state unless I-Am from this device or the device is removed manually.

595

Chapter 8. Object Database - Device

Return Value
The routine returns BACSTAC_TRUE if the list of Devices was successfully copied.

BACstacSetDCCValue
Name
BACstacSetDCCValue — sets the DCC status

Synopsis
BACSTAC_BOOLEAN BACstacSetDCCValue(
BACSTAC_HDEVICE hDevice,
BACSTAC_DCC_VALUE value);

Arguments
hDevice

Handle of the device. In the Server case this argument will be ignored.
pValue

The value of the DCC-Value to be set.

Description
Sets a value of the Device Communication Control Value (DCC-Value). This value indicates whether or not a device
is able to initiate and respond to APDUs on the communication internetwork, depending on whether the DCC-Value
is DCC_ENABLE, DCC_DISABLE, or DCC_DISABLE_INITIATION. This routine instructs the Server or Gateway
application to either disable or enable initiating and responding APDUs. The default value of DCC-Value is DCC_ENABLE. This routine sets the DCC-Value in one Server/Gateway application.

Return Value
The routine returns BACSTAC_TRUE if DCC-Value was successfully copied.

Arguments

A pointer to an address of the device.
pValue

The value of the DCC-Value to be set.

Description
Sets a value of the Device Communication Control Value (DCC-Value). This value indicates whether or not a device
is able to initiate and respond to APDUs on the communication internetwork, depending on whether the DCC-Value is
DCC_ENABLE, DCC_DISABLE, or DCC_DISABLE_INITIATION. This routine determines the device by its BACstac address. This routine instructs a Gateway application to either disable or enable initiating and responding APDUs.
The default value of DCC-Value is DCC_ENABLE. This routine sets the DCC-Value in a Gateway application.

Return Value
The routine returns BACSTAC_TRUE if DCC-Value was successfully copied.

BACstacSetDeviceAPDUProperties
Name
BACstacSetDeviceAPDUProperties — sets APDU properties for a remote device

Synopsis
BACSTAC_BOOLEAN BACstacSetDeviceAPDUProperties(
BACSTAC_HDEVICE hDevice,
const BACSTAC_APDU_PROPERTIES *pAPDUProps);

Arguments
hDevice

The Device handle of the remote device
pAPDUProps

A pointer to the APDU Properties Data structure which contains the values of the APDU Properties to be set as
the default values. This data structure is described in the Section called APDU Properties in Chapter 2.

Description
The function the APDU properties to be used in client requests directed to the given device.
Initially APDU properties for a newly created device are set accordingly to the default APDU properties, and then
modified by BACstac automatically based on property values received in I-Am and other requests.
BACstacSetDeviceAPDUProperties sets the specified APDU properties (those that have non-zero bit in their mask)
to the given value and makes them "fixed", so BACstac no longer changes them automatically.
Note: Raw API functions (which uses device addresses instead of handles) do not use these APDU properties, but
only the default APDU properties if others are not provided explicitly by the corresponding parameter of the function.

Return Value
The routine returns BACSTAC_TRUE on success.

Writes the current values of Max-APDU-Length, Segmentation-Supported, Max-Segments-Accepted, APDUSegment-Timeout, APDU-Timeout and Number-Of-APDU-Retries into the corresponding properties of the device
object for the device referenced by the handle. It may be used in server and gateway applications.

Return Value
The routine returns BACSTAC_TRUE if the device properties were successfully written.

602

Chapter 9. Object Database - Objects
The BACstac object database can be used by an application to store information about BACnet devices, objects and
properties.
BACstac server/gateway applications can dynamically create and delete local objects. The objects consist of lists of
property values which can be used by the BACstac default actions to satisfy requests.
BACstac client applications can create and delete local images of objects in remote devices.
This information is then used automatically when generating requests to the remote device using the "simple" API.

BACstacCreateDBObject
Name
BACstacCreateDBObject — creates an object in a local device

Synopsis
BACSTAC_STATUS BACstacCreateDBObject(
BACSTAC_HDEVICE hDevice,
const BACSTAC_DB_OBJECT *pDBObj,
BACSTAC_HOBJECT *pObjectHandle,
BACSTAC_PROPERTY_COUNT *firstFailed);

Arguments
hDevice

The handle of the device in which a new object should be created. In a server application, this argument can be
BACSTAC_INVALID_HANDLE.
pDBObj

A pointer to the object description, which contains the property list with their initial values, and additional flags
determining default actions for each property. First two properties in the list must be object-identifier and objectname. It is recommended that the third property in the list should be object-type, but this is not enforced now.
Values of object-identifier and object-name properties must be unique inside of each device.
pObjectHandle

A pointer to a variable that, on success, will contain the handle of the newly created object.

603

Chapter 9. Object Database - Objects
firstFailed

A pointer to a variable that in the case of failure will contain the index of the property in the object description
that caused failure. The index starts with one, and zero is used to denote that the error is unrelated to any property.

Description
Creates an object in the local database. A list of properties to be contained in the device must be provided. The handle
of the new Object is returned. The maximum number of objects that can be contained in a Device is specified when
the Device is created (by BACstacServerInit() or BACstacCreateDevice() in gateway applications).

Return Value
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_STATUS
in Appendix E.

Name

The handle of the Device containing the Object.
pObjectID

The Object Identifier of the Object.

604

Chapter 9. Object Database - Objects
phObject

A pointer to a variable into which to place the Object handle.

Description
Creates a local image of an Object including a description of a number of its Properties. A handle to the Object is
returned to the application, if the Object image is successfully created or already exists. The Object is identified by an
Object Identifier and Device handle.

Return Value
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_STATUS
in Appendix E.

filters, either Object Name or Object Id specification, and a tag to choose. BACSTAC_WHO_HAS_HOOK_INFO data type is described in the Section called Who-Has in Chapter 3.
pObjectsAvailable

A pointer to a variable, to be set to the actual number of Object handles that were available to be copied into
the buffer. The number copied into the buffer is MIN(Count, Available). If both objectListBuffer == NULL and
objectListBufferCount == 0, the number of Object handles (names, identifiers) available will be returned without
copying any Object attributes.

Gets a list of the Object handles of objects of local devices which have a given object name, or a given Object Identifier.

The routine returns BACSTAC_TRUE if the Object List is successfully copied.

Chapter 10. Object Database - Property
The BACstac object database can be used by an application to store information about BACnet devices, objects and
properties.
BACstac server/gateway applications can set the values of properties in local objects in the BACstac object database.
Applications can also set flags to modify the BACstac default actions (such as callbacks, read/write permission) for
each property.
BACstac client applications can specify a set of properties in local images of objects in remote devices to be cached
(using the ReadMode flag).

hDevice

changeListInfo

elements to be added to the property. The BACSTAC_CHANGE_LIST_INFO data structure is described in the
Section called Add/Remove List Element in Chapter 3.
pError

A pointer to a variable to hold BACnet Error information. pError may be NULL.

621

A pointer to the sequence number of the first element in the pElements list which cannot be added to the list.
pFirstFailed may be NULL.
flags

This parameter can contain one of the following flags:
BACSTAC_FORCE_FLAG
The property should be written even if the property is non-writable or even invisible from the network.
BACSTAC_INVOKE_CB_FLAG
The write callback should be invoked as it is usually done by the default action.

Description
Adds one or more list elements to a local property, which is a list. If one or more of the new elements are already
present in the list property, they will be ignored: duplicates of the elements will not be added to the list. If an element
cannot be added to the list by this routine for some other reason, an error is returned, along with the sequence number
of the element.
This routine is similarity BACstacAddElement(), but it also returns a BACnet error, which makes it more suitable for
BACnet service hooks.

Return Value
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_STATUS
in Appendix E.

list properties can be attached to the list-change callback.

in Appendix E.

Arguments
hDevice
