pReadAccessSpec

A pointer to the BACSTAC_READ_ACCESS_SPEC data structure, which specifies the object and properties.
This data structure is described in the Section called Read Property Multiple in Chapter 3.
pReadAccessResult

A pointer to the memory block to place a BACSTAC_READ_RAW_RESULT_LIST data structure which indicates success or failure of the reading of each specified Property. In the case of successful access to a single
Property, its value shall be returned within this argument, and in the case of access failure this argument shall
convey the Property Access Error information. The BACSTAC_READ_RAW_RESULT_LIST data structure is
described in a the Section called Read Property Multiple in Chapter 3.
iAlloc

A pointer to an allocator interface. This parameter may be NULL then pReadAccessResult must contain an array
of BACSTAC_READ_RESULT_ITEM with properly initialized buffer inside of each property contents. If the
allocator interface is not NULL the array of BACSTAC_READ_RESULT_ITEM and the buffer for each element
is allocated dynamically using this interface. The allocated memory should be freed using the BACstacFreeRPMRawResultList() routine.
flags

This parameter can contain one of the following flags:
BACSTAC_FORCE_FLAG
The property should be read even if the property is internal and should not be visible from the network.
BACSTAC_INVOKE_CB_FLAG
The write callback should be invoked as it is usually done by the default action.

Description
This routine obtains the values of specified properties stored in the BACstac database. The special property identifiers:
PROP_ALL, PROP_REQUIRED, PROP_OPTIONAL may be used to obtain all, required, or optional properties
correspondingly.

626

Chapter 10. Object Database - Property

Return Value
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_STATUS
in Appendix E.
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. Possible return codes are the following:
BACSTAC_STATUS_OK
The operation has been successful.
BACSTAC_STATUS_NOT_INITIALIZED
BACstac was not previously initialized.
BACSTAC_STATUS_SERVICE_NOT_FOUND
BACstac service has been stopped or restarted.
BACSTAC_STATUS_INVALID_DEVICE_HANDLE
Invalid device handle.
BACSTAC_STATUS_INVALID_PARAM
One or more parameters were incorrect.
BACSTAC_STATUS_DATATYPE_MISALIGNMENT
One of the given buffer is not properly alignment.
BACSTAC_STATUS_OUT_OF_MEMORY
The operation cannot be performed due to lack of memory.
BACSTAC_STATUS_UNKNOWN_ERROR
An unexpected error has occurred. This may be due to implementation defect in BACstac or improper work of
the program, which caused to memory corruption.

BACstacReadRangeLocal
Name
BACstacReadRangeLocal — reads a range of the list from a property in the BACstac database

Synopsis
BACSTAC_STATUS BACstacReadRangeLocal(
BACSTAC_HDEVICE hDevice,
const BACSTAC_READ_RANGE_INFO *readRangeInfo,
BACSTAC_PROPERTY_CONTENTS *pValue,
BACSTAC_BIT_STRING *pResultFlags,
BACSTAC_ERROR_TYPE *pError,
BACSTAC_IALLOC *iAlloc,
BACSTAC_UINT flags);

Arguments
hDevice

The handle of the Device containing the Object. In a server application, this argument can be BACSTAC_INVALID_HANDLE.
readRangeInfo

A pointer to the BACSTAC_READ_RANGE_INFO data structure. The fields of this data structure include object
and property identifiers, array index if the property is an array of lists (BACSTAC_VOID_INDEX if not), a
Range-Type tag and Range bounds. The Range-Type tag shall be BACSTAC_RANGE_NONE or BACSTAC_RANGE_BY_POSITION. The Read-Range-Info data structure is described in the Section called Read Range in
Chapter 3.
objectID
ePropertyID

The Object and Property Identifier of the local property.

629

Chapter 10. Object Database - Property
nIndex

If the property is an array of lists then the array index specifies the element of the array on which the operation
should be performed. If the property is not an array, the index value BACSTAC_VOID_INDEX should be used.
The array index of the first element in BACnet arrays is 1.
position

The index of the first (if ’count’ is positive) or last (if ’count’ is negative) element in the list to be read. The index
of the first element in a list is 1.
count

The absolute value of the ’count’ parameter specifies the number of records to be read. If ’count’ is positive, the
record specified by ’position’ shall be the first record read and returned; if ’count’ is negative the record specified
by ’position’ shall be the last record. ’count’ may not be zero.
pValue

Pointer to a Property Contents containing a buffer into which selected elements are copied. If the provided buffer
is insufficient to hold all elements then as many elements as possible that satisfy the selection criteria will be
copied into the buffer. Upon successful completion the routine, the buffer always contains at least one element
pointed by the position. The number of elements does not exceed the number the absolute value of the ’count’
parameter. The number of elements may be less than the requested by the ’count’ parameter if either the list has
less elements or the output buffer is not sufficient to hold all selected elements.
pResultFlags

A pointer to a bit string to place three flags that describe characteristics of the result data. Those flags are:
BACSTAC_FIRST_ITEM
The result includes the first list or array element.
BACSTAC_LAST_ITEM
The result includes the last list or array element.
BACSTAC_MORE_ITEMS
The result does not include all elements that satisfy the selection criteria. This happens if the buffer is not
sufficient to hold all elements.
pError

A pointer to a variable to hold BACnet Error information. pError may be NULL.
iAlloc

A pointer to an allocator interface. This parameter may be NULL then the buffer pointed by the ’pValue’ parameter will be used to receive the result. If the allocator interface is provided then the buffer will be allocated and
should be freed later using the BACstacFreeContents() routine.

630

Chapter 10. Object Database - Property
flags

This parameter can contain one of the following flags:
BACSTAC_FORCE_FLAG
The property should be read even if the property is internal and should not be visible from the network.

Description
This routine extracts a range of list elements from a local property stored in the BACstac database. The property must
be a list or an array of lists.
This routine is similar BACstacRetrieveListItems(), but it also returns a BACnet error, which makes it more suitable
for BACnet service hooks.
Depending on whether BACSTAC_USE_64_BIT_READ_RANGE is defined, BACstacReadRangeLocal() can be
either an alias to BACstacReadRange64Local(), which accepts BACSTAC_READ_RANGE_64_INFO, or BACstacReadRange32Local(), which accepts BACSTAC_READ_RANGE_32_INFO.

Return Value
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. Possible return codes are the following:
BACSTAC_STATUS_OK
Upon successful completion.
BACSTAC_STATUS_INVALID_PARAM
One or more parameters functions were incorrect. For example, the pValue parameter was null, or iAlloc was
NULL and the buffer was not properly initialized to hold returned elements, or the position or count parameter
was zero.
BACSTAC_STATUS_UNKNOWN_OBJECT
The specified object does not exist.
BACSTAC_STATUS_UNKNOWN_PROPERTY
The specified property does not exist in the object.
BACSTAC_STATUS_NOT_A_LIST
The specified property was neither a list nor an array of lists.
BACSTAC_STATUS_NOT_AN_ARRAY
A non-void array index was given for the property that is not an array of lists.
BACSTAC_STATUS_INVALID_ARRAY_INDEX
Invalid array index was given for the property that is an array of lists. (i.e. the index is zero or larger than the last
element of the array).

631

Chapter 10. Object Database - Property
BACSTAC_STATUS_VAL_OUT_OF_RANGE
The position parameter was larger than the BACSTAC_ELEMENT_COUNT_MAX constant.
BACSTAC_STATUS_OUT_OF_MEMORY
The operation cannot be performed due to lack of memory.
BACSTAC_STATUS_VAL_OUT_OF_SPACE
The given buffer (from the Property Contents) does not have enough space for the element pointed by the position
parameter.
BACSTAC_STATUS_UNKNOWN_ERROR
An unexpected error has occurred. This may be due to implementation defect in BACstac or improper work of
the program, which caused to memory corruption.

The Object and Property Identifier of the local Property.
nIndex

The index of an array item. If the Property is not an array, the index value BACSTAC_VOID_INDEX should
be used. If the Property is an array, the index value BACSTAC_ENTIRE_ARRAY can be used to read the
entire array. If the Property is an array, the index value BACSTAC_ARRAY_COUNT will return the number of
elements in the array. The indices of BACnet arrays start counting at 1.

Pointer to a Property Contents containing a buffer into which to copy the value. Upon successful completion of
this routine, the Property Contents tag attribute indicates the type of the Property.

parameter will be used to receive the result. If the allocator interface is provided then the buffer will be allocated
and should be freed later using the BACstacFreeContents() routine.

Description
This routine extracts the value stored in the BACstac database for the given property.
This routine carries some similarity with BACstacReadProperty2(), but it significantly differ in the way it performs
the operation and may give the different result. While BACstacRetrievePropertyInstance2() extracts the value for the
given property from the BACstac database, BACstacReadProperty2() will send a Request-Property request. This is the
main reason why BACstacRetrievePropertyInstance2() can be used in any hook while use of BACstacReadProperty2()
in any hook except the Read-Property-Multiple to read a property from its own database can cause a dead-lock. Also
BACstacRetrievePropertyInstance2() is significantly faster than BACstacReadProperty2() when it comes to reading
from its own database and requires much less resources to perform.

Return Value
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_STATUS
in Appendix E.

The size of the buffer that receives the ASN.1 value.

A pointer to the variable that will contain the actual length of the received ASN.1 value.

638

Chapter 10. Object Database - Property

Description
This routine extracts the ASN.1 value stored in the BACstac database for the given property.
This routine is similar to BACstacRetrievePropertyInstance2() except that it returns the value in ASN.1 format. Most
properties are stored in the BACstac database in the ASN.1 format, so this routine copies the database value to the
supplied buffer. A few properties (usually those that are marked as AUTO in TPI) can use a different format to store
information, this function encodes the current property value to the supplied buffer. The main use of this function is
store property values on some permanent storage to preserve them over restart.

Return Value
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_STATUS
in Appendix E.

Arguments
eType

The type of callback, which may be CB_READ, CB_WRITE, or CB_CHANGE_LIST. If the given property
is commandable then CB_WRITE attaches this property to both write and write-commandable callback. The
write-commandable callback is invoked first, and the write callback is invoked only if the write-commandable
callback returned CALLBACK_STATUS_DEFAULT.

Specifies whether a callback of the given type should be attached to a Property. Callbacks are called by the BACstac default actions to access a physical device or perform any other user defined logic while processing a service
request. For example, the user may want to store the written value in a permanent storage. A callback cannot be
attached to Status-Flags, Object-List, and the following properties if they are marked as AUTO in the TPI file: ActiveCOV-Subscriptions, Local-Date, Local-Time, UTC_Offset, Daylight_Savings_Status Time-Of-Device-Restart. Only
list properties can be attached to the list-change callback. When a Property isn’t attached to a callback, the default actions access the value of this property stored in the BACstac database while processing a perform request. For attached
properties a user specified callback is called. See BACstacSetReadCb(), BACstacSetWriteCb(), BACstacSetChangeListCb(), BACstacSetWriteCmdCb() functions for more information.

in Appendix E.

646

Chapter 11. Handling Requests - Default
Actions
BACstac applications which choose to use the BACstac object database can have many common BACnet requests
handled by BACstac default actions. The default actions can be overridden by defining hooks to handle the BACnet
requests.
The following services have default actions: AddListElement, RemoveListElement, ReadProperty, ReadPropertyMultiple, WriteProperty, WritePropertyMultiple, Who-Is, Who-Has, I-Am (client), and I-Have (client).
The default actions will check the request parameters for validity and use the BACstac object database to satisfy the
request. For requests which need to perform IO, an application-supplied callback can be used.
The Read/WritePropertyMultiple default actions break the requests into a series of Read/WriteProperty requests which
can be handled by hooks or default actions one property at a time.
The Read/WriteProperty default actions also handle the required BACnet behaviour for IO objects for the out-ofservice, present-value, priority-array, and relinquish-default properties. They will use application-supplied callbacks
for requests which need to perform IO. In particular, when out-of-service is TRUE, some property may become
writable as it is required by the BACnet standard. However, BACstac always invokes read and write callbacks for
present-value and other properties even if out-of-service is TRUE. Therefore, the application supplied callback should
check the value out-of-service and usually return CALLBACK_STATUS_DEFAULT if the property is required to be
decoupled from the physical device when out-of-service is TRUE.
The I-Am default action creates a local device image, caching the BACnet address of the remote device, and its
APDU-length and segmentation-supported properties. The I-Have default action will create a local object image and
set its object-name and object-type properties.

BACSTAC_PROP_READ_CB
Name
BACSTAC_PROP_READ_CB — readProperty callback

655

Chapter 11. Handling Requests - Default Actions

Synopsis
BACSTAC_CALLBACK_STATUS (*BACSTAC_PROP_READ_CB)(
BACSTAC_HOBJECT hObject,
BACSTAC_PROPERTY_ID ePropertyID,
BACSTAC_ARRAY_INDEX nIndex);

Arguments
hObject
ePropertyID

The Object and Property Identifier of the Property to be read (for example the Present Value Property of Analog
Input Object #1). The same callback routine is invoked for all properties of all objects.
nIndex

An index of an array item. If the Property is not an array, the index value BACSTAC_VOID_INDEX should
be used. If the Property is an array, the index value BACSTAC_ENTIRE_ARRAY can be used to read the
entire array. If the Property is an array, the index value BACSTAC_ARRAY_COUNT will return the number of
elements in the array. The indices of BACnet arrays start counting at 1.

Description
BACSTAC_PROP_READ_CB is the type declaration for the read callback. This routine is provided by the BACstac
application and is invoked by the BACstac default actions when a ReadProperty or ReadPropertyMultiple request is
being processed. A pointer to the routine is registered with the BACstac server by BACstacSetReadCb(). The callback
has the opportunity to supply to update the value of the property stored in the BACstac database. To store a new value
of the property BACstacStorePropertyInstance() should be used.
The callback is invoked for any property that has been attached to the read callback regardless of the current value
of the Out-Of-Service property. When Out-Of-Service is TRUE, some properties are no longer represent the physical
value of the device associated with this object. Therefore, the application callback should check the value of the OutOf-Service property, and if Out-Of-Service is TRUE and the target property is required to be decoupled from the
physical device when Out-Of-Service is TRUE then the callback should not take any action and return immediately
with CALLBACK_STATUS_DEFAULT.

Return Value
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_CALLBACK_STATUS in Appendix E.

656

Chapter 11. Handling Requests - Default Actions

BACSTAC_PROP_WRITE_CB
Name
BACSTAC_PROP_WRITE_CB — writeProperty callback

Synopsis
BACSTAC_CALLBACK_STATUS (*BACSTAC_PROP_WRITE_CB)(
BACSTAC_HOBJECT hObject,
BACSTAC_PROPERTY_ID ePropertyID,
BACSTAC_ARRAY_INDEX nIndex,
const BACSTAC_PROPERTY_CONTENTS *pContents);

Arguments
hObject
ePropertyID

The Object and Property Identifier of the Property to be written (for example the Present Value Property of Binary
Output Object #2). The same callback routine is invoked for all Properties of all Objects.
nIndex

The index of an array item. If the Property is not an array, the index value BACSTAC_VOID_INDEX should be
used. If the Property is an array, the index value BACSTAC_ENTIRE_ARRAY can be used to write the entire
array. If the Property is an array, the index value BACSTAC_ARRAY_COUNT can be used to resize the array
provided that this array can be variable size. The indices of BACnet arrays start counting at 1.
pContents

Pointer to a Property Contents containing the value of the Property. The Property Contents tag attribute indicates
the type of the Property.

Description
BACSTAC_PROP_WRITE_CB is the type declaration for the write callback. This routine is provided by the BACstac
application and is invoked by the BACstac default actions when a Write Property request is being processed. A pointer
to the routine is registered with the BACstac server by BACstacSetWriteCb(). The callback has the opportunity to use
the value for the Property supplied in the Property Contents argument.
The write callback is intended to allow an application to set a parameter of a physical instrument. This callback
is invoked for any property that has been attached to the write callback regardless of the current value of the OutOf-Service property. When Out-Of-Service is TRUE, some properties are no longer represent the physical value of
the device associated with this object. Therefore, the application callback should check the value of the Out-OfService property, and if Out-Of-Service is TRUE and the target property is required to be decoupled from the physical
657

Chapter 11. Handling Requests - Default Actions
device when Out-Of-Service is TRUE then the callback should not take any action and return immediately with
CALLBACK_STATUS_DEFAULT.

Return Value
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_CALLBACK_STATUS in Appendix E.

BACSTAC_WRITE_CMD_CB
Name
BACSTAC_WRITE_CMD_CB — write commandable callback

Synopsis
BACSTAC_CALLBACK_STATUS (*BACSTAC_PROP_WRITE_CB)(
BACSTAC_HOBJECT hObject,
BACSTAC_PROPERTY_ID propertyID,
BACSTAC_ARRAY_INDEX nIndex,
const BACSTAC_PROPERTY_CONTENTS *writtenValue,
const BACSTAC_PROPERTY_CONTENTS *newPresentValue,
const BACSTAC_CALLBACK_INFO *extraInfo);

Arguments
hObject

The object handle of the written property.
propertyID

The property identifier that is going to be changed. It can be either priority-array or relinquish-default. Usually, neither priority-array or relinquish-default is directly from the network, but when the write request for a
commandable property is received, it is translated as writing to the corresponding element of the priority-array
property. Thus, normally it should be priority-array. However, if the application has configured the relinquishdefault property as writable (i.e. it can be changed using write-property request) then the callback will be invoked
during writing relinquish-default as well.

658

Chapter 11. Handling Requests - Default Actions
nIndex

The index of an array item. If the Property is not an array, the index value is BACSTAC_VOID_INDEX. If a
commandable property is written then the index value corresponds to the priority parameter in the write property.
If the write request does not specify priority for a commandable property then the default value 16 is used, which
corresponds the least privileged index of the priority-array property.
writtenValue

Pointer to a property contents containing the written value. The property contents tag attribute indicates the type
of the Property.
newPresentValue

If the value of the present-value property is changed, this is a pointer to property contents with the new value of
the present-value property. If the present-value is not changed by this write request then this pointer is NULL.
extraInfo

Pointer to a additional information.

Description
BACSTAC_WRITE_CMD_CB is the type declaration for the write commandable callback. This routine is provided
by the BACstac application and is invoked by the BACstac default actions when a Write Property request for a
commandable property is being processed. A pointer to the routine is registered with the BACstac server by BACstacSetWriteCb(). The callback has an opportunity to use the newly written value as well as the new value for the
commandable property (if the latter is changed).
The write commandable callback is extension of the write callback interface intended to provide additional information useful for a commandable property. In contrast to normal properties, the value of the commandable property is
determined by the current values of priority-array and relinquish-default properties. When a commandable property
is written, then the corresponding element of the priority-array is set to the new value and then the new value of the
present-value property is calculated. The write commandable callback gives the user both information -- the written
value and the new value of the present-value property if it is changed. This allows the application to control that the
written value is inside of the allowed range (or store the new value of the priority-array in non-volatile memory if it is
necessary) as well as setting a new value to the physical instrument represented by this object.
The write callback callback is invoked regardless of the current value of the Out-Of-Service property. When Out-OfService is TRUE, the commandable properties are no longer represent the physical value of the device associated with
this object. Therefore, the application callback should check the value of the Out-Of-Service property, and if Out-OfService is TRUE then the callback should not change the current value of the physical device and return immediately
with CALLBACK_STATUS_DEFAULT.

Return Value
The callback can return either CALLBACK_STATUS_OK, CALLBACK_STATUS_WRITTEN, CALLBACK_STATUS_DEFAULT, or any error constructed using the CALLBACK_STATUS_ERROR macro. If the callback
returns CALLBACK_STATUS_OK then the written value will be put into the database. If the callback returns
CALLBACK_STATUS_WRITTEN then the new value of the property has been written by the callback, so the default action does not need to write anything to the property. If the callback returns CALLBACK_STATUS_DEFAULT
then the default action will continue as if there were no write commandable callback (i.e. a usual write callback will
659

Chapter 11. Handling Requests - Default Actions
be invoked is one of the affected property is attached to it). If the callback returns any other code then the writing
procedure will be aborted and the returned error will be sent in the response.

BACSTAC_CHANGE_LIST_CB
Name
BACSTAC_CHANGE_LIST_CB — change list callback

Synopsis
BACSTAC_CALLBACK_STATUS (*BACSTAC_CHANGE_LIST_CB)(

BACSTAC_LIST_OPERATION operation,
const BACSTAC_PROPERTY_CONTENTS *pChange,
const BACSTAC_PROPERTY_CONTENTS *pResult,
BACSTAC_ELEMENT_COUNT *pFirstFailed);

Arguments
hObject
ePropertyID

The Object and Property Identifier of the Property to be written (for example the Present Value Property of Binary
Output Object #2). The same callback routine is invoked for all Properties of all Objects.
nIndex

The index of an array item. If the Property is not an array, the index value BACSTAC_VOID_INDEX should be
used. If the Property is an array, the index value BACSTAC_ENTIRE_ARRAY can be used to change the entire
array. The indices of BACnet arrays start counting at 1. The index value BACSTAC_ARRAY_COUNT is not
allowed.
pChange

The list operation, which may be either LIST_ADD_OPERATION or LIST_REMOVE_OPERATION.
pChange

Pointer to a Property Contents containing the list of elements that will be added or removed.

660

Chapter 11. Handling Requests - Default Actions
pResult

Pointer to a Property Contents containing the new value for the property.
pFirstFailed

Pointer to the first failed element number. This is an output parameter of this callback. On error, the first failed
element number shall convey the numerical position starting at 1, of the offending element in the list of elements
pointed by pResult. If the failure caused by any reason other than the given list of elements then the first failed
element number shall be zero. If the callback returns CALLBACK_STATUS_OK or CALLBACK_STATUS_DEFAULT then there is no need to set this variable.

Description
BACSTAC_CHANGE_LIST_CB is the type declaration for the list-change callback. This routine is provided by the
BACstac application and is invoked by the BACstac default actions when an Add or Remove List Elements request is
being processed. A pointer to the routine is registered with the BACstac server by BACstacSetChangeListCb(). The
callback has the opportunity to use the value for the Property supplied in the Property Contents argument.

Return Value
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_STATUS
in Appendix E.

BACSTAC_HOBJECT hObject);

Arguments
hObject

The Object whose one or more properties was changed.

Description
BACSTAC_OBJECT_CHANGE_CB is the type declaration for the object-change callback. This routine is provided
by the BACstac application and is invoked by the BACstac default actions after change of one or more properties of
specified object. A pointer to the routine is registered with the BACstac server by BACstacSetObjChangeCb().

Blocks for Hooks
A BACstac application which chooses to override the BACstac default actions by registering hooks to handle requests,
can still use the BACstac object database with building block routines. These routines implement much of the logic of
the default actions and can simplify the code needed in a hook.

Name
BACstacAddElement — adds an element to a list in the BACstac database

Synopsis

BACSTAC_HOBJECT hObject,

BACSTAC_ELEMENT_COUNT *pFirstFailed);

Arguments
hObject
ePropertyID

The Object and Property Identifier of the local Property.

The index of an array item. If the Property is not an array of lists, the index value BACSTAC_VOID_INDEX
should be used.

A pointer to a list of elements to be added to the property.

errCode

Pointers to variables to hold appropriate BACnet Error information. errClass and errCode may be NULL.

663

Chapter 12. Handling Requests - Building Blocks for Hooks
pFirstFailed

pFirstFailed may be NULL.

Description

present in the list property, they will be ignored: duplicates of the elements will not be added to the list. If an element
cannot be added to the list by this routine for some other reason, an error is returned, along with the sequence number
of the element.

the BACnet requirement that a Present_Value property in input objects must be writable when Out-Of-Service is

BACstacRetrieveEventParameters
Name
BACstacRetrieveEventParameters — reads event algorithm parameters

Synopsis
BACSTAC_STATUS BACstacRetrieveEventParameters(
BACSTAC_HOBJECT hObject,
BACSTAC_BUFFER *buffer,
BACSTAC_IALLOC *iAlloc);

Arguments
hObject

The handle of the object that applies the event algorithm.
buffer

Pointer to a buffer to receive the event parameters as the Event Parameter data structure.
iAlloc

A pointer to an allocator interface. This parameter may be NULL then the buffer pointed by the buffer parameter
will be used to receive the result. If the allocator interface is provided then the buffer will be allocated and should
be freed later.

Description
Retrieves the event algorithm parameters. If the given handle points to an Event Enrollment object then the value of
the Event_Parameters property is returned. If the object handle is a monitored object then values of all intrinsic event
related properties are returned in the same format as the Event_Parameters property in an Event Enrolment object.
Thus this access routine allows to unite processing algorithmic and intrinsic alarms and events.

669

Chapter 12. Handling Requests - Building Blocks for Hooks

Return Value
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. Possible return codes are the following:
BACSTAC_STATUS_OK
Upon successful completion.
BACSTAC_STATUS_INVALID_PARAM
One or more parameters functions were incorrect. For example, the buffer parameter was null, or iAlloc was
NULL and the pBuffer was not properly initialized to hold returned elements.
BACSTAC_STATUS_INVALID_OBJECT_HANDLE
The object handle was invalid.
BACSTAC_STATUS_UNKNOWN_PROPERTY
The property required for event algorithm support does not exist in the specified object.
BACSTAC_STATUS_OUT_OF_MEMORY
The operation cannot be performed due to lack of memory.
BACSTAC_STATUS_VAL_OUT_OF_SPACE
The given buffer does not have enough space for the Event Parameters.
BACSTAC_STATUS_UNKNOWN_ERROR
An unexpected error has occurred. This may be due to implementation defect in BACstac or improper work of
the program, which caused to memory corruption.

The object handle was invalid.

Chapter 13. IOCTL
BACstac ioctl requests provides a mechanism to read and modify some internal variables of the BACstac configuration, obtain statistics about BACstac network performance, perform some specialized commands not available through
the ordinary BACstac API.
Any ioctl request can be executed either locally or remotely.
BACstac ioctl interface differs from ordinary API services: ioctl request does not use C structure for ioctl request
input and output parameter, but stores these parameters as input and output sequences.
Typical work with an ioctl request consists from the following steps:
creating a new ioctl;
filling it up with input parameters;
• execution of the ioctl request either locally or remotely;
• reading output parameters;
• removing request when it is no longer needed.

•

•

The first input parameter of any ioctl request is an ioctl request number; other parameters are request specific. The
first output parameter of any ioctl request is BACSTAC_IOCTL_STATUS, and others are also request specific. The
list of input/output parameters for each ioctl request is presented in Appendix F of this document, and the detail of list
of all BACSTAC_IOCTL_STATUS returned by BACstac ioctl service can be found in Appendix E of this document.

Synopsis

void);

Arguments
None

Arguments

An address of the request source. For client or server application this address shall be NULL. For gateway
application it shall not be NULL.
destAddress

A destination address of the request.

A pointer to the APDU properties structure that sets APDU properties for this transaction. This does not change
global settings for the application APDU properties. This argument may be NULL. In this case the global APDU
properties are used. The APDU Properties data type is described in the Section called APDU Properties in
Chapter 2.

Description
This routine executes an ioctl request on a remote device. For successful execution of the ioctl request, remote execution of BACstac ioctl requests shall be enabled by setting BACstac Ioctl Access Filter.

Return Values
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_STATUS
in Appendix E.

BACSTAC_IOCTL_ACCESS_FILTER
Name
BACSTAC_IOCTL_ACCESS_FILTER — ioctl remote access filter

Synopsis
BACSTAC_IOCTL_FILTER_STATUS (*BACSTAC_IOCTL_FILTER_PROC)(
const BACSTAC_ADDRESS *pSourceAddress,
BACSTAC_IOCTL_REQUESTID requestID,
BACSTAC_HIOREQ hIoReq);

698

Chapter 13. IOCTL

Arguments
pSourceAddress

A pointer to the source BACnet address.
requestID

An ioctl request identifier. For details see Appendix F of this document.
hIoReq

The handle to the ioctl request.

Description
BACSTAC_IOCTL_FILTER_PROC() is the type declaration of the application provided ioctl remote access filter
routine. This routine allows a BACstac application to control the remote access to ioctl service. If the application does
not provide an ioctl remote access filter, any remote ioctl request is passed to the user by Private Transfer Hook as any
other Private Transfer request. If ioctl remote access filter routine is supplied it gets all its arguments from an ioctl
requests. This routine can accept an ioctl request for execution, or it can ignore the ioctl request with no answer to an
ioctl request source, or it can choose to reject an ioctl request and to notify the request source.
An access filter can be registered by the registering API routine BACstacSetIoctlAccessFilter() at any time. One access
filter procedure is currently registered. A newly registered access filter procedure replaces old one. A NULL pointer
can be used to deregister the access filter.

Return Values
FILTER_STATUS_ACCEPT

Execution of the ioctl request is allowed.
FILTER_STATUS_REJECT

The ioctl request does not permitted, BACSTAC_IOCTL_NO_PERMISSION will be returned.
FILTER_STATUS_IGNORE

The ioctl request shall be ignored.

Arguments
hIoReq

A handle of the ioctl request.
pAddress

A pointer to a BACnet address of the request destination.
status

A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the asynchronous operation. See the Section called
BACSTAC_STATUS in Appendix E.

Description
BACSTAC_IOREQ_ACR_PROC data type is the type declaration of an ioctl asynchronous completion routine (ACR).
This routine allows a BACstac application to process the information that is received as the result of an ioctl request
asynchronously. If the application does not provide an ioctl ACR, any ioctl request shall be executed synchronously.
See the description of BACstacIoSetACR() routine in this document.

Return Values
None.

700

Chapter 14. Generating Requests - Simple API
The BACstac libraries provide two techniques for generating requests. The simple API, described in this chapter, based
on the BACstac object database and default actions to hide some of the request complexity from the application. The
raw API, described in Chapter 7 arlier chapter, provides full control over generating a BACnet request.
An application supplies a handle of a local device or object image to a remote device or object. The simple API request
will use local information (address, device ID, object ID, APDU parameters) from the images when constructing the
request.
The simple API requests block until a reply is received or the request times out. The simple API for confirmed requests
also includes optional storage for receiving BACnet Error, Abort and Reject responses.

BACstacAcknowledgeAlarm
Name

Synopsis

A pointer to the memory block which contains a number of acknowledgment parameters: a process identifier

state, a time stamp to identify the event notification that is being acknowledged, the identifier of the operator or
process that is acknowledging this event notification, and the time this acknowledgment was issued. This data
structure is of data type BACSTAC_ACK_ALARM_INFO. It is described in the Section called Acknowledge
Alarm in Chapter 3.
pError

A pointer to the memory block into which to place the error information, if any. pError may be NULL.

in Appendix E.

A numeric identifier of the process within the COV-client that should receive the notification.

in Appendix E.

the event has been noted by an operator or supervisory program.

Private Transfer in Chapter 3.

in Chapter 3.

BACstacDeviceCommControl
Name
BACstacDeviceCommControl — sends a deviceCommunicationControl request

Synopsis
BACSTAC_STATUS BACstacDeviceCommControl(

709

Chapter 14. Generating Requests - Simple API
BACSTAC_HDEVICE hDevice,
BACSTAC_UNSIGNED nTimeDuration,
BACSTAC_DCC_VALUE dccValue,
const BACSTAC_CHAR *pszPassword,
BACSTAC_ERROR *pError);

Arguments
hDevice

Handle of the destination device.
nTimeDuration

The number of minutes, or indefinite time BACSTAC_DCC_INDEFINITE, that the remote device shall ignore
APDUs if dccValue is DCC_DISABLE or DCC_DISABLE_INITIATION. If the value of the next argument
is DCC_ENABLE, the time duration argument will be ignored and the time period will be considered to be
indefinite. The present version of BACstac Server and Gateway applications support only the indefinite duration
value if dccValue is DCC_ENABLE, DCC_DISABLE, or DCC_DISABLE_INITIATION. If a definite time
duration argument is used, this routine shall return BACSTAC_SERVICE_BACNET_ERROR value, Error Class
ERR_CLASS_SERVICES, Error Code ERR_CODE_OBJ_DELETION_DENIED. The duration time, expressed
as a number of minutes, is a possible value only if the Gateway/Server application is provided with special means
(for example, a service application hook) to process this service.
dccValue

It may have one of three values: DCC_DISABLE to instruct the remote device to stop initiating and responding
to all APDUs expect Device-Communication-Control and Reinitialize-Device APDUs; or DCC_ENABLE to
enable all communications; or DCC_DISABLE_INITIATION to instruct the remote device to disable initiation
any requests, but the device will still respond to all confirmed request.
pszPassword

This optional argument shall be a character string no longer than 21 characters. For those devices that require
password protection, the service shall be denied if this argument is absent or the password is incorrect. For those
devices that do not require a password, this argument is ignored.
pError

A pointer to a variable to hold BACnet Error information. The error pointer may be NULL.

Description
Sends a Device-Communication-Control request to instruct a remote device to stop initiating and responding to all
APDUs on the communication internetwork, except Device-Communication-Control and Reinitialize-Device APDUs,
for a specified duration of time. The time duration may be set to indefinite, meaning communication must be reenabled by a Device-Communication-Control or Reinitialize-Device service, not by time. This routine can enable
communications. This routine can also disable all communications; in this case the remote device shall ignore all
APDUs including Device-Communication-Control and Reinitialize-Device APDUs for a specified period of time.

710

Chapter 14. Generating Requests - Simple API

Return Value
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_STATUS
in Appendix E.

BACstacGetAlarmSummary
Name
BACstacGetAlarmSummary — sends a getAlarmSummary request

Synopsis
BACSTAC_STATUS BACstacGetAlarmSummary(
BACSTAC_HDEVICE hDevice,
BACSTAC_ALARM_SUMMARY *pSummaryBuffer,
BACSTAC_ELEMENT_COUNT nBufferCount,
BACSTAC_ELEMENT_COUNT *pSummaryAvailable,
BACSTAC_ERROR *pError);

Arguments
hDevice

The handle of the device to be requested.
pSummaryBuffer

A pointer to a memory block into which to place summary information, which is a list of Alarm Summary
items. Each item of data type BACSTAC_ALARM_SUMMARY consists of three parameters: the Object ID of
the appropriate object, the Event-state of this object, and Acked-Transitions property values. The BACSTAC_ALARM_SUMMARY data structure is described in the Section called Get Alarm Summary in Chapter 3. This
argument may be NULL; in this case the next argument nBufferCount == 0.
nBufferCount

The length of the Summary buffer expressed as a number of Alarm Summaries. If the value of this argument is
0, the pointer to a Summary Buffer must be NULL.
pSummaryAvailable

A pointer to the buffer into which to place the actual number of existing Alarm Summaries.

711

Chapter 14. Generating Requests - Simple API
pError

A pointer to the memory block into which to place the error information, if any. pError may be NULL.

Description
This routine generates a Get Alarm Summary service request. It is used by a client BACnet user to obtain a summary
of "alarm-active" objects within the given device that is capable of alarm processing. The "alarm-active" objects are
objects that have any value but STATE_NORMAL for the Event_State property and NOTIFY_TYPE_ALARM for
the Notify_Type property.

Return Value
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_STATUS
in Appendix E.

Name

BACSTAC_ELEMENT_COUNT nBufferCount,
BACSTAC_ELEMENT_COUNT *pSummaryAvailable,
BACSTAC_ERROR *pError);

Arguments
hDevice

The handle of the device requested.

712

Chapter 14. Generating Requests - Simple API
pFilter

A pointer to a memory block which contains a data structure of data type BACSTAC_ENROLLMENT_FILTER.
This data structure is described in the Section called Get Enrollment Summary - Enrollment Filter in Chapter 3.
This argument contains five filters: enrollment, event state, event type, priority, and notification class. Some of
these filters are optional.
pSummaryBuffer

A pointer to a memory block into which to place summary information, which is a list of Enrollment Summary
items. Each item of data type BACSTAC_ENROLLMENT_SUMMARY consists of the following parameters:
the Object ID of the appropriate object, its event type, event state, notification priority, and notification class property values. The BACSTAC_ENROLLMENT_SUMMARY data structure is described in the Section called Get
Enrollment Summary in Chapter 3. This argument may be NULL; in this case the next argument, nBufferCount,
must be 0.
nBufferCount

The length of the Summary buffer, expressed as the number of Enrollment Summaries. If the value of this
argument is 0, the pointer to a Summary Buffer must be NULL.
pSummaryAvailable

A pointer to a variable which is to be set to the actual number of existing Enrollment Summaries that were
available to be copied into the buffer.
pError

A pointer to the memory block in which to place any error information. pError may be NULL.

Description
Obtains a summary of event-initiating objects within the given device. Several different filters may be applied to define
the search criteria. This routine generates a Get Enrollment Summary Service request.

Return Value
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_STATUS
in Appendix E.

pServiceInfo

A pointer to a memory block that holds a data structure of data type BACSTAC_EVENT_INFO_INFO. This data
structure may contain optional ObjectID parameter to specify the last Object Identifier received in a preceding Get
Event Info ACK if it’s moreEvents field was BACSTAC_TRUE. If ObjectID parameter is omitted, the returned
summary shall start with the first event-active object.
The BACSTAC_EVENT_INFO_INFO data structure is described in the Section called Get Event Information in
Chapter 3.
pInfoBuffer

A pointer to a memory block of data type BACSTAC_EVENT_INFO to place the response information. It contains a list of Event Summary items. Each item of data type BACSTAC_EVENT_SUMMARY consists of a
number of parameters that describe the appropriate object. ObjectID, Event-State, Acked-Transitions, NotifyType, and Event-Enable parameters convey values of the corresponding properties of the object. Event-Stamps
parameter conveys the timestamps of the last event notifications for TO-OFFNORMAL, TO-FAULT, and TONORMAL events. Event-Priorities parameter conveys the priorities specified in the Priority property of the associated notification class object. Event Info data structure contains actual number of the items returned, and the
total length of Event-summary list buffer expressed as a number of items this buffer can hold. The last parameter
of BACSTAC_EVENT_INFO data structure is More Events flag which indicates whether (BACSTAC_TRUE)
or not (BACSTAC_FALSE) more objects exist that should be listed, but that cannot be conveyed by the reply because APDU is too short. The BACSTAC_EVENT_SUMMARY and BACSTAC_EVENT_INFO data structures
are described in the Section called Get Event Information in Chapter 3.
pError

A pointer to the memory block into which to place the error information if any. pError may be NULL.
iAlloc

A pointer to an allocator interface. This parameter may be NULL then the buffer located inside of pInfoBuffer
(pInfoBuffer->pSummaries) will be used to store the result. If the allocator interface is provided then the buffer
will be allocated and should be freed later using the BACstacFreeEventInfoAck() routine.

714

Chapter 14. Generating Requests - Simple API

Description
Sends a Get Event Information service request. It is used by a BACnet client user to obtain a summary of "eventactive" objects within the given device. The "event-active" objects are objects that have any value other than STATE_NORMAL for the Event_State property, or have an acked-transitions property which has at least one of the bits
(TO_OFFNORMAL, TO_FAULT, TO_NORMAL) set to BACSTAC_FALSE.

Return Value
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_STATUS
in Appendix E.

Arguments

Name

Synopsis
BACSTAC_STATUS BACstacReadProperty2(
BACSTAC_HOBJECT hObject,

720

Chapter 14. Generating Requests - Simple API

Arguments
hObject

The handle of the Object containing the Property.
ePropertyID

The Property Identifier of the desired Property.
nIndex

The index for an array item. If the Property is not an array, the index shall be BACSTAC_VOID_INDEX. If the
Property is an array, the index value BACSTAC_ENTIRE_ARRAY can be used to read the entire array. If the
Property is an array, the index value BACSTAC_ARRAY_COUNT will return the number of elements in the
array. The indices of BACnet arrays start counting at 1.
pContents

Pointer to Property Contents. This data structure must contain a pointer to a buffer into which to copy the value.
Upon the successful return of this routine, the Property Contents tag attribute indicates the data type of the
Property.
pError

A pointer to a variable to hold BACnet Error information. pError may be NULL.
iAlloc

A pointer to an allocator interface. This parameter may be NULL then the buffer pointed by the pContents
parameter will be used to receive the result. If the allocator interface is provided then the buffer will be allocated
and should be freed later using the BACstacFreeContents() routine.

Description
Reads the value of a Property of an Object. Normally this routine sends a Read-Property request to the device specified
by its object handle to read the given property in the specified object.
On success, the result is placed into the buffer specified in the Property Contents and the value pointed by pError
is undefined. If the result of the operation was a negative confirmation (Error, Abort, or Reject) then the function
returns BACSTAC_STATUS_BACNET_ERROR, BACSTAC_STATUS_BACNET_ABORT, or BACSTAC_STATUS_BACNET_REJECT correspondingly and put the received negative confirmation to the field pointed by pError. On all other types
of error (such as not enough resources), neither pContents nor pError obtained meaninful value.

in Appendix E.

BACstacReadPropertyMultiple2
Name
BACstacReadPropertyMultiple2 — sends a readPropertyMultiple request

Synopsis
BACSTAC_STATUS BACstacReadPropertyMultiple2(
BACSTAC_HDEVICE hDevice,
BACSTAC_READ_LIST *readAccessSpec,
BACSTAC_READ_RESULT_LIST *readAccessResult,
BACSTAC_OBJECT_COUNT nReadAccessCount,
BACSTAC_ERROR *pError,
BACSTAC_IALLOC *iAlloc);

Arguments
hDevice

The handle of the destination Device.
readAccessSpec

A pointer to a list of BACSTAC_READ_LIST data structures which convey the Object handles and Property
Identifiers of desired Objects and Properties. This argument corresponds to the List of Read Access Specifications
in ANSI/ASHRAE Standard 135-2020 or later.
This data structure is described in the Section called Read Property Multiple - Client in Chapter 3. The Property
Identifier may be also ALL, REQUIRED, or OPTIONAL. The Property Identifier ALL means that all defined
Properties of the Objects are to be copied. The Property Identifier REQUIRED means that only those Properties
having a conformance code "R" or "W" shall be copied. The Property Identifier OPTIONAL means that only
those Properties having a conformance code "O" shall be copied.
readAccessResult

A pointer to a list of one or more BACSTAC_READ_RESULT_LIST data structures to indicate the success or
failure of the reading of each specified Property. In the case of successful access to a single Property its value shall
be returned within this argument, and in case of access failure this argument shall convey the Property Access
722

Chapter 14. Generating Requests - Simple API
Error information. This argument corresponds to the List of Read Access Results in ANSI/ASHRAE Standard
135-2020 or later. The BACSTAC_READ_RESULT_LIST data structure is described in the Section called Read
Property Multiple - Client in Chapter 3.
nReadAccessCount

A number of BACSTAC_READ_LIST data structures in the readAccessSpec buffer.
pError

A pointer to a buffer in which to place any error information. The routine shall continue to be executed until an
attempt has been made to access all specified properties. Only if none of the specified Properties can be accessed,
will an Error be returned. If any of the specified Properties of the specified Objects can be accessed, pError is
NULL.
iAlloc

A pointer to an allocator interface. This parameter may be NULL then buffers inside of the array pointed by the
readAccessResult parameter will be used to receive the result of a request. If the allocator interface is provided
then the buffer will be allocated and should be freed later using the BACstacFreeRPMResultList() routine.

Description
Reads the values of one or more specified properties of one or more Objects. This routine may read a single Property
of a single Object, a list of Properties of a single Object, or any number of properties of any number of objects within
one Device. This routine sends a Read-Property-Multiple request to the Device containing the Objects.

Return Value
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_STATUS
in Appendix E.

727

Arguments
hDevice

The handle of the device containing the monitored object.
pSubscriber

A pointer to a memory block which contains a data structure defining a set of parameters: whether the request
is for subscription or cancellation, the Process identifier, the monitored object identifier, whether confirmed or
unconfirmed notification is required, and the subscription lifetime. This data structure is of data type BACSTAC_SUBSCRIBE_COV_INFO. It is described in the Section called Subscribe COV in Chapter 3.
pError

A pointer to the memory block into which to place the error information, if any. pError may be NULL.

Description
Subscribes a COV client for the receipt of COV notifications from a standard object, or cancel the existing subscription.
If the standard object may optionally support COV reporting, the COV notification may be sent to one or more
subscriber clients. The subscription establishes a connection between the change of value detection and reporting
mechanism within the COV-server device and a logical Process within a COV-client.

Return Value
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_STATUS
in Appendix E.

A regular set of BACSTAC_STATUS Return Values. See also Appendix E of this document.

BACstacUnconfEventNotification2
Name
BACstacUnconfEventNotification2 — sends an unconfirmedEventNotification request

Synopsis
BACSTAC_STATUS BACstacUnconfEventNotification2(
BACSTAC_HOBJECT hInitObject,
BACSTAC_EVENT_NOTIF *pEventNotif,
const BACSTAC_ADDRESS *pDestAddress);

734

Arguments
hInitObject

Handle of the object which initiates the notification.
pEventNotif

A pointer to the Event Notification data structure. This data structure is described in the Section called Event
Notification in Chapter 4. The structure is used as an input and output parameter. The Initiating Device Identifier
Object Identifier attributes are ignored on input; when the function returns, they contain actual values used in the
request based on the given object handle; the rest fields are should initialized in appropriate values before this
function is invoked.
pDestAddress

A pointer to a variable containing the destination Address.

Description
Sends an Unconfirmed Event Notification service request message to a remote BACnet Address. It is used to notify a
remote device that an event was occurred. A confirmation reply is not expected. The event recipient could later use the
Acknowledge-Alarm service to indicate that the event has been noted by an operator or supervisory program. Only
one recipient can be notified by a single invocation of this service.

Return Value
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_STATUS
in Appendix E.

This argument of data type BACSTAC_PRIVATE_TRANSFER_INFO conveys the service request information
containing Vendor-Identifier, Service-Number and Service-Parameters. This data type is described in the Section
called Private Transfer in Chapter 3.

Description
Sends an Unconfirmed Private-Transfer service request to invoke proprietary or non-standard service in a remote device. The Private-Transfer service provides a mechanism for specifying a particular proprietary service in a standardized manner using Vendor-Identifier and Service-Number arguments. These two parameters serve to unambiguously
identify the intended purpose of the Service-Parameters information. A confirmation reply is not expected.

Return Value
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_STATUS
in Appendix E.

Description
Sends a UTC-Time-Synchronization request, which allows a remote Device to be notified of the correct Greenwich
mean time (Universal Time Coordinated) so that Devices may synchronize their internal clock with one another.
This service may be broadcast, multicast, or addressed to a single recipient. Since this is an unconfirmed service, no
response is expected.

A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_STATUS
in Appendix E.

The pointer to the BACSTAC_WRITE_FILE_SPEC data structure which indicates the type of file access (FILE_ACCESS_STREAM or FILE_ACCESS_RECORD) and contains data to copy into the file. This data structure is
described in the Section called Write File in Chapter 3.
pResult

This argument is to convey the File Access Type and start point coordinate to the request initiator if the data
writing was successful. This data structure of data type BACSTAC_WRITE_FILE_RESULT is described in the
Section called Write File in Chapter 3.

A pointer to a variable to hold BACnet Error information. pError may be NULL.

Description
Write an octet string into a specified position in a specified File. The File may be accessed as records or as a stream
of octets which is defined by the value of File_Access_Method property of the File object. Since the present version
of BACstac does not support a default processing of this service, the destination has to include a Hook procedure to
process it. Otherwise this service will send back the Reject (Unrecognized_Service) message. This routine corresponds
to the AtomicWriteFile BACnet service.

Return Value
A BACstac status code that indicates the success or failure of the routine. See the Section called BACSTAC_STATUS
in Appendix E.

Synopsis
BACSTAC_STATUS BACstacWriteProperty(
BACSTAC_HOBJECT hObject,

Arguments
hObject

The handle of the Object containing the Property.
ePropertyID

The Property Identifier of the desired Property.
nIndex

An index of an array item. If the Property is not an array, the index value BACSTAC_VOID_INDEX should be
used. If the Property is an array, the index value BACSTAC_ENTIRE_ARRAY can be used to modify the entire
array. The indices of BACnet arrays start counting at 1.
nPriority

The priority level for the Write-Property request, if the Property is a commandable Property (such as the presentvalue property of Output and Value Objects). If the Property is not commandable, the priority level BACSTAC_VOID_PRI should be used. If the Property is commandable, a priority level from 1 to 16 or BACSTAC_DEFAULT_PRI (16) can be used. The value is written into the Priority-Array Property of the Object, and the
highest priority value in that array is used as the value for the commandable property.
pContents

Pointer to the Property Contents. This data structure must contain a pointer to a buffer containing the value.
The Property Contents tag attribute must indicate the data type of the Property. A NULL value can be used to
relinquish control of a commandable value for a given priority level. When all entries of a Priority Array Property
in an Object are NULL, the commandable Property in the Object takes its value from the Relinquish-Default
Property.
pError

A pointer to a variable to hold BACnet Error information. pError may be NULL.

scheme.

a Write-Property-Multiple request to the Device containing the Objects. The service execution shall continue until all

741

Appendix A. CBNOBJ.EXE
Description:
CBNOBJ.EXE is used to create a Device Template for use in Server or Gateway applications.

Syntax:
CBNOBJ input.tpi output.c [ deviceTemplateName ]

Two first command line parameters are required. If the deviceTemplateName parameter is not specified in the
command line then CBNOBJ looks for a special comment in the header of the TPI file:
-- Device Template Name: deviceTemplateName

If the device template name is not specified anywhere explicitly then the name of the output C file (stripped of the C
extension) is used as the device template name.

Arguments:
input.tpi

The input file name. This file should contain TPI-formatted text. The ".tpi" is the recommended file extension though
you can use any other extensions if you like. CBNOBJ looks for the input file in the current working directory unless
the full path is specified.
If one of the full paths contains space symbols you should enclose this path in double quotes: e.g.
cbnobj "..\test test\test.tpi" test.c deviceName
output.c

The output file name. You are to compile this .c file separately and link to the other application modules.
If output.c already exists CBNOBJ.EXE will overwrite it without prompt. Be sure to save a copy of the old C file
if you still need it before its contents are erased.
deviceTemplateName

The global identifier of the Device Template. A BACstac application should declare this external identifier and pass a
pointer to it into the BACstac API routines that create Devices. For example, a Server application could use CBNOBJ
to create a Device template module with the global identifier myDeviceTemplateName, and use it to create the local
Device in the Server. In this case the CBNOBJ’s command line will look as usual:
cbnobj input.tpi output.c myDeviceTemplateName

And your application code should include the following:
extern const struct DEVICE_TEMPLATE myDeviceTemplateName;
...
BACSTAC_SRV_INIT init_data;
BACstacSetSrvInitDevice(init_data, &myDeviceTemplateName);

742

Appendix A. CBNOBJ.EXE
..
BACstacServerInit(&init_data,NULL);

Error Messages:
The error messages generated by CBNOBJ fall into four categories. The first category is a system error messages.
These errors are always fatal, so CBNOBJ exists immediately after printing them to stderr. The rest of errors are not
fatal but CBNOBJ often exists after them too to avoid spurious error messages caused by previous errors. All errors
except system ones have the prefix that consists of file name and line number separated by colon.

System Errors
fatal error: Unable to open input file [file_name]: [system error]

The mostly possible cause of this error is that the input file was not found in the specified directory. For more information refer to the [system error] message.
fatal error: Unable to open output file [file_name]: [system error]

This error is usually caused by inability to create the output file. See the [system error] message for more information.
fatal error: Unable to write to output file: [system error]

A possible reason for this error is lack of disk space. Refer to the [system error] message for more information.
fatal error: Not enough memory

The program cannot allocate memory. This should not happen unless CBNOBJ is run on small embedded devices.

Syntax Errors
Unexpected EOF

An unexpected end-of-file occurred when reading the input file.
’X’ expected before [symbols]
”’ expected before [symbols]

An octet string was expected. The octet string should be enclosed in quotes and be preceded by ’X’. Instead of
expected ’X’ or ”’, the following [symbols] were encountered.
’,’ expected before [symbols]

The incorrect format of WeeNDay, Bit_String, Date, Object_Identifier or Sequence. The comma was expected but the
following [symbols] were encountered.
’,’ or ’}’ expected before [symbols]
’,’ or ’)’ expected before [symbols]

The incorrect format of Bit_String, Array or SequenceOf. The comma, ’}’ or ’)’ was expected but the following
[symbols] were encountered.

encountered.

but the following [symbols] were encountered.

Unsupported PICS ’[number]’

The ’PICS #’ statement specifies an unsupported character set. Currently, supported values are 0 (UTF-8), 1 (DBCS),
2 (JIS_X_0208), 5 (ISO_8859-1). If the code page is DBCS then the next line should contain the code page number
in parenthesis. For example: (1252).

The file has started with UTF-8 BOM (i.e. the byte sequence 0xEF,0xBB,0xBF), which indicates UTF-8 encoding but
the PICS statement indicates an other encoding than UTF-8 (i.e. not ’PICS 0’). So the encoding of the file cannot be
correctly detected.

The specified code page is invalid or not supported by the current system.

This will appear when the opening string of the TPI input file is not found by the CBNOBJ. This opening string may

with this name and that its name is spelled correctly.

Object properties support:
CBNOBJ doesn’t support the following object properties:

When initializing a device template with CBNOBJ these properties values should be indicated as follows:
device-address-binding: ?
event-parameters: ?

The values of all the other object properties should be declared accordingly to the TPI format (see Appendix B of this

752

Appendix B. TPI File Format
A TPI file is used as an input file for the BACnet Object Compiler (CBNOBJ.EXE), which generates a device template,
and contains a BACnet Protocol Implementation Conformance Statement (PICS) expressed in a standardized text
form. This format is known as Text PICS (for detailed information about PICS see ANSI/ASHRAE Standard 135-2020
or later, Chapter 12): hence the file extension is .TPI. The Object Compiler is described in Appendix A.
The TPI files serve to implement both human-readable and program-readable description of BACnet objects and
services within a given device. This description must adhere to certain rules defined in this document. TPI files are
text files and contain normal editable text lines ending in carriage-return/linefeed pairs (invisible on the screen in most
cases and omitted in the remainder of this document). Space characters are recognized as separators, and extra spaces
are ignored. TPI files may include comments marked with a double minus (--): all characters on the line following
this sign will be ignored by CBNOBJ.

Format of TPI files:
List of Objects in test device:
{
Object_1
Object_2
........
Object_N
}
End of BACnet Protocol Implementation Conformance Statement

The TPI file format does not put any limits on the objects’ number (i.e. N in the example above). To define an object
you should define a collection of object property values. Each "Object_X" item has the following format:
{
Property_1: Property_Value_1
Property_2: Property_Value_2
. . . .
Property_M: Property_Value_M
}

The property list for an object depends on its type. Each object type has its own set of properties (for the descriptions of
each property type see ANSI/ASHRAE Standard 135-2020 or later Annex C and chapter 21). There are 28 standard object types (detailed descriptions are available in ANSI/ASHRAE Standard 135-2020 or later chapter 12) supported (see
Appendix C - Supported Objects and Properties for a detailed description): device, accumulator, analog-input, analogoutput, analog-value, averaging, binary-input, binary-output, binary-value, calendar, command, event-enrollment, file,
group, life safety point, life safety zone, load-control, loop, multi-state-input, multi-state-output, multi-state-value,
notification-class, program, pulse-converter, trend-log and schedule, structured-view.
A TPI file can contain any number of instances for every object supported. The only exception is the "device" object
that must be exactly one in a single file. In the other words, one TPI file can be used to provide definition for only
one device template though you can use this template as a pattern as many times as you want to provide multiple twin
devices.
To make the device template defined by your file function properly you should list all the objects in the object-list
property of the device object using the format "([object type], [instance number])" (see ANSI/ASHRAE Standard
135-2020 or later clause 12.10). The object-list property of your device will be formatted like the following example:
object-list:

753

Appendix B. TPI File Format
((device, 12345),
(analog-output, 1),
(analog-input, 1)}

However you still can create new objects at runtime bypassing CBNOBJ. In this case you use the functions BACstacCreateDBObject and BACstacDestroyObject that still add the new-created objects to the device’s object-list automatically.
Any other property value must be one of the following types:
TYPES

RULES AND REQUIREMENTS

Boolean

Takes one of the following values: "F" (False), "T"
(True), or "?" (set by default).

Bit string

A set of bit values separated by commas and enclosed in
parentheses. An element of a bit string must take one of
the following values: "F" (means 0), "T" (means 1), or
"?" (means the default value for the given property type).

Character string

A string of character symbols enclosed in double, single,
or accent grave quotes ("like this"(, ’like this’,
or ‘like this’). The maximum length for an ASCII
string is 100 characters.

Enumerated value

An expression of this type should be one of the
predefined values specific to each property that are
currently supported (see Appendix D). No quotes or
brackets are required, and no spaces between words are
allowed.

Date

The date expression enclosed in parentheses:
(Friday, 04-October-1996). There can be spaces
after comma or you can do without it. You shouldn’t
put any spaces before or after dashes. Otherwise an
error occurs. The date field can take the special value
"unspecified" (0xFF) by replacing the field with ’*’.
You can also replace any field part (day, month, date or
year) with default ‘?’. The field’s parts ranges are: day
of month (1 to 31), day of week (1 to 7), year (last two
digits of the year — 0 to 99) and month (1 to 12)
Examples:
(?, 1-January-1980) (Monday, ?-January-1980)
(Wednesday, 3-?-1980) (Monday, 3-?-?)

Octet string

Pairs of hex digits, enclosed in single quotes or accent
grave quotes, and preceded by an ’X’. For example:
X‘001122‘.

754

Appendix B. TPI File Format
TYPES

RULES AND REQUIREMENTS

Real

This type expression should lie in the range of 6.8 * 10-38
to 6.8 * 1038. A number may be presented either in the
fixed point format (as follows: 6.213748569339) or
using the exponential form, e.g. "6.21E-34" means
6.21*10-34.

Integer

this type numbers range from -2,147,483,648 to
2,147,483,647 (i.e. the valid range for 4-byte signed
integer).

Time

Represented using a hh:mm:ss.xx format. Here hh is
hours value (range from 0 to 23), mm: minutes (0 to
59), ss: seconds (0 to 59) and xx: hundredth (0 to 99). A
field can take the special value "unspecified" (0xFF) by
replacing the field with ’*’.
Examples:
14:35:26.12 01:?:41.?

Unsigned

Unsigned value must be an integer value in the range
from 0 to 4,294,967,295 (i.e. the valid range for a 4-byte
unsigned integer).

Array

These types are constructed values, represented by
Sequence of enclosing the values in braces ("{" and "}"),
with the elements separated by commas.

Sequence

That is constructed value also (for details see
ANSI/ASHRAE Standard 135-2020 or later, Sections
20.2.16 and 20.2.17. Its elements are separated by
commas and enclosed in braces ("{" and "}") too.
However there is a straight distinction between this type
and Sequence of . The Sequence contains different
type-based elements so that every of them is marked by
a proper label. These labels are called context tags and
is presented as an unsigned integer number placed
before the corresponding value in square brackets ("["
and "]"). For detailed Tagging Rules see ANSI/ASHRAE
Standard 135-2020 or later, Section 20.2.20. Look at
the following example (action-command type):

{[0] (device, 1), [1] (analog-input, 2), [2] event-enabl
[4] (F,F,T), [5] 1, [7] T, [8] F }

755

Appendix B. TPI File Format
TYPES

RULES AND REQUIREMENTS

Choice

If an element is a constructed value itself, then that
element should also be enclosed in braces. Elements of
Choices (see ANSI/ASHRAE Standard 135-2020 or
later, Section 20.2.18) are also context-tagged values
and should be preceded by the context tag. For an
instance when you ask for ReadResult property your
object can react with either property value or error
message:
{ [2]present-value, [5]{object,read-access-denied}}}

Storage space for each property is limited. These limitations are the same as for the BACstac Object Database and are
described in the BACstac Installation Guide.
Objects can be described in arbitrary order, except the Device object which must be always first. The order of properties in an object description can be arbitrary except the first three, which must be at the beginning in the following
order:
{
object-identifier: ([object type], [instance number])
object-name: ”
object-type:
}

By default, all properties are read-only, i.e. they cannot be modified through Write Property or similar BACnet requests. This effect is equivalent to access modifier ’R’ appearing. The presence of the modifier ’W’ (’Writable’) means
that the given property may be changed or read by other devices. Once you have not put a "W" modifier to a property
at design time you won’t be able to do it at runtime. However while working bypassing CBNOBJ you can write to
read-only property using hooks (see User’s Guide chapter 2.2 and 2.6 for details). The modifier ’O’ (’Optional’) is
put for optional properties. In the following example, the present-value property is initially set to the value 72.3, and
is made writable:
present-value: 72.3 W

Otherwise this code line might look like present-value: 72.3. In this case the present-value property is still 72.3 but it
is read-only.

756

Appendix C. Supported Objects and Properties
This appendix contains description of object type structure for of the twenty-eight types of object supported by the
BACstac stack. For each property, its BACnet name is given in first column and this is also the name used TPI files.
The second column specifies the corresponding name in the BACSTAC_PROPERTY_ID enumeration, which is used
to refer to that property in BACstac applications. The third column specifies the BACnet type for this property. The
fourth column contains flags that describe whether a property is optional (the ’O’ flag) or required and whether it is
writable by default (the ’W’ flag) or not. It should be noted that BACstac now does not require the presence of all
non-optional properties, but they are needed to be BACnet compliant.
Most BACnet types has one to one correspondence with the BACstac type used to represent it in BACstac API, but
there are a few exceptions.
First, CharacterString can be represented not only by DATA_TYPE_ANY_CHAR_STRING, but it can be also represented by five other BACstac data types: DATA_TYPE_UTF_8_STRING, BACSTAC_DBCS_STRING, DATA_TYPE_JIS_X_0208_STRING, DATA_TYPE_UCS_2_STRING, DATA_TYPE_UCS_4_STRING, which mean a CharacterString
of the corresponding character set.
Second, the current-command-priority property, which has the BACnetOptionalUnsigned type in BACnet has the
DATA_TYPE_OPT_CMD_UNSIGNED data type in BACstac, while DATA_TYPE_OPT_UNSIGNED is used to represent
BACnetOptionalUnsigned in all other properties.
Third, all Unsigned data types in BACnet denoted as Unsigned8, Unsigned16, Unsigned32 or just Unsigned are represented by DATA_TYPE_UNSIGNED in BACstac except in case of the car-position and next-stopping-floor properties,
which has the Unsigned8 in BACnet, but the DATA_TYPE_FLOOR_NUMBER in BACstac.

BACSTAC_CALLBACK_STATUS
BACSTAC_CALLBACK_STATUS is defined as BACSTAC_UI32, which can contain either any standard BACnet
error or one of the predefined values defined below. To return any BACnet error, you can use the CALLBACK_STATUS_ERROR macro. This macro takes two arguments: Error Class and Error Code, which are BACSTAC_ERROR_CLASS and BACSTAC_ERROR_CODE enumerations defined below in this chapter. For all legal combinations of Error Class and Error Code, see Chapter 18 of the BACnet standard.
CALLBACK_STATUS_OK, CALLBACK_STATUS_WRITTEN and CALLBACK_STATUS_DEFAULT are considered as success, and all other codes are considered as indication of failure. If a failure happens, nothing is written to
the database and the appropriate BACnet error will be generated in response. On success, either simple ACK (for write
requests) or complex ACK containing the read value will be sent in response.
The list of predefined callback status codes are:
CALLBACK_STATUS_OK

The value of the property was successfully written to or read from the device. The new value will be stored in the
BACstac database, and, for the read request, it will be returned as response.
CALLBACK_STATUS_WRITTEN

The new value of the property has been written by the callback, so the default action does not need to write anything
to the property.
CALLBACK_STATUS_DEFAULT

The value of the property was not either written to or read from the device, but the default actions should act if the
callback was not attached to this property. For the write request, the new value will be placed in the database. For the
read request, the value stored in the database will be returned in response.

932

Appendix E. Return Values
CALLBACK_STATUS_FAILURE

General failure for reasons any other than defined in Chapter 18 of the BACnet standard. This code should be used
only when there is no more specific BACnet error for this failure.
Returning this status code causes the BACstac to respond with an BACnet error specifying an error class of DEVICE
and an error code of OTHER.
CALLBACK_STATUS_DEV_SHUT_DOWN

NOTE: This code is deprecated and described here for information purpose only. It will be removed from the future
versions of BACstac. Do not use it in your applications!
This status code was intended to ignore the service request, as if the device was not operational. However, it may not
work for Read and Write Property Multiple requests, and it also may produce non fully BACnet compliant behavior
in some other cases. Moreover, this is no way for a single physical device represented by this callback to choose to
respond or not to respond. It always should to do so to be BACnet compliant. However, if there is a need to shutdown
the whole BACnet device (with all physical devices represented by it), it should be done using the BACstacSetDCCValue() function.
CALLBACK_STATUS_DEV_BUSY

The value of the property was not written to or read from the device successfully, because the device expects to be
involved in higher priority processing for a time in excess of the usual request/confirm timeout period.
Returning this status code causes the BACstac to respond with an BACnet error specifying an error class of DEVICE
and an error code of DEVICE_BUSY.
CALLBACK_STATUS_DEV_OP_PROBLEM

The value of the property was not written to or read from the device successfully, because the device has detected an
operational problem that prevents it from carrying out the requested operation.
Returning this status code causes the BACstac to respond with an BACnet error specifying an error class of DEVICE
and an error code of OPERATIONAL_PROBLEM.
CALLBACK_STATUS_PROP_OUT_OF_RANGE

The value of the property was not written to the device successfully, because it is outside of the allowed range.
Returning this status code causes the BACstac to respond with an BACnet error specifying an error class of PROPERTY and an error code of VALUE_OUT_OF_RANGE.
CALLBACK_STATUS_PROP_OUT_OF_SPACE

The value of the property was not written to the device successfully, because not enough dynamic memory space
exists in the device.
Returning this value causes the BACstac to respond with an BACnet error specifying an error class of PROPERTY
and an error code of NO_SPACE_TO_WRITE_PROPERTY.

BACSTAC_HOOK_STATUS
0 = HOOK_STATUS_OK

The hook completed successfully. The hook handled the request and generated a reply, or (for asynchronous hooks)
the hook saved the request arguments and the reply will be generated by another application thread.

gateway application that has the same device instance number as existing device but having a different network

An attempt has been made to write to an Object_Name property with a value that is already in use in a different

The buffer size is incorrect. This error usually happens as result of an improper initialization of a property contents
parameter. For instance, this error may happen when a number of elements in the property contents is too large to be
hold inside of the property contents buffer based on its size, or when the end of a null-terminated string is not found
before the end of the buffer has been reached.

response did not fit into a message buffer, or it exceeded the response length specified by the original request. It may

exceeds the multiplication of Server parameters MaxAPDULength * MaxSegmentAccepted.

Appendix F. IOCTL Requests & Parameters
Any IOCTL request starts with the request identifier (see BACSTAC_IOCTL_REQUESTID) that determines the type
of the IOCTL request. The number and types of parameters depends on the request type, as it is described in the
corresponding table below. The requested identifier is encoded as an application-tagged ENUMERATED value. All
other parameters are encoded as the corresponding application-tagged values. This allows to send an IOCTL over
network to another BACstac Core encoded inside of the PrivateTransfer parameters.
On receive an IOCTL response from local or remove BACstac Core, the response contains the IOCTL Status code
(see BACSTAC_IOCTL_STATUS) as the first parameter of the response. It is encoded as an application-tagged ENUMERATED value. The number and the types of other parameters of the response depends on the request type as
defined in the corresponding table. All values are encoded as application-tagged values.
